rules.title: Verify kinematic equation consistency
rules.description: Ensure that the selected kinematic equation matches the given variables and unknowns (e.g., use v = u + at only when acceleration is constant).
rules.check_logic: Check if the problem specifies constant acceleration. If yes, verify that the equations of motion (v = u + at, s = ut + 0.5at^2, etc.) are applied correctly based on the given variables and unknowns.
common_errors: Using equations of motion when acceleration is not constant.
Mixing different equations without checking variable consistency.
Forgetting to explicitly state which kinematic equation is being used.

rules.title: Verify sign conventions for velocity, acceleration, and displacement
rules.description: Ensure that all vector quantities (e.g., velocity, acceleration, and displacement) use a consistent sign convention relative to the chosen coordinate system.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the same axis direction is consistently considered positive throughout the solution. Check the signs for initial velocity, acceleration, and displacement, and ensure they align with the chosen coordinate system.
common_errors: Inconsistent sign conventions for velocity and acceleration.
Forgetting to reverse signs when changing reference frames.
Misinterpreting upward or downward motion in vertical problems.

rules.title: Check dimensional and unit consistency in kinematics equations
rules.description: Ensure that all terms in kinematic equations have consistent dimensions and units (e.g., s = ut + 0.5at^2 must have all terms with the dimension of length).
rules.check_logic: Verify that time (t) is in seconds, acceleration (a) in m/s^2, and displacement (s) in meters for SI units. Ensure consistent units across all terms and convert units if necessary before applying equations.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for time, displacement, or velocity.
Failing to convert units before applying equations.
Adding or equating terms with incompatible dimensions.

rules.title: Verify independence of horizontal and vertical motion in projectile problems
rules.description: Ensure that horizontal and vertical motions are treated as independent. Horizontal motion has constant velocity, and vertical motion follows uniform acceleration due to gravity.
rules.check_logic: Verify that horizontal velocity remains constant and vertical motion follows s = ut + 0.5at^2 with a = -g. Ensure that time is the common parameter linking the two motions and that calculations for each direction are independent.
common_errors: Assuming horizontal acceleration exists when it does not.
Incorrectly coupling horizontal and vertical motions.
Forgetting to use consistent time for both directions.

rules.title: Verify relative motion equations
rules.description: Ensure the correct application of relative velocity equations (e.g., v_AB = v_A - v_B). Verify that vector subtraction aligns with the chosen coordinate system.
rules.check_logic: Check if relative velocity equations are applied correctly based on the reference frame. Verify the direction and magnitude of all velocity vectors and ensure proper handling of vector subtraction.
common_errors: Reversing the direction of relative velocity vectors.
Omitting the negative sign for vector subtraction.
Failing to properly account for the reference frame.

rules.title: Verify initial conditions and boundary values
rules.description: Ensure that the initial velocity, displacement, and acceleration values are consistently applied as per the problem statement.
rules.check_logic: Verify that initial values are correctly substituted into equations and that boundary conditions (e.g., at t = 0, s = 0) are consistent with the problem statement and equations used.
common_errors: Incorrectly interpreting initial conditions.
Forgetting to apply boundary conditions at t = 0 or other defined points.
Mixing up initial and final values.

rules.title: Verify validity of constant acceleration assumption
rules.description: Ensure that the assumption of constant acceleration is valid for the specific problem (e.g., no forces causing variable acceleration are present).
rules.check_logic: Verify that the problem explicitly states or implies constant acceleration. If external forces vary with time or position, ensure that constant acceleration equations are not used.
common_errors: Using constant acceleration equations in non-constant acceleration scenarios.
Ignoring forces or constraints that affect acceleration.
Incorrectly assuming gravity is the only force in vertical motion problems.

rules.title: Verify kinematics in circular motion
rules.description: Ensure correct application of angular kinematic equations and relationships between linear and angular quantities (e.g., v = rω and a_c = v^2/r).
rules.check_logic: Verify that angular displacement, velocity, and acceleration are used correctly. Check the relationship between linear and angular quantities and ensure that angular quantities are expressed in radians for SI units.
common_errors: Misinterpreting the relationship between linear and angular velocity.
Incorrectly calculating centripetal acceleration.
Forgetting to use radians for angular quantities in SI units.

rules.title: Verify time of flight calculations in projectile motion
rules.description: Ensure that the time of flight is calculated correctly using vertical motion equations and that it accounts for the entire trajectory.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the time of flight is determined using vertical motion equations (e.g., s = ut + 0.5at^2) and that it includes both ascent and descent. Ensure that the correct initial velocity and acceleration due to gravity are used.
common_errors: Calculating time of flight for only half the trajectory.
Using incorrect initial velocity or acceleration values.
Ignoring the effect of initial height on total time of flight.

rules.title: Verify range calculations in projectile motion
rules.description: Ensure that the horizontal range of a projectile is calculated correctly using the appropriate equations and initial conditions.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the range is calculated using horizontal motion equations (e.g., range = horizontal velocity × time of flight). Ensure that the time of flight is consistent with vertical motion calculations.
common_errors: Using incorrect time of flight in range calculations.
Ignoring the effect of initial height on the range.
Assuming horizontal velocity changes when it remains constant.

rules.title: Verify relative velocity equation
rules.description: The relative velocity between two objects A and B is given by v_AB = v_A - v_B. This principle applies when the velocities are measured in the same inertial reference frame.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the relative velocity computation follows the vector subtraction v_AB = v_A - v_B, where all velocity vectors are expressed in the same coordinate system.
common_errors: Using addition instead of subtraction for relative velocity
Mixing up the order of subtraction (v_AB should be v_A - v_B, not v_B - v_A)
Using incompatible coordinate systems for velocity components

rules.title: Ensure consistency in sign conventions
rules.description: In relative motion problems, consistent sign conventions must be used for all velocity components. For example, positive x-direction is typically to the right, and positive y-direction is upward.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all velocity components adhere to the same sign convention throughout the solution, and document any justified deviations clearly.
common_errors: Inconsistent sign conventions for velocity components (e.g., mixing positive and negative directions arbitrarily)
Reversing the sign of one component without justification
Failing to adjust signs when switching to a new reference frame

rules.title: Check proper switching between reference frames
rules.description: When switching between reference frames, relative velocities must be transformed correctly using the equation v_A_in_B = v_A_in_C - v_B_in_C, where C is the common reference frame.
rules.check_logic: Verify that switching between reference frames uses the correct vector subtraction and that all vectors are expressed in the same coordinate system before transformation.
common_errors: Failing to identify the common reference frame correctly
Neglecting to subtract the velocity of the reference frame
Incorrectly assuming velocities are independent of the reference frame

rules.title: Ensure dimensional consistency in velocity calculations
rules.description: All terms in relative velocity equations must have consistent units, typically meters per second (m/s) in SI units. This ensures dimensional accuracy.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all velocity terms have the same units and dimensions before performing any operations (e.g., subtraction or addition).
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for velocities (e.g., m/s for one term and km/h for another)
Failing to convert units to a consistent system before calculations
Mixing dimensional quantities (e.g., adding a velocity and a displacement)

rules.title: Apply geometric constraints for relative motion
rules.description: In problems involving constrained motion (e.g., objects connected by a rope), the relative motion between objects must satisfy the geometric constraints imposed by the system (e.g., constant rope length).
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the relative velocities or displacements satisfy the geometric constraints (e.g., sum of displacements equals rope length).
common_errors: Ignoring the length constraint for connected objects
Incorrectly assigning relative velocities that violate the geometric constraint
Failing to consider the impact of pulleys on relative motion

rules.title: Check validity of kinematic equations for relative motion
rules.description: Kinematic equations for relative motion are valid only under uniform acceleration or constant velocity conditions in inertial reference frames.
rules.check_logic: Verify that relative motion equations are applied only in scenarios of constant acceleration or velocity, and ensure the reference frame is inertial.
common_errors: Applying kinematic equations in non-inertial frames without accounting for pseudo-forces
Using kinematic equations in scenarios with variable acceleration
Assuming all reference frames are inertial without verification

rules.title: Verify relative acceleration relationship
rules.description: The relative acceleration between two objects A and B is given by a_AB = a_A - a_B. This applies in an inertial reference frame where accelerations are measured relative to a common origin.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that relative acceleration is calculated using vector subtraction a_AB = a_A - a_B, with proper consideration of the coordinate system.
common_errors: Mixing up the order of subtraction (a_AB should be a_A - a_B, not a_B - a_A)
Neglecting to account for direction when subtracting acceleration vectors
Using non-inertial reference frames without proper adjustments

rules.title: Ensure correct calculation of relative displacement
rules.description: Relative displacement between two objects A and B is given by s_AB = s_A - s_B, where both s_A and s_B are measured from the same reference point.
rules.check_logic: Verify that relative displacement calculations use vector subtraction and that all displacements are measured with respect to the same origin.
common_errors: Using addition instead of subtraction for relative displacement
Mixing up the order of subtraction (s_AB should be s_A - s_B, not s_B - s_A)
Failing to specify or use a common reference point for displacement measurements

rules.title: Consider the impact of angles on relative motion
rules.description: In problems involving relative motion with angular components, ensure correct consideration of angles, using trigonometric relationships to resolve velocity and displacement into components.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that angles are correctly used to resolve vectors into components, with correct application of trigonometric functions and consistent units (e.g., radians or degrees).
common_errors: Incorrectly resolving velocity or displacement vectors without regard to angles
Using incorrect trigonometric functions based on angle orientation (e.g., sine versus cosine)
Failing to convert angle units consistently when necessary

rules.title: Verify equations of motion for horizontal and vertical components
rules.description: In projectile motion, the horizontal motion is constant (no acceleration), while the vertical motion is uniformly accelerated due to gravity. The horizontal displacement is given by x = v_x * t, and the vertical displacement is given by y = v_y * t - (1/2) * g * t^2.
rules.check_logic: Ensure horizontal motion uses x = v_x * t, and vertical motion uses y = v_y * t - (1/2) * g * t^2 without errors in terms, coefficients, or signs. Confirm that g is positive in magnitude and applied with the correct sign based on the chosen coordinate system.
common_errors: Using acceleration in the horizontal motion equation
Missing the (1/2) factor in the vertical displacement formula
Incorrect sign for the gravitational term (-g * t^2)

rules.title: Check adherence to consistent sign conventions
rules.description: In projectile motion, a consistent coordinate system is required. For example, upward is typically positive and downward (gravity) is negative. Horizontal directions should also have consistent signs (e.g., +x for rightward).
rules.check_logic: Verify that gravity (g) is given a negative sign if upward is positive and that horizontal displacements/velocities are consistent with the chosen coordinate system. Ensure that all components of motion adhere to the same convention throughout the problem.
common_errors: Assigning gravity a positive value when upward is positive
Inconsistent signs for initial vertical velocity and acceleration due to gravity
Mixing up left/right or up/down conventions in calculations

rules.title: Validate range formula for horizontal displacement
rules.description: The horizontal range of a projectile is given by R = (v_0^2 * sin(2θ)) / g, assuming launch and landing heights are the same. This formula only applies under this condition.
rules.check_logic: Check that the condition of equal launch and landing heights is met before applying R = (v_0^2 * sin(2θ)) / g. If the heights differ, ensure the range is calculated using the appropriate kinematic equations.
common_errors: Using the range formula when the projectile lands at a different height than the launch height
Incorrectly substituting angle θ (e.g., using sin(θ) instead of sin(2θ))
Forgetting to square the initial velocity (v_0^2)

rules.title: Ensure correct time of flight calculation
rules.description: The total time of flight for a projectile launched and landing at the same height is given by T = (2 * v_0 * sin(θ)) / g. If launch and landing heights differ, a quadratic equation must be solved.
rules.check_logic: Verify use of T = (2 * v_0 * sin(θ)) / g only when launch and landing heights are equal. For differing heights, ensure a quadratic equation is solved for time, and confirm that the correct root of the equation is used.
common_errors: Using the symmetric time of flight formula when launch and landing heights are different
Missing the factor of 2 in the symmetric time of flight equation
Incorrectly solving the quadratic equation for unequal heights

rules.title: Verify decomposition of initial velocity into components
rules.description: The initial velocity vector (v_0) must be broken into horizontal (v_x = v_0 * cos(θ)) and vertical (v_y = v_0 * sin(θ)) components based on the launch angle θ.
rules.check_logic: Ensure horizontal and vertical velocity components are correctly calculated using trigonometric functions and the launch angle. Confirm that the angle is in the correct unit (radians or degrees) as required by the trigonometric functions.
common_errors: Using sin(θ) instead of cos(θ) for the horizontal component
Using cos(θ) instead of sin(θ) for the vertical component
Incorrect angle input (e.g., degrees instead of radians without conversion)

rules.title: Confirm correct calculation of maximum height
rules.description: The maximum height of a projectile is reached when the vertical velocity becomes zero. It is given by H = (v_0^2 * sin^2(θ)) / (2 * g).
rules.check_logic: Check that H = (v_0^2 * sin^2(θ)) / (2 * g) is used to calculate the maximum height and that the vertical velocity is zero at this point. Ensure sin^2(θ) is calculated correctly and that g is positive in magnitude.
common_errors: Incorrect use of sin^2(θ) (e.g., using sin(θ) instead of squaring the term)
Forgetting to divide by 2g
Assuming maximum height occurs at T/2 without verifying symmetry

rules.title: Perform dimensional and unit consistency check
rules.description: All equations in projectile motion must be dimensionally consistent. For example, displacement must have units of length, time must have units of seconds, and g must have units of m/s^2.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that all terms in the equations have consistent units and dimensions. For example, check that g is in m/s^2 and time is in seconds. Verify that trigonometric functions are dimensionless and that derived quantities have the correct units.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for g (e.g., cm/s^2 instead of m/s^2)
Mismatched units for displacement (e.g., mixing meters and centimeters)
Incorrect dimensional analysis leading to invalid terms in equations

rules.title: Check validity conditions for projectile motion assumptions
rules.description: Projectile motion assumes no air resistance, a constant gravitational field, and motion near the Earth's surface. These assumptions must hold for the equations to be valid.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the problem assumes no air resistance and that the motion occurs in a uniform gravitational field near the Earth's surface. Confirm that the effects of Earth's curvature or Coriolis forces are negligible.
common_errors: Ignoring air resistance in situations where it is significant
Applying projectile motion equations in non-uniform gravitational fields
Extending results to cases where Earth's curvature or Coriolis effects are significant

rules.title: Verify initial conditions for projectile motion
rules.description: The initial velocity, angle, and position must be clearly defined and consistent with the problem setup. These values are critical for accurate calculations.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the initial velocity, angle, and position are explicitly stated and used consistently in all calculations. Verify that the angle is measured from the horizontal and that the initial position is correctly incorporated into displacement equations.
common_errors: Omitting the initial position in displacement calculations
Using an incorrect reference for the launch angle
Inconsistent or undefined initial velocity values

rules.title: Verify Centripetal Force Equation
rules.description: Ensure the centripetal force is calculated using the formula F_c = m*v^2/r, where m is mass, v is velocity, and r is the radius of the circular path.
rules.check_logic: Check if F_c = m*v^2/r is correctly used for centripetal force calculations.
common_errors: Missing or incorrect value for radius r.
Incorrect substitution of linear velocity v with angular velocity.
Incorrect formula used for centripetal force.

rules.title: Check Sign Convention for Centripetal Force
rules.description: Centripetal force always acts inward towards the center of the circular path. Ensure calculations respect this inward direction.
rules.check_logic: Verify centripetal force is directed towards the center (positive inward force).
common_errors: Incorrect sign for centripetal force - treating it as outward.
Misinterpretation of force direction in coordinates.

rules.title: Coordinate System Consistency
rules.description: Ensure the chosen coordinate system consistently reflects all components of motion and forces, usually with radial direction defined inward.
rules.check_logic: Validate that the coordinate system chosen aligns with centripetal acceleration components and force directions.
common_errors: Incorrect notation or axis for radial direction.
Mixing up radial and tangential components.

rules.title: Check Kinematic Constraints for Circular Motion
rules.description: For a body moving in a circle, its velocity vector is tangent to the circle, and its acceleration vector points radially inward.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that velocity is tangential and acceleration is radial and inward.
common_errors: Misalignment of velocity vector as radial.
Incorrect acceleration direction assigned.

rules.title: Validate Conditions for Circular Motion
rules.description: Ensure that assumed circular motion applies under conditions where linear speed is not zero and path follows a circle.
rules.check_logic: Verify linear speed isn't approaching zero and path curvature is consistent with circular geometry.
common_errors: Assuming circular motion when there is linear path deviation.
Incorrectly applying circular motion equations to non-circular movements.

rules.title: Dimensional Consistency in Circular Motion
rules.description: Ensure calculations within circular motion maintain dimensional consistency; particularly verify that units of force, velocity, and radius are compatible.
rules.check_logic: Check all quantities (m, v, r) within F_c = m*v^2/r for dimensionally consistent units.
common_errors: Velocity not in consistent units (e.g., m/s vs km/h).
Mixing up mass units (kg vs g).
Incorrect conversion of radius units.

rules.title: Ensure Proper Use of Angular Variables
rules.description: In circular motion involving angular analysis, ensure angular velocity  and radius r are related correctly by v = *r.
rules.check_logic: Confirm the use of v = *r in problems involving angular motion.
common_errors: Failure to convert between linear and angular velocity.
Mistaking  for linear velocity v.

rules.title: Verification of Additional Forces in Circular Motion
rules.description: Ensure that any additional forces acting on the object in circular motion, such as friction or tension, are correctly identified and incorporated into the total force balance as needed.
rules.check_logic: Check for consideration of external forces beyond centripetal force and how they affect overall motion.
common_errors: Neglecting friction or tension in force balance.
Incorrectly adding or omitting external forces affecting circular motion.

topics.name: Newton's Laws and Free Body Diagrams

rules.title: Verify Correct Form of Newton's Second Law
rules.description: Newton's Second Law states that the sum of the forces acting on an object must equal the mass of the object times its acceleration (ΣF = ma). This fundamental equation applies to any object with mass under the influence of forces.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the sum of forces is expressed as ΣF = ma, where 'm' is the object's mass and 'a' is its acceleration. Verify that all forces acting on the object are included in the summation.
common_errors: Mistaking weight for mass
Incorrectly isolating the acceleration component
Missing force components in the sum

rules.title: Ensure Consistent Sign Convention in Coordinate Systems
rules.description: Whenever forces and accelerations are resolved into components along coordinate axes (e.g., x, y), it is essential to maintain consistent sign conventions (e.g., right and up are positive).
rules.check_logic: Verify that forces and accelerations align with the chosen coordinate system sign conventions throughout the problem. Ensure that the positive and negative directions are clearly defined and consistently applied.
common_errors: Inconsistent sign usage for forces along different axes
Not defining the positive direction
Switching axes without redefining direction

rules.title: Check Vertical Geometric Constraints
rules.description: Geometric constraints can enforce conditions like an object must remain on a surface. For vertical scenarios, tension in a rope or normal force on a surface typically counteracts weight.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the normal force or tension balances vertical forces as per the defined constraint (e.g., no net vertical acceleration if stationary on a surface). Verify that the forces satisfy the geometric constraints of the problem.
common_errors: Neglect of normal forces when an object is on a surface
Incorrect calculation of tension
Ignoring constraints like fixed surfaces or ropes

rules.title: Confirm Conditions for Newton's Laws Application
rules.description: Newton's Laws can only be applied in inertial frames of reference where no acceleration or rotation affects the observer, and forces must be real at macroscopic scale.
rules.check_logic: Check if the problem defines or implies an inertial reference frame. If the frame is non-inertial, ensure pseudo-forces are included to account for the effects of acceleration or rotation.
common_errors: Applying laws without considering inertial frames
Forgetting to account for pseudo-forces in non-inertial reference frames
Misidentifying the frame of reference

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency for Forces
rules.description: In mechanics, forces must be measured in units consistent with mass times acceleration (e.g., Newtons in SI units). Dimensional analysis ensures all terms in an equation balance correctly.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all force and acceleration terms have units consistent with Newtons (kg·m/s²) in SI. Ensure that unit conversions, if any, are correctly applied.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for mass or acceleration
Inconsistent unit usage among different force components
Forgetting to convert units when necessary

rules.title: Check Action-Reaction Force Pairs
rules.description: Newton's Third Law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, meaning forces always occur in pairs between two interacting bodies.
rules.check_logic: Verify that every force has a corresponding equal and opposite reaction force, typically between two interacting bodies in isolation. Ensure that the forces act on different objects and are of the same magnitude but opposite in direction.
common_errors: Forgetting to include or identify reaction forces
Misidentifying action-reaction force pairs
Confusing internal forces with action-reaction pairs

rules.title: Differentiate Between External and Internal Forces
rules.description: For solving and analyzing systems with Newton's Laws, it's crucial to identify external forces acting on a system as distinct from internal forces acting among components in the system.
rules.check_logic: Differentiate and correctly label external forces versus internal forces in system analysis. Ensure that only external forces are included in the equations of motion for the system as a whole.
common_errors: Confusing internal with external forces
Neglecting to include external forces in equations of motion
Incorrectly summing internal forces in system-level analysis

rules.title: Analyze Friction Forces
rules.description: Frictional forces oppose the relative motion or tendency of motion between two surfaces in contact. Static friction prevents motion up to a maximum value, while kinetic friction acts during motion.
rules.check_logic: Verify that frictional forces are correctly identified and calculated using the appropriate coefficients of friction (static or kinetic). Ensure that static friction does not exceed its maximum value (μsN).
common_errors: Using the wrong coefficient of friction
Exceeding the maximum static friction force
Neglecting frictional forces in the analysis

rules.title: Verify Net Force for Equilibrium
rules.description: For an object in equilibrium, the net force acting on it must be zero. This applies to both static equilibrium (no motion) and dynamic equilibrium (constant velocity).
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the sum of all forces acting on the object is zero in both the horizontal and vertical directions. Verify that there is no net acceleration.
common_errors: Forgetting to include all forces in the summation
Incorrectly resolving forces into components
Assuming equilibrium without verifying net force

rules.title: Check static friction force doesn't exceed maximum value
rules.description: Static friction force must always be less than or equal to the maximum static friction force, which is determined by the coefficient of static friction (μ_s) and the normal force (N): f_s ≤ μ_s * N.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the calculated static friction force is less than or equal to μ_s * N. If the object is on the verge of motion, f_s = μ_s * N. Ensure that the object is stationary when applying this rule.
common_errors: Using the coefficient of kinetic friction instead of static friction
Exceeding the maximum static friction force
Misidentifying whether the object is in static equilibrium or moving

rules.title: Ensure kinetic friction formula is correctly applied
rules.description: Kinetic friction force is always equal to μ_k * N, where μ_k is the coefficient of kinetic friction and N is the normal force. This applies only when the object is in motion.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that f_k = μ_k * N is applied only when relative motion exists between the surfaces. Confirm that μ_k is used instead of μ_s for moving objects.
common_errors: Using μ_s instead of μ_k for moving objects
Applying kinetic friction when the object is stationary
Forgetting the normal force component in inclined systems

rules.title: Confirm correct calculation of normal force
rules.description: The normal force is the perpendicular reaction force exerted by a surface. On a flat surface, it equals the weight of the object (mg) if no other vertical forces are present. On an inclined plane, N = mg * cos(θ).
rules.check_logic: Verify that the normal force is calculated based on the correct orientation of the surface and any additional vertical forces. Ensure that the angle of inclination and any applied vertical forces are accounted for.
common_errors: Ignoring the angle of inclination in calculations
Not accounting for additional vertical forces (e.g., applied forces, tension)
Assuming normal force always equals weight

rules.title: Ensure consistent coordinate system and sign conventions
rules.description: Coordinate systems should be defined clearly, with consistent sign conventions for forces and displacements. For inclined planes, axes are typically aligned parallel and perpendicular to the incline.
rules.check_logic: Check that all forces, accelerations, and displacements use a consistent coordinate system and sign convention throughout the problem. Verify that the chosen coordinate system aligns with the problem's geometry.
common_errors: Inconsistent sign for friction or gravitational components
Misalignment of coordinate axes with incline
Switching between coordinate systems mid-solution

rules.title: Verify correct sign for work done by friction
rules.description: Work done by friction is negative if it opposes motion and positive if it aids motion. The work is calculated as W = f * d * cos(θ), where θ is the angle between friction force and displacement.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the sign of work done by friction matches the relative direction of friction force and displacement. Confirm that the displacement component parallel to the force is used in calculations.
common_errors: Assigning incorrect sign to work done by friction
Assuming friction always opposes motion without checking directions
Using displacement instead of the component parallel to force

rules.title: Ensure friction models are applied within validity range
rules.description: Friction models (static and kinetic) are approximations. Static friction applies only when there is no relative motion, and kinetic friction applies only when motion occurs relative to the surface.
rules.check_logic: Verify that static friction is used only for stationary cases and kinetic friction for moving cases. Ensure μ values are realistic (0 ≤ μ ≤ 1 in most cases).
common_errors: Using friction formulas outside their applicable range
Assigning unrealistic values to coefficients of friction
Confusing static and kinetic friction conditions

rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of friction and contact force equations
rules.description: Friction force (f) and normal force (N) must have dimensions of force [M·L/T²], and coefficients of friction (μ_s, μ_k) are dimensionless.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that units in all friction-related equations are consistent and result in proper force units. Verify that coefficients of friction are dimensionless.
common_errors: Using coefficients of friction with dimensions
Incorrect unit conversions for normal force or weight
Mixing incompatible units in calculations

rules.title: Verify geometric constraints on inclined plane problems
rules.description: For inclined planes, the components of weight are mg*sin(θ) along the incline and mg*cos(θ) perpendicular to the incline. These must align with the coordinate system.
rules.check_logic: Check that weight components are resolved correctly using the incline angle and are consistent with the chosen coordinate system. Ensure that sine and cosine are not swapped.
common_errors: Swapping sine and cosine in weight components
Ignoring the angle of inclination in force components
Misapplying trigonometric functions to calculate forces

rules.title: Verify smooth transition between static and kinetic friction
rules.description: When an object transitions from rest to motion, the static friction force reaches its maximum value (f_s = μ_s * N) before kinetic friction (f_k = μ_k * N) takes over.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the transition from static to kinetic friction is handled correctly. Verify that f_s does not exceed μ_s * N and that f_k is applied immediately after motion begins.
common_errors: Allowing static friction to exceed its maximum value during transition
Failing to switch to kinetic friction once motion starts
Using inconsistent friction values during the transition

topics.name: Work-Energy Theorem and Conservation of Energy

rules.title: Verify correct application of the Work-Energy Theorem
rules.description: The Work-Energy Theorem states that the net work done on an object is equal to its change in kinetic energy (W_net = ΔKE). This applies to systems where forces are acting on a single object or a system of objects, without additional constraints like relativity or quantum effects.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the net work (sum of work done by all forces) equals the difference in kinetic energy of the object or system (KE_final - KE_initial).
common_errors: Incorrect computation of work done by individual forces.
Omission of one or more forces contributing to the net work.
Incorrect calculation of change in kinetic energy (e.g., missing 1/2 factor or squaring velocity incorrectly).

rules.title: Ensure proper use of the Conservation of Mechanical Energy
rules.description: The principle of mechanical energy conservation states that the total mechanical energy (kinetic + potential) of a system remains constant if only conservative forces (e.g., gravity, spring forces) act on it. Non-conservative forces, such as friction or air resistance, invalidate this principle.
rules.check_logic: Verify that E_initial = E_final (KE_initial + PE_initial = KE_final + PE_final) when no non-conservative forces are present.
common_errors: Neglecting potential energy contributions for gravity or springs.
Assuming mechanical energy conservation when non-conservative forces are doing work.
Arithmetical errors in summing kinetic and potential energies.

rules.title: Account for work done by non-conservative forces
rules.description: When non-conservative forces (e.g., friction, air resistance) do work, the total mechanical energy changes. The work done by these forces is equal to the change in mechanical energy of the system (W_nc = ΔE_mechanical).
rules.check_logic: Ensure that W_nc = (KE_final + PE_final) - (KE_initial + PE_initial), where W_nc includes work from non-conservative forces.
common_errors: Omitting the contribution of non-conservative forces.
Misinterpreting the direction and sign of work done by non-conservative forces.
Assuming conservation of mechanical energy despite non-conservative forces.

rules.title: Verify correct use of sign conventions for work and energy
rules.description: Work and energy are scalar quantities but can have positive or negative signs based on the direction of forces and displacement. Work is positive if the force component is in the direction of displacement, and negative if it opposes displacement.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that work done by forces is calculated with correct attention to the angle between force and displacement. Check the sign of gravitational potential energy based on the chosen reference point.
common_errors: Incorrect sign for work done by opposing forces (e.g., friction).
Misinterpreting the angle between force and displacement.
Incorrect sign for potential energy due to inconsistent reference height.

rules.title: Check dimensional and unit consistency in work-energy calculations
rules.description: All terms in energy and work calculations should have consistent dimensions of energy (ML^2/T^2) and be expressed in compatible units (e.g., Joules in SI units).
rules.check_logic: Verify that work, kinetic energy, and potential energy terms have consistent dimensions and units throughout the solution.
common_errors: Using incompatible units for mass, distance, and force (e.g., mixing grams with meters and Newtons).
Forgetting to square velocity in kinetic energy calculations.
Incorrect unit conversions (e.g., from cm to meters).

rules.title: Ensure applicability of conservation laws
rules.description: The Conservation of Energy principle or the Work-Energy Theorem applies only in classical mechanics for non-relativistic speeds and non-quantum scenarios. Mechanical energy conservation requires the absence of non-conservative forces.
rules.check_logic: Check that the problem context does not involve relativistic speeds, quantum effects, or significant non-conservative forces when applying conservation laws.
common_errors: Applying conservation laws in scenarios with non-conservative forces without accounting for their work.
Using conservation of energy in relativistic or quantum contexts without modifications.

rules.title: Ensure geometric constraints are respected in energy calculations
rules.description: In problems involving inclined planes, pendulums, or other geometrically constrained systems, the potential energy and displacements must reflect the actual geometry of the system.
rules.check_logic: Verify that potential energy is calculated based on the correct height, and that work calculations properly account for the displacement along the surface or path.
common_errors: Using vertical height instead of displacement along an incline.
Ignoring the geometry when calculating work done by forces.
Misrepresenting angles or distances in trigonometric calculations.

rules.title: Verify work-power relationship in dynamic systems
rules.description: Power is the rate at which work is done, and it is related to force and velocity in dynamic systems (P = F·v for constant force and velocity).
rules.check_logic: Ensure that power calculations appropriately relate to the work done over time or force applied at a specific velocity.
common_errors: Using incorrect formulas for power in dynamic systems.
Confusing instantaneous power with average power.
Neglecting time dependence when calculating work and power.

rules.title: Verify Power is the Dot Product of Force and Velocity
rules.description: Power is calculated as the dot product of the force vector and the velocity vector of the object. This assumes the force and velocity are expressed in the same coordinate system.
rules.check_logic: Ensure Power P = F · v = F_x*v_x + F_y*v_y + F_z*v_z, where F and v are vectors in the same coordinate system.
common_errors: Using scalar multiplication instead of dot product
Ignoring directional components of force and velocity
Using mismatched coordinate systems for force and velocity

rules.title: Check Conservation of Energy with Dissipative Forces
rules.description: When dissipative forces like friction are present, mechanical energy is not conserved. Energy is transformed into heat or other forms of non-mechanical energy.
rules.check_logic: Verify if E_final = E_initial - work_done_by_dissipative_forces, where work_done_by_dissipative_forces accounts for friction, air resistance, or other non-conservative forces.
common_errors: Forgetting to subtract work done by friction from total energy
Incorrectly assuming mechanical energy is conserved in the presence of friction
Failing to account for all forms of dissipative forces

rules.title: Ensure Mechanical Energy Dimensional Consistency
rules.description: Mechanical energy equations must adhere to dimensional consistency, ensuring all terms relating to energy are expressed in Joules.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all energy terms have units consistent with kg·m^2/s^2 (Joules) and that unit conversions are correctly applied.
common_errors: Using conflicting units for energy calculations
Omitting proper conversion between units
Mixing incompatible unit systems (e.g., SI and imperial)

rules.title: Validate Power Calculation Over Time
rules.description: Power is the rate of energy transfer over time. For scenarios involving energy changes, power is calculated as the derivative of energy with respect to time.
rules.check_logic: Ensure P = dE/dt, where E is the total energy including potential, kinetic, and work done. Verify that the time derivative is correctly computed.
common_errors: Ignoring rate of change of energy over time
Calculating power without considering energy changes over time
Misinterpreting the derivative of energy with respect to time

rules.title: Confirm Correct Sign Convention in Calculations
rules.description: Power and energy equations are sensitive to the sign convention used in the coordinate system. Ensure consistent use of positive and negative signs based on component directions.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the sign convention is consistent across all calculations, particularly for forces and motion directions that contribute positively or negatively to power.
common_errors: Inconsistent sign usage leading to incorrect power calculation
Missing negative sign in calculations involving resistance forces like friction
Using conflicting sign conventions in different parts of the calculation

rules.title: Ensure Dynamic Conditions for Accurate Power Analysis
rules.description: Power analysis requires objects to be moving. Static cases with zero velocity should not involve power calculations linked to kinetic aspects.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that velocity v ≠ 0 for legitimate power calculation. If v = 0, ensure power is not attributed to kinetic energy transfer.
common_errors: Calculating power for static cases where object velocity is zero
Ignoring the need for motion in assessing power
Misinterpreting static forces as contributing to power

rules.title: Identify Misapplications of Frictionless Power Assumptions
rules.description: In scenarios with significant friction, assumptions that power can be transferred through frictionless work are invalid.
rules.check_logic: Verify that frictional forces are accounted for in power calculations, especially in systems where friction is non-negligible.
common_errors: Assuming frictionless conditions in a friction-present scenario
Excluding friction from work calculations leading to power
Underestimating the impact of friction on energy dissipation

rules.title: Assess Geometric Constraints in Energy Calculations
rules.description: Energy calculations involving geometric constraints such as inclines or curves must consider the modified forces and resulting work/energy changes.
rules.check_logic: Verify that geometric parameters like angle of incline, curvature, or path constraints are accounted for in energy formulations.
common_errors: Neglecting incline angles in potential energy and work calculations
Using straight path assumptions in geometrically constrained problems
Ignoring the effect of curvature on energy dissipation or work

rules.title: Validate Work-Energy Theorem Application
rules.description: The work-energy theorem states that the net work done on an object is equal to its change in kinetic energy. Ensure this principle is correctly applied.
rules.check_logic: Verify that W_net = ΔK = K_final - K_initial, where W_net is the total work done by all forces.
common_errors: Ignoring contributions of all forces to net work
Miscalculating changes in kinetic energy
Applying the theorem incorrectly in non-inertial reference frames

rules.title: Ensure Correct Reference Point for Potential Energy
rules.description: Potential energy calculations depend on the choice of a reference point. Ensure the reference point is clearly defined and consistently used.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the reference point for potential energy (e.g., height = 0) is explicitly stated and consistently applied in calculations.
common_errors: Using inconsistent reference points for potential energy
Failing to define a reference point in energy problems
Misinterpreting relative potential energy differences

rules.title: Verify Conservation of Linear Momentum
rules.description: In an isolated system with no external forces, the total linear momentum before and after a collision or interaction remains constant. This principle applies to both elastic and inelastic collisions.
rules.check_logic: Ensure no net external forces act on the system. Verify that the vector sum of initial momenta equals the vector sum of final momenta.
common_errors: Ignoring external forces acting on the system
Miscalculating momentum as a scalar instead of a vector
Using incorrect initial or final velocities

rules.title: Verify Kinetic Energy Conservation in Elastic Collisions
rules.description: In elastic collisions, both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved due to the absence of energy dissipation (e.g., no deformation or heat generation).
rules.check_logic: Identify if the collision is elastic. Confirm that the total kinetic energy before the collision equals the total kinetic energy after the collision.
common_errors: Forgetting to verify if the collision is elastic
Incorrectly calculating kinetic energy (e.g., missing the 1/2 factor or squaring velocities)
Misinterpreting inelastic collisions as elastic

rules.title: Account for Energy Loss in Inelastic Collisions
rules.description: In inelastic collisions, kinetic energy is not conserved due to energy dissipating into other forms like heat, sound, or deformation. Only momentum is conserved.
rules.check_logic: Determine if the collision is inelastic. Verify that kinetic energy is not conserved, while momentum conservation is still satisfied.
common_errors: Assuming kinetic energy conservation in inelastic collisions
Failing to account for energy loss mechanisms
Incorrectly applying momentum conservation due to external forces

rules.title: Check Relative Velocity Relationship in Elastic Collisions
rules.description: In one-dimensional elastic collisions, the relative velocity of approach before collision equals the relative velocity of separation after collision.
rules.check_logic: For elastic collisions, verify that the magnitude of the initial relative velocity equals the magnitude of the final relative velocity.
common_errors: Forgetting to apply the relative velocity condition
Using incorrect signs for velocities
Confusing initial and final velocities

rules.title: Verify Application of Impulse-Momentum Theorem
rules.description: The impulse-momentum theorem states that the impulse applied to an object equals the change in its linear momentum. This is applicable in scenarios where forces act over a short time interval.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that impulse (force × time duration) equals the change in momentum (mΔv).
common_errors: Incorrectly calculating impulse (e.g., neglecting force-time duration)
Forgetting to account for direction (vector nature of momentum)
Mixing up initial and final velocities

rules.title: Check Dimensional Consistency of Momentum and Impulse
rules.description: Momentum has units of mass × velocity (kg·m/s), and impulse also shares the same units. Dimensional consistency ensures that equations involving momentum and impulse are correctly formulated.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all terms in momentum and impulse equations have consistent units (e.g., kg·m/s).
common_errors: Using incorrect units for velocity or mass
Failing to match units of impulse and momentum
Mixing up scalar and vector quantities

rules.title: Ensure Proper Use of Sign Conventions in Momentum Calculations
rules.description: Momentum is a vector quantity, and its sign depends on the chosen coordinate system. Proper sign conventions must be maintained for accurate calculations.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that velocity components and resulting momentum values respect the chosen coordinate system (e.g., positive for rightward, negative for leftward).
common_errors: Assigning incorrect signs to velocities or momenta
Inconsistently applying the coordinate system
Neglecting vector nature of momentum in multi-dimensional problems

rules.title: Ensure Validity Conditions for Momentum Conservation
rules.description: Momentum conservation applies only in isolated systems with no external forces. This condition must be verified before applying the conservation law.
rules.check_logic: Determine if the system is isolated with no net external force. If not, momentum conservation cannot be directly applied.
common_errors: Failing to check for external forces before applying conservation laws
Misidentifying internal and external forces
Applying momentum conservation to non-isolated systems

rules.title: Determine Collision Type Before Analysis
rules.description: Identifying whether a collision is elastic or inelastic is essential for applying the correct conservation principles.
rules.check_logic: Establish whether the collision is elastic or inelastic based on the presence of kinetic energy conservation.
common_errors: Neglecting to determine if a collision is elastic or inelastic
Confusing criteria for elastic and inelastic collisions
Attempting to apply inappropriate conservation laws

rules.title: Verify Impulse-Momentum Theorem Application
rules.description: The impulse-momentum theorem states that the change in momentum of an object (Δp) is equal to the impulse (F_net * Δt) applied to it. This applies when forces act over a specific time interval.
rules.check_logic: Verify if Δp (m*v_final - m*v_initial) equals F_net * Δt, ensuring all quantities are correctly calculated and vector directions are considered.
common_errors: Incorrect calculation of Δp by missing one of the velocity terms.
Forgetting to consider the force as a vector, leading to incorrect direction.
Using average force instead of net force.

rules.title: Verify Momentum Conservation in Isolated Systems
rules.description: Momentum is conserved in an isolated system where no external forces act. The total momentum before interaction equals the total momentum after interaction.
rules.check_logic: Verify if Σp_initial = Σp_final for all objects involved in the system, ensuring vector components are handled correctly.
common_errors: Forgetting to include all objects in the system.
Misidentifying forces as external when they are internal.
Incorrectly handling vector components of momentum.

rules.title: Verify Correct Sign Conventions for Momentum and Forces
rules.description: Momentum and force are vector quantities. The choice of a coordinate system determines the sign of these quantities. Consistent use of sign convention is crucial.
rules.check_logic: Verify if momentum (m*v) and impulse (F_net * Δt) have signs consistent with the chosen coordinate system, and ensure all vector components are correctly signed in multi-dimensional problems.
common_errors: Using inconsistent sign conventions for velocity and force.
Assigning incorrect signs to momentum components in 2D or 3D problems.

rules.title: Check Constraints for Elastic Collisions
rules.description: In an elastic collision, both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved. This constraint applies only when no energy is lost to deformation, heat, or other mechanisms.
rules.check_logic: Verify if both Σp_initial = Σp_final and ΣKE_initial = ΣKE_final hold true, and confirm that no energy is lost to non-conservative forces.
common_errors: Conserving only momentum and neglecting kinetic energy conservation.
Incorrectly assuming a collision is elastic when energy dissipation is evident.

rules.title: Check Constraints for Perfectly Inelastic Collisions
rules.description: In a perfectly inelastic collision, momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not. The colliding bodies stick together after collision.
rules.check_logic: Verify if Σp_initial = Σp_final and confirm that the final velocities of colliding objects are equal, ensuring proper calculation of kinetic energy loss.
common_errors: Forgetting that the final velocities of the objects must be equal.
Incorrectly calculating loss of kinetic energy.

rules.title: Verify Dimensional Consistency of Impulse and Momentum Equations
rules.description: The quantities in impulse and momentum equations must have consistent units and dimensions. Impulse has the same dimensions as momentum (ML/T).
rules.check_logic: Ensure that F_net * Δt and m*v have consistent units (e.g., kg·m/s), and verify that all unit conversions are correctly applied.
common_errors: Mixing incompatible units for force, time, mass, or velocity.
Using inconsistent time units between Δt and velocity calculations.

rules.title: Check Validity Conditions for Momentum Conservation
rules.description: Momentum conservation only applies to isolated systems with no net external force. If external forces exist, they must be accounted for in the impulse-momentum theorem.
rules.check_logic: Verify if F_net_external = 0 for the system. If not, apply the impulse-momentum theorem instead of momentum conservation, and ensure external forces like friction or applied forces are modeled accurately.
common_errors: Applying momentum conservation in the presence of significant external forces.
Failing to model external forces like friction or applied force accurately.

rules.title: Verify Impulse from Force-Time Graph
rules.description: The impulse imparted to an object is equal to the area under the force-time graph over the time interval of interest.
rules.check_logic: Verify if the calculated impulse (area under the curve) matches the change in momentum (Δp), ensuring proper integration of the graph, including negative areas.
common_errors: Incorrect integration of the force-time graph (e.g., missing negative areas).
Using only peak force instead of calculating the area under the curve.

rules.title: Verify Collision Analysis in Different Frames of Reference
rules.description: Momentum conservation and collision analysis must hold true in any inertial frame of reference. Transformations between frames must preserve relative velocities and momentum.
rules.check_logic: Verify if momentum conservation and collision constraints are satisfied in the chosen frame of reference, and ensure proper transformations between frames.
common_errors: Failing to account for relative velocities when switching frames.
Incorrectly applying momentum conservation in non-inertial frames.

rules.title: Verify rotational kinematic equation consistency
rules.description: Ensure that the rotational kinematic equations (e.g., θ = ω₀t + 0.5αt², ω = ω₀ + αt) are applied correctly. These equations require constant angular acceleration.
rules.check_logic: Check if the problem explicitly states or implies constant angular acceleration. If angular acceleration is variable or unspecified, rotational kinematic equations cannot be used.
common_errors: Using rotational kinematic equations when angular acceleration is not constant.
Incorrect substitution of angular acceleration (α) or initial angular velocity (ω₀).
Mixing up linear and rotational variables (e.g., using linear acceleration in place of angular acceleration).

rules.title: Ensure consistent sign conventions for angular quantities
rules.description: Angular displacement, velocity, and acceleration can be positive or negative depending on the chosen coordinate system. Ensure consistency in the sign conventions throughout the solution.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the student has explicitly chosen a direction (e.g., counterclockwise as positive) and maintained this convention for all angular quantities. Ensure that any changes in sign are justified by the problem's setup.
common_errors: Switching sign conventions partway through the solution.
Incorrectly assigning signs to angular quantities based on direction.
Confusing clockwise and counterclockwise directions in the coordinate system.

rules.title: Validate torque equation application
rules.description: Torque (τ) is given by τ = r × F = rFsin(θ), where r is the lever arm, F is the force, and θ is the angle between r and F. This equation is valid for rigid bodies with forces applied at a fixed distance.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the student calculates torque using the correct r, F, and θ, and ensures the force is not passing through the axis of rotation. Confirm that the direction of torque is consistent with the right-hand rule.
common_errors: Forgetting to include the sin(θ) factor when torque is not perpendicular to the lever arm.
Using the wrong value for r (e.g., distance to the wrong axis of rotation).
Omitting torque contributions when multiple forces act on the body.

rules.title: Check conservation of rotational mechanical energy
rules.description: The total rotational mechanical energy (K_rot = 0.5Iω²) is conserved in the absence of non-conservative torques, such as friction. Ensure this principle is applied only when valid.
rules.check_logic: Verify that no non-conservative torques are present before applying rotational energy conservation. If friction or other dissipative forces exist, include their work in the energy balance. Ensure that all forms of energy (rotational, translational, potential) are accounted for.
common_errors: Applying conservation of rotational energy in the presence of non-conservative torques.
Forgetting to include rotational kinetic energy in total energy calculations.
Incorrectly calculating the rotational inertia (I) of the object.

rules.title: Verify correct calculation of moment of inertia
rules.description: Moment of inertia (I) depends on the mass distribution relative to the axis of rotation. Using the correct formula or integral is critical.
rules.check_logic: Check if the student uses the appropriate formula for I based on the geometry and axis of rotation (e.g., I = 0.5MR² for a solid disk about its central axis). For irregular objects, verify the use of integration. Ensure the parallel axis theorem is applied when the axis of rotation is shifted.
common_errors: Using the wrong formula for the shape and axis of rotation.
Forgetting to apply the parallel axis theorem when necessary.
Incorrectly calculating or integrating for non-standard geometries.

rules.title: Validate conservation of angular momentum
rules.description: Angular momentum (L = Iω) is conserved in a system with no external torques. Ensure this principle is applied only when external torques are absent.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the problem specifies or implies no external torques before assuming conservation of angular momentum. Confirm that changes in angular momentum are consistent with changes in I or ω when mass distribution changes.
common_errors: Applying conservation of angular momentum in the presence of external torques.
Incorrectly calculating angular momentum (e.g., using the wrong I or ω).
Failing to account for changes in I when the distribution of mass changes.

rules.title: Ensure correct linkage between linear and rotational kinematics
rules.description: For rolling objects or systems combining linear and rotational motion, ensure correct use of the relation v = ωr, a_t = αr, and s = θr.
rules.check_logic: Check if the student uses the correct relationship between linear and angular quantities based on the rolling condition or constraint. Verify that rolling without slipping is explicitly stated or implied before using these relations.
common_errors: Using v = ωr when the object is not rolling without slipping.
Confusing tangential and radial acceleration.
Forgetting to apply rolling constraints when required.

rules.title: Verify dimensional and unit consistency in rotational quantities
rules.description: Ensure that all equations involving angular quantities (e.g., torque, angular momentum) are dimensionally consistent and use appropriate units (e.g., radians, N·m).
rules.check_logic: Verify that units for angular displacement (radians), angular velocity (rad/s), angular acceleration (rad/s²), torque (N·m), and moment of inertia (kg·m²) are consistent throughout the solution. Ensure radians are used in calculations involving angular quantities.
common_errors: Using degrees instead of radians in rotational equations.
Mixing linear and angular units (e.g., using m/s instead of rad/s).
Incorrectly simplifying or canceling units in torque or energy calculations.

rules.title: Verify understanding of gyroscopic precession
rules.description: For rotating objects experiencing a torque perpendicular to their angular momentum, ensure the precession motion is correctly analyzed.
rules.check_logic: Check if the student uses the relation Ω = τ / L, where Ω is the precession angular velocity, τ is the applied torque, and L is the angular momentum. Verify that the direction of precession is consistent with the right-hand rule.
common_errors: Incorrectly calculating the precession angular velocity.
Ignoring the direction of precession determined by the torque and angular momentum.
Confusing precession with simple rotational motion.

topics.name: Moment of Inertia and Rotational Energy

rules.title: Verify rotational kinetic energy formula
rules.description: The rotational kinetic energy is given by the formula: KE_rot = (1/2)Ic9�b2, where I is the moment of inertia and c9 is the angular velocity. This equation applies to rigid bodies in rotation about a fixed axis.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the rotational kinetic energy is calculated using KE_rot = (1/2)Ic9�b2, and verify that I (moment of inertia) and c9 (angular velocity) are correctly identified, calculated, and used.
common_errors: Forgetting the (1/2) factor in the equation
Using linear velocity (v) instead of angular velocity (c9)
Incorrectly calculating or omitting the moment of inertia (I)

rules.title: Apply the parallel axis theorem correctly
rules.description: The parallel axis theorem states that I_total = I_cm + Md�b2, where I_cm is the moment of inertia about the center of mass, M is the mass of the object, and d is the distance from the axis of rotation to the center of mass.
rules.check_logic: Verify if the moment of inertia for an axis not passing through the center of mass is calculated using the parallel axis theorem. Ensure accurate values for d (distance) and M (mass) are used, and confirm that I_cm is correctly determined.
common_errors: Omitting the Md�b2 term when shifting the axis of rotation
Using the wrong distance (d) between the center of mass and the rotation axis
Confusing I_cm with I about the given axis

rules.title: Check perpendicular axis theorem application
rules.description: The perpendicular axis theorem states that for a planar object, I_z = I_x + I_y, where I_z is the moment of inertia about an axis perpendicular to the plane, and I_x and I_y are about axes in the plane. This is valid only for thin, planar objects.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the perpendicular axis theorem is applied only to thin, planar objects. Verify that I_x and I_y are correctly calculated and summed to determine I_z, and confirm that the axes intersect at a single point.
common_errors: Applying the theorem to non-planar or 3D objects
Incorrectly summing I_x and I_y
Using the theorem when axes do not intersect at a single point

rules.title: Verify units of moment of inertia
rules.description: The moment of inertia (I) has the SI unit kg�b7m�b2, derived from the formula I = a mr�b2, where m is the mass and r is the distance. Consistency of units is critical in calculations.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that the final unit of I is kg�b7m�b2. Verify that all inputs (mass in kilograms, distance in meters) are in correct units, and ensure that the distance is squared (r�b2) when summing terms in I.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for mass or distance
Failing to square the distance (r�b2) when summing terms in I
Using inconsistent units (e.g., grams instead of kilograms)

rules.title: Check rotational energy conservation
rules.description: Rotational energy is conserved if there are no external torques acting on the system. This applies to isolated systems or systems with purely conservative internal forces.
rules.check_logic: Verify if external torques are zero. If yes, ensure the total rotational energy remains constant over time. Confirm that friction or other non-conservative forces are absent.
common_errors: Ignoring external torques that do work on the system
Assuming rotational energy conservation in the presence of friction
Confusing conservation of rotational energy with conservation of angular momentum

rules.title: Ensure correct sign convention for torque
rules.description: Torque (c4) is defined as c4 = r �d F = rFsin�3b8, where the direction is determined using the right-hand rule. Positive torque typically corresponds to counterclockwise rotation, and negative torque to clockwise rotation.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that the torque sign is determined using the right-hand rule and is consistent with the chosen coordinate system. Verify that the angle �3b8 is correctly used in c4 = rFsin�3b8.
common_errors: Reversing the sign convention for clockwise and counterclockwise torques
Neglecting the angle �3b8 in c4 = rFsin�3b8
Forgetting to use the cross product properly

rules.title: Verify geometric constraints in rotational systems
rules.description: In rotational mechanics, constraints like fixed radii or rigid body rotations must be respected. For example, all points on a rigid rotating disk have the same angular velocity but different linear velocities.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that angular velocity (c9) is constant across the rigid body and that linear velocity (v = rc9) is calculated appropriately for different points. Confirm that rigid body assumptions are not violated.
common_errors: Assuming linear velocity is the same for all points on a rigid body
Failing to account for the dependency of linear velocity on radius (v = rc9)
Applying non-rigid body assumptions to rigid systems

rules.title: Perform dimensional analysis for rotational energy equations
rules.description: The equations for rotational energy and moment of inertia must be dimensionally consistent. For example, KE_rot = (1/2)Ic9�b2 should result in units of energy (kg�b7m�b2/s�b2).
rules.check_logic: Verify that each term in the rotational energy equation has compatible dimensions, and the final result has dimensions of energy (kg�b7m�b2/s�b2). Ensure that I and c9 are expressed in consistent units.
common_errors: Omitting or miscalculating the square of c9 in KE_rot = (1/2)Ic9�b2
Using inconsistent units for I or c9
Failing to check that the final energy has units of kg�b7m�b2/s�b2

rules.title: Verify angular momentum conservation
rules.description: Angular momentum is conserved in a system if there are no external torques acting on it. This principle applies to both rigid bodies and systems of particles.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that external torques are zero. If so, verify that the total angular momentum (L = Ic9) remains constant over time. Check that changes in I or c9 are consistent with conservation.
common_errors: Ignoring external torques that affect angular momentum
Assuming angular momentum conservation in the presence of friction or other non-conservative forces
Failing to account for changes in I or c9 when analyzing the system

rules.title: Verify torque equilibrium condition
rules.description: For a system in static equilibrium, the sum of all torques acting on the system about any axis must be zero. This ensures rotational equilibrium.
rules.check_logic: Check if the sum of torques (A3A4) equals zero around the chosen axis of rotation.
common_errors: Forgetting to include all torque contributions (e.g., reaction forces or weights)
Incorrectly calculating the lever arm (distance perpendicular to the force)
Using inconsistent torque directions (e.g., mixing clockwise and counterclockwise signs)

rules.title: Verify force equilibrium condition
rules.description: For a system in static equilibrium, the sum of all forces acting on the system in each direction (x, y, z) must be zero. This ensures translational equilibrium.
rules.check_logic: Verify that A3A2F_x = 0, A3A2F_y = 0, and A3A2F_z = 0 for the system.
common_errors: Omitting a force component (e.g., friction or normal force)
Incorrectly resolving forces into their components
Using the wrong sign convention when summing forces

rules.title: Ensure consistent torque sign convention
rules.description: Torque direction follows a sign convention: counterclockwise torques are often considered positive, and clockwise torques are negative. This must be consistent throughout the solution.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all torques adhere to a consistent sign convention (e.g., CCW positive, CW negative).
common_errors: Mixing clockwise and counterclockwise signs inconsistently
Using the wrong sign convention for a specific torque

rules.title: Check pivot point selection for torque analysis
rules.description: The choice of pivot point for torque calculation can be flexible, but a strategically chosen pivot point can simplify the analysis by eliminating torque contributions from unknown forces.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the pivot point is logically selected to simplify calculations and check that torque calculations are correctly performed about this point.
common_errors: Choosing a pivot point that adds complexity unnecessarily
Omitting torque contributions about the chosen pivot point
Incorrectly assuming torque cancels at the pivot point without verification

rules.title: Ensure conditions for static equilibrium are met
rules.description: Static equilibrium assumes the system is stationary, with no net acceleration or angular acceleration. This is valid only if the system is truly at rest or moving at constant velocity.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that the system is either stationary or moving at a constant velocity before proceeding with static equilibrium equations.
common_errors: Using static equilibrium equations for a system undergoing acceleration
Neglecting external influences that could induce motion

rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency in torque calculations
rules.description: Torque is represented as the product of force in Newtons and distance in meters, thus its unit is Newton-meters (N�b7m).
rules.check_logic: Ensure torque calculations maintain dimensional consistency with results expressed in N�b7m.
common_errors: Mixing incompatible units in torque calculations (e.g., using kilograms instead of Newtons)
Failing to multiply the force by the lever arm distance to calculate torque

rules.title: Verify geometric constraints in lever arms
rules.description: The lever arm is the shortest (perpendicular) distance from the axis of rotation to the force's line of action. Errors in geometry can skew torque calculations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that lever arms are correctly measured as perpendicular distances to the force's line of action.
common_errors: Using an incorrect measurement for the lever arm (not perpendicular)
Misidentifying the point of application for force leading to incorrect lever arm calculations

rules.title: Ensure correct application of static friction limits
rules.description: Static friction opposes motion up to a maximum value given by f_s �A4 �B5_s�B7N, where �B5_s is the coefficient of static friction and N is the normal force.
rules.check_logic: Verify that static friction remains within its limit �A4 �B5_s�B7N and effectively prevents motion.
common_errors: Exceeding the static friction limit in calculations
Incorrect normal force determination affecting friction calculations
Assuming static friction acts when unnecessary

rules.title: Check the angle of torque application
rules.description: Torque is maximized when force is applied perpendicular to the lever arm. The angle at which force is applied influences the torque produced.
rules.check_logic: Ensure forces contributing to torque are evaluated considering the angle of application and its effect on torque magnitude.
common_errors: Ignoring the angle between force and lever arm
Misusing trigonometric functions to resolve torque components

rules.title: Verify angular momentum conservation equation
rules.description: Angular momentum is conserved if no external torque acts on a system. Mathematically, L_initial = L_final, where L = Iω for rigid bodies (moment of inertia times angular velocity).
rules.check_logic: Check if the net external torque on the system is zero. If torque = 0, ensure L_initial = L_final. Verify that the moment of inertia and angular velocity are correctly calculated for all components of the system.
common_errors: Forgetting to check for external torques on the system.
Using incorrect moments of inertia for the system components.
Not accounting for changes in rotational inertia when the system configuration changes.

rules.title: Ensure consistent sign convention for angular momentum
rules.description: Angular momentum is a vector quantity. Its sign depends on the direction of rotation, usually determined using the right-hand rule.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the chosen direction (e.g., clockwise or counterclockwise) is consistently applied for all angular momentum and torque calculations. Ensure the right-hand rule is correctly applied to determine the direction of angular momentum vectors.
common_errors: Mixing up clockwise and counterclockwise directions in the same problem.
Applying the right-hand rule incorrectly for angular momentum directions.
Ignoring the vector nature of angular momentum and treating it as a scalar.

rules.title: Check validity of angular momentum conservation
rules.description: Angular momentum conservation only applies if the system is isolated with no external torques. Ensure this condition is satisfied before applying the conservation law.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the sum of external torques acting on the system is zero before applying angular momentum conservation. Explicitly check for frictional or other non-conservative forces that might introduce external torques.
common_errors: Applying angular momentum conservation when external torques are present.
Ignoring frictional or other non-conservative torques that act on the system.

rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency of angular momentum equations
rules.description: Angular momentum (L) has SI units of kg·m²/s. Ensure that all terms in the equations are dimensionally consistent.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that angular momentum, torque, and angular velocity terms respect their respective units (kg·m²/s, N·m, rad/s). Check that all derived quantities are dimensionally consistent.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for moment of inertia or angular velocity.
Adding or equating terms with incompatible dimensions (e.g., torque and angular momentum).

rules.title: Verify kinematic constraints in angular momentum systems
rules.description: For systems with geometric constraints (e.g., a pulley or rotating bar), ensure the angular velocity and radius relationships are correctly applied.
rules.check_logic: Check if v = rω is satisfied for linear and angular velocities, or if other constraints (e.g., rope length conservation) are respected. Verify that the radius used in torque or angular momentum calculations corresponds to the correct point of application.
common_errors: Incorrectly relating linear velocity to angular velocity.
Ignoring constraints imposed by fixed pivots or hinges.
Misinterpreting radius in the torque or angular momentum calculations.

rules.title: Verify torque-angular momentum relationship
rules.description: The rate of change of angular momentum equals the net external torque acting on the system: τ = dL/dt. Ensure this relationship holds when external torques are present.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the derivative of angular momentum matches the calculated torque for non-conservation cases. Ensure that the torque is calculated using the correct lever arm and force direction.
common_errors: Neglecting time-dependence of angular momentum in non-conservation cases.
Calculating torque incorrectly (e.g., using incorrect lever arm or force).
Confusing internal forces/torques with external ones.

rules.title: Account for system redefinition during motion
rules.description: If the system's boundaries change (e.g., a person moving inward on a rotating platform), ensure the change in moment of inertia is properly accounted for.
rules.check_logic: Check for changes in system configuration and verify that the moment of inertia and angular velocity are updated accordingly. Ensure that the conservation of angular momentum is applied correctly to the redefined system.
common_errors: Failing to adjust the moment of inertia for changing system boundaries.
Assuming angular velocity remains constant when the moment of inertia changes.
Incorrectly summing or redistributing masses in composite systems.

rules.title: Relate conservation of angular momentum to kinetic energy
rules.description: In systems where angular momentum is conserved, rotational kinetic energy may change if the moment of inertia changes. Verify the relationship between rotational kinetic energy (1/2 Iω²) and angular momentum.
rules.check_logic: Check if changes in rotational kinetic energy are consistent with conservation of angular momentum and changes in moment of inertia. Verify that the correct formulas for rotational kinetic energy and angular momentum are used.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming rotational kinetic energy is conserved when angular momentum is conserved.
Failing to account for changes in angular velocity when moment of inertia changes.
Using incorrect formulas for rotational kinetic energy.

rules.title: Account for external forces affecting angular momentum
rules.description: External forces can create torques that affect angular momentum. Ensure all external forces and their lever arms are accounted for in torque calculations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all external forces acting on the system are identified and their torques are calculated correctly. Ensure that the net torque is consistent with the observed changes in angular momentum.
common_errors: Ignoring external forces that create torques.
Incorrectly calculating lever arms for external forces.
Failing to distinguish between internal and external forces.

rules.title: Verify Universal Law of Gravitation Formula
