rules.description: Ensure that the formula F = G * (m1 * m2) / r^2 is correctly applied to calculate the gravitational force between two masses.
rules.check_logic: Check if the gravitational force F between two masses m1 and m2 is calculated using the formula F = G * (m1 * m2) / r^2, where r is the distance between the masses. Verify that G is the gravitational constant and has the correct value and units.
common_errors: Using incorrect formula for gravitational force
Confusing r (distance) with other lengths
Neglecting the inverse square dependence on distance
Using incorrect value or units for G

rules.title: Validate Kepler's First Law of Elliptical Orbits
rules.description: Confirm that the trajectory of a planet follows an elliptical orbit with the sun at one of the focal points.
rules.check_logic: Check if the orbit is described as elliptical with the sun at one focus, conforming to Kepler's First Law. Ensure that the ellipse's parameters (semi-major axis, semi-minor axis, and eccentricity) are correctly defined.
common_errors: Assuming circular orbits instead of elliptical
Misplacing the sun not at a focal point
Inaccurate identification of the orbit's major/minor axes
Incorrect calculation of eccentricity

rules.title: Validate Kepler's Second Law of Equal Areas
rules.description: Confirm that a line joining a planet and the sun sweeps out equal areas in equal times, indicating variable orbital speed.
rules.check_logic: Check the description of constant areal velocity, ensuring equal area is swept in equal time intervals. Verify that the planet's speed is higher when closer to the sun and lower when farther away, consistent with the law.
common_errors: Assuming constant speed rather than variable speed
Misinterpretation of equal areas over unequal times
Incorrectly visualizing the areas swept
Neglecting the relationship between speed and distance from the sun

rules.title: Check Kepler's Third Law of Planetary Motion
rules.description: Ensure the square of a planet's orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit.
rules.check_logic: Verify if the relation T^2 = k * a^3 holds for orbital period T and semi-major axis a, where k is the proportionality constant. Ensure the correct units are used for T and a.
common_errors: Neglecting the proportionality constant
Confusion between period and frequency
Using wrong units for period and semi-major axis
Ignoring the dependence of k on the central mass

rules.title: Check Gravitational Force Direction and Sign
rules.description: Ensure gravitational force vectors are directed towards the center of mass, reflecting the attractive nature of gravity.
rules.check_logic: Verify if force vectors are directed inwardly towards the body exerting gravitational force, with negative sign in radial coordinates indicating attraction. Confirm that the vector representation is consistent with the coordinate system used.
common_errors: Using incorrect sign for attractive force
Considering forces as repulsive
Mistakes in vector direction
Inconsistent vector representation in different coordinate systems

rules.title: Verify Coordinate System Use for Gravitation
rules.description: Ensure calculations use consistent coordinate systems, commonly polar or spherical coordinates for planetary motion analysis.
rules.check_logic: Check uniform application of coordinate systems ensuring consistency in distance (r), angles (theta), and orientation. Verify that transformations between coordinate systems, if used, are correctly applied.
common_errors: Inconsistent application of coordinate systems
Mixing Cartesian and Polar coordinates incorrectly
Errors in angular component assignment
Incorrect transformations between coordinate systems

rules.title: Check Dimensional Consistency in Gravitational Calculations
rules.description: Verify that all terms and quantities in relevant equations have consistent and correct units and dimensions.
rules.check_logic: Ensure each physical quantity adheres to dimensional consistency principle and proper unit usage, e.g., [F] = [MLT^-2], [G] = [L^3M^-1T^-2]. Check for unit conversions where necessary.
common_errors: Incorrect or inconsistent units for force and gravitational constant
Misalignment in units of distance and mass
Overlooking unit conversions in physics problems
Using inconsistent units across different terms in the equation

rules.title: Ensure Conditions of Gravitational Field Validity
rules.description: Confirm the applicability of gravitational laws assuming point masses and non-relativistic speeds when calculating gravitational interaction.
rules.check_logic: Verify the assumption of point-like masses and ignore relativistic effects unless specified otherwise. Ensure that the gravitational field is calculated under conditions where Newtonian mechanics is valid.
common_errors: Applying gravitational laws to non-point masses without adjustments
Ignoring relativistic corrections where necessary
Assuming universal applicability without checking validity conditions
Using Newtonian mechanics in relativistic scenarios without justification

rules.title: Verify Gravitational Potential Energy Formula
rules.description: Ensure that the formula U = -G * (m1 * m2) / r is correctly applied to calculate gravitational potential energy between two masses.
rules.check_logic: Check if the gravitational potential energy U between two masses m1 and m2 is calculated using the formula U = -G * (m1 * m2) / r, where r is the distance between the masses. Verify the negative sign indicating the attractive nature of gravity.
common_errors: Using incorrect formula for gravitational potential energy
Neglecting the negative sign in the formula
Confusing r (distance) with other lengths
Using incorrect value or units for G

topics.name: Non-inertial Reference Frames and Pseudo Forces

rules.title: Apply pseudo force in non-inertial frames
rules.description: In a non-inertial reference frame, an additional pseudo force must be introduced to account for the observed motion. The pseudo force is given by F_pseudo = -m * a_frame, where m is the mass of the object and a_frame is the acceleration of the non-inertial frame.
rules.check_logic: Verify if a pseudo force has been correctly added with the magnitude (-m * a_frame) and direction (opposite to the frame's acceleration).
common_errors: Omitting the pseudo force in calculations.
Using incorrect magnitude or sign for the pseudo force.
Confusing the pseudo force direction with the frame acceleration direction.

rules.title: Modify Newton's second law in non-inertial frames
rules.description: Newton's second law (F_net = m * a) must be modified in a non-inertial reference frame by including the pseudo force. The equation becomes: F_net + F_pseudo = m * a_observed.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the pseudo force is included in the net force equation, and the observed acceleration is used in calculations.
common_errors: Using the inertial acceleration instead of the observed acceleration.
Failing to add the pseudo force term in the net force equation.

rules.title: Ensure correct sign convention for pseudo force
rules.description: The pseudo force always acts opposite to the acceleration of the non-inertial reference frame. This sign convention must be adhered to for correct results.
rules.check_logic: Check if the pseudo force direction is opposite to the acceleration of the reference frame.
common_errors: Assigning the pseudo force in the same direction as the reference frame's acceleration.
Inconsistent application of sign conventions in calculations.

rules.title: Use consistent coordinate system in non-inertial frames
rules.description: When solving problems in non-inertial frames, the chosen coordinate system (e.g., Cartesian or polar) must remain consistent throughout the calculation, and the pseudo force must be expressed in the same system.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that all forces, accelerations, and pseudo forces are resolved consistently within the chosen coordinate system.
common_errors: Switching between coordinate systems mid-calculation without transformation.
Failing to resolve pseudo force components into the chosen coordinate system.

rules.title: Account for geometric constraints in non-inertial frames
rules.description: In problems involving non-inertial frames, any geometric constraints (e.g., objects on inclined planes, pendulum motion) must also include the effects of pseudo forces.
rules.check_logic: Verify that pseudo forces are included when analyzing forces and accelerations along constrained paths.
common_errors: Ignoring pseudo forces when applying geometric constraints.
Incorrect resolution of pseudo forces along the constrained directions.

rules.title: Include Coriolis force in rotating reference frames
rules.description: In rotating reference frames, the Coriolis force must be included. It is given by F_coriolis = -2m(ω × v), where ω is the angular velocity of the frame and v is the velocity of the object relative to the rotating frame.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the Coriolis force is included with the correct magnitude and direction using the cross product formula.
common_errors: Forgetting to include the Coriolis force in rotating frames.
Using incorrect cross product order for ω and v.
Incorrectly calculating the magnitude or direction of the Coriolis force.

rules.title: Include centrifugal force in rotating reference frames
rules.description: In a rotating reference frame, the centrifugal force must be included. It is given by F_centrifugal = -mω²r, where r is the radial distance of the object from the axis of rotation.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the centrifugal force is included with the correct magnitude and direction (outward from the axis of rotation).
common_errors: Omitting the centrifugal force in rotating frames.
Using the wrong direction for the centrifugal force (should be radially outward).
Incorrectly calculating the radial distance or angular velocity.

rules.title: Ensure dimensional consistency in pseudo force equations
rules.description: In equations involving pseudo forces, ensure that all terms have consistent dimensions. For example, pseudo force should have units of force (e.g., Newtons in SI).
rules.check_logic: Check that the dimensions of all terms in the pseudo force equation are consistent (e.g., mass × acceleration results in force).
common_errors: Using incorrect units for mass or acceleration in pseudo force calculations.
Adding terms with inconsistent dimensions (e.g., mixing force and acceleration).

rules.title: Verify Pressure-Varying with Depth Formula
rules.description: The pressure in a fluid increases linearly with depth according to the equation P = P0 + ρgh, where P is pressure at depth, P0 is atmospheric pressure, ρ is fluid density, g is gravitational acceleration, and h is the depth below the fluid surface.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the equation P = P0 + ρgh is applied for homogenous, incompressible fluids at equilibrium. Verify that h is measured as depth below the fluid surface and that ρ and g are consistent with the fluid and environment.
common_errors: Multiplying atmospheric pressure instead of adding it
Using incorrect values for density or gravitational acceleration
Misinterpreting h as height above fluid surface instead of depth

rules.title: Evaluate Buoyant Force Using Archimedes' Principle
rules.description: According to Archimedes' principle, the buoyant force acting on an object submerged in a fluid is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.
rules.check_logic: Confirm buoyant force calculation: F_buoyant = ρfluid * V_immersed * g. Ensure that V_immersed corresponds to the submerged volume of the object and that ρfluid is the density of the surrounding fluid.
common_errors: Calculating buoyant force using the object's total volume instead of immersed volume
Incorrect sign for buoyant force direction
Ignoring buoyant force application when object floats at constant depth

rules.title: Check Pressure at Fluid Surface
rules.description: In fluid statics, the pressure at the surface of a fluid is equal to the atmospheric pressure unless additional forces are applied (e.g., surface tension effects).
rules.check_logic: Ensure surface pressure is equal to atmospheric pressure unless surface tension or external forces are explicitly considered. Verify that the problem context justifies any deviations.
common_errors: Confusing surface pressure with pressure at a depth
Neglecting significant surface tension effects in small scales

rules.title: Correct Usage of Coordinate Systems in Fluid Statics
rules.description: Typically, in fluid statics problems, a coordinate system is established with 'upward' as positive z-axis. This affects the interpretation of forces and pressure gradients.
rules.check_logic: Verify the correct orientation of coordinate systems and ensure that pressure increases in the downward direction with depth. Confirm that all forces and gradients are consistent with the chosen coordinate system.
common_errors: Mixing up sign conventions for pressure gradients
Defining inconsistent coordinate systems, leading to calculation errors

rules.title: Verify Assumption of Incompressibility
rules.description: The equations governing fluid statics assume incompressible fluid dynamics, meaning the fluid density does not change with pressure or depth under normal static conditions.
rules.check_logic: Check that incompressibility is valid for the fluid in question (e.g., water) and not assumed for compressible fluids like gases. For compressible fluids, verify that density variations are accounted for.
common_errors: Applying fluid static principles to compressible fluids without adjusting density
Misapplying incompressibility assumption in variable density scenarios

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in Fluid Statics
rules.description: All equations in fluid statics must obey dimensional consistency, ensuring calculations of pressure and force yield units consistent with pascal (Pa) and newton (N) respectively.
rules.check_logic: Verify units in pressure calculations: [Pa] = [kg/m^3][m/s^2][m] = [N/m^2]. Ensure that all unit conversions are correctly applied, particularly for density and gravitational acceleration.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for density, such as grams instead of kilograms
Inconsistent unit conversion leading to erroneous pressure/force values

rules.title: Check Conditions for Floating Object Equilibrium
rules.description: For an object floating in equilibrium on a fluid surface, the buoyant force equals the gravitational force acting on the object.
rules.check_logic: Ensure equilibrium condition: F_buoyant = F_gravity. Verify that the object's weight is balanced by the buoyant force and account for partial immersion effects for non-uniform objects.
common_errors: Ignoring partial immersion effects for non-uniform objects
Miscalculating buoyant force due to incorrect fluid density

rules.title: Account for Surface Tension Effects in Small-Scale Fluid Statics
rules.description: In small-scale fluid systems, surface tension can significantly affect pressure and force calculations, particularly at interfaces between fluids or between a fluid and a solid.
rules.check_logic: Verify that surface tension effects are included when dealing with small-scale systems or interfaces. Ensure that the Young-Laplace equation is applied where appropriate: ΔP = 2γ/R, where γ is surface tension and R is the radius of curvature.
common_errors: Neglecting surface tension effects in small-scale systems
Incorrect application of the Young-Laplace equation

rules.title: Verify Continuity Equation Application
rules.description: The continuity equation (A1 * v1 = A2 * v2) ensures mass conservation in an incompressible fluid. It applies when the fluid is incompressible and there is no leakage in the system.
rules.check_logic: Check whether flow rates (A*v) at different cross-sectional areas are equal for an incompressible fluid. Ensure that the fluid density remains constant and there are no leaks or additional sources/sinks in the system.
common_errors: Ignoring changes in cross-sectional area when calculating velocity changes.
Applying the continuity equation to a compressible fluid without adjustments.
Using inconsistent units for area and velocity.

rules.title: Check Validity of Bernoulli's Equation
rules.description: Bernoulli's equation (P + 0.5*rho*v^2 + rho*g*h = constant) applies to inviscid, incompressible fluid flow along a streamline. Ensure the fluid is steady, non-viscous, and incompressible for valid application.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the system satisfies the conditions: steady flow, incompressible fluid, inviscid (negligible viscosity), and application along a single streamline. Confirm that the flow is laminar and not turbulent.
common_errors: Applying Bernoulli's equation to turbulent flow.
Ignoring viscosity effects when they are significant.
Using Bernoulli's equation across different streamlines.

rules.title: Verify Sign Conventions in Bernoulli's Terms
rules.description: The pressure (P), kinetic energy per unit volume (0.5*rho*v^2), and potential energy per unit volume (rho*g*h) terms in Bernoulli's equation must be properly signed based on the chosen coordinate system.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that gravitational potential energy (rho*g*h) has a consistent sign based on the chosen vertical axis direction (positive for increasing height). Confirm that all terms are aligned with the chosen reference frame.
common_errors: Using inconsistent signs for potential energy when height decreases.
Forgetting to account for negative pressure gradients in flow direction.

rules.title: Ensure Cross-sectional Area Consistency
rules.description: In the continuity equation, A1 * v1 = A2 * v2, the cross-sectional area (A) must be geometrically accurate and consistent with the shape of the flow passage.
rules.check_logic: Check whether the cross-sectional area is computed correctly for given geometric shapes (e.g., circular, rectangular, etc.). Verify that the correct formula is used for the specific geometry and that dimensions (e.g., radius vs. diameter) are not mixed.
common_errors: Using incorrect formulas for cross-sectional area (e.g., not using πr^2 for circular pipes).
Ignoring changes in area due to pipe expansion or contraction.
Mixing radius and diameter when calculating area.

rules.title: Verify Dimensional Consistency in Fluid Dynamics Equations
rules.description: Ensure that all terms in the continuity equation and Bernoulli's equation have consistent units throughout calculations.
rules.check_logic: Check whether units of pressure, velocity, density, and gravitational potential energy are consistent and compatible across terms. Ensure that unit conversions are applied where necessary.
common_errors: Mixing units of pressure (e.g., Pascals vs. atm).
Using inconsistent units for velocity (e.g., m/s vs. cm/s).
Forgetting to convert density to proper units (e.g., kg/m³).

rules.title: Check Conservation of Energy in Bernoulli's Equation
rules.description: Bernoulli's equation represents conservation of energy per unit volume along a streamline. Ensure that the sum of pressure, kinetic, and potential energy terms remains constant along a streamline.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the sum of P + 0.5*rho*v^2 + rho*g*h is equal at two points on the same streamline. Confirm that all terms are calculated correctly and that no energy losses (e.g., due to friction) are ignored if the system is not ideal.
common_errors: Neglecting one or more energy terms in the equation.
Failing to account for changes in velocity or height properly.
Incorrectly calculating one of the terms (e.g., 0.5*rho*v^2).

rules.title: Verify Boundary Conditions at Interfaces
rules.description: At interfaces or boundaries (e.g., pipe exits, reservoirs), ensure that appropriate boundary conditions (e.g., pressure = atmospheric pressure) are applied.
rules.check_logic: Check whether boundary conditions like atmospheric pressure or zero velocity at a stagnant point are correctly applied. Ensure that the no-slip condition is considered where applicable and that discontinuities are justified.
common_errors: Failing to set pressure to atmospheric pressure at open surfaces.
Ignoring no-slip conditions (velocity = 0 at stationary boundaries) where applicable.
Incorrectly assuming velocity or pressure continuity at boundaries where discontinuities occur.

rules.title: Ensure Correct Identification of Streamlines
rules.description: Bernoulli's equation applies only along a single streamline. Ensure that calculations are restricted to a single streamline and do not mix properties from different streamlines.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that all points considered in Bernoulli's equation lie on the same streamline. Verify that the streamline is clearly defined and that properties are not averaged across multiple streamlines.
common_errors: Applying Bernoulli's equation between points that are not on the same streamline.
Assuming uniform pressure or velocity across different streamlines without justification.

rules.title: Adjust for Compressible Fluids if Necessary
rules.description: For compressible fluids, the continuity equation and Bernoulli's equation require modifications to account for density variations.
rules.check_logic: Verify whether the fluid is compressible. If so, ensure that density variations are included in the continuity equation and Bernoulli's equation. Use the appropriate compressible flow equations if needed.
common_errors: Applying incompressible fluid equations to compressible fluids without adjustments.
Ignoring density variations in high-speed flows (e.g., near Mach 1).
Using incorrect compressible flow equations.

rules.title: Verify Angular Frequency and Linear Frequency Relationship
rules.description: For Simple Harmonic Motion, angular frequency ω is related to linear frequency f by ω = 2πf. This relationship is fundamental for oscillatory systems.
rules.check_logic: Ensure ω = 2πf is used correctly in calculations relating angular frequency and linear frequency, and verify unit consistency (e.g., radians per second for ω and hertz for f).
common_errors: Incorrect conversion factor between ω and f
Using linear frequency instead of angular frequency in equations

rules.title: Check Energy Conservation in SHM Systems
rules.description: In ideal Simple Harmonic Motion, mechanical energy is conserved. The sum of kinetic and potential energy in the system remains constant.
rules.check_logic: Verify if E_total = E_kinetic + E_potential remains constant over time, and ensure proper expressions for kinetic energy (1/2 mv²) and potential energy (1/2 kx²) are used.
common_errors: Ignoring potential energy contributions near maximum displacement
Forgetting kinetic energy at equilibrium position
Incorrect expressions for energy terms

rules.title: Validate Position and Velocity Equations for Spring-Mass Systems
rules.description: Position x(t) and velocity v(t) of a mass on a spring are given by x(t) = A cos(ωt + φ) and v(t) = -Aω sin(ωt + φ), where A is amplitude and φ is the phase constant.
rules.check_logic: Verify that position and velocity equations are correctly applied with proper amplitude, angular frequency, and phase constants. Ensure units are consistent and trigonometric functions are correctly evaluated.
common_errors: Incorrect sign for velocity expression
Misidentifying amplitude or missing phase shift
Using incorrect angular frequency in equations

rules.title: Ensure Correct Sign Convention for Forces and Displacements
rules.description: In SHM, the restoring force is typically considered negative in direction opposite to displacement (F = -kx for spring systems).
rules.check_logic: Check that restoring forces are consistently negative when displacements are positive, and verify that Hooke's Law is applied correctly.
common_errors: Misinterpretation of force directions
Incorrect sign usage when applying Hooke's Law
Confusion between restoring force and applied force

rules.title: Verify Validity Conditions for SHM Applicability
rules.description: SHM applies in systems where net restoring forces are proportional to displacement and damping forces are negligible.
rules.check_logic: Ensure system criteria such as linear restoring force proportionality (e.g., Hooke's Law) and negligible damping are met. Verify that the system is not influenced by external forces or significant non-linearities.
common_errors: Applying SHM principles in non-linear force systems
Ignoring damping effects which invalidate ideal SHM assumption
Overlooking external forces affecting the system

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in SHM Equations
rules.description: All equations in SHM should be dimensionally consistent. Units must balance, specifically for ω, x(t), and v(t).
rules.check_logic: Check if each term in equations maintains consistent dimensions, particularly length [L], time [T], and mass [M]. Ensure angular frequency is in radians per second, position in meters, and velocity in meters per second.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for angular frequency
Mixing units inconsistently in calculations
Overlooking dimensional consistency in derived equations

rules.title: Validate Period-Time Relation in Oscillations
rules.description: The period T of a mass-spring oscillator is calculated as T = 2π√(m/k). This applies under ideal conditions of simple harmonic oscillators.
rules.check_logic: Verify whether the calculated period matches T = 2π√(m/k) using the correct formula, proper unit conversion, and accurate values for mass and spring constant.
common_errors: Incorrect physical constant usage
Using period formulas outside applicable contexts
Neglecting unit consistency in mass or spring constant

rules.title: Check for Phase Shift Due to Damping in Real Oscillators
rules.description: Real-world oscillators may exhibit phase shifts due to damping forces. Evaluate phase changes in the presence of damping.
rules.check_logic: Determine if phase shifts have been correctly factored into calculations where damping is present. Verify that the damping coefficient and its effect on the phase constant are accurately considered.
common_errors: Ignoring phase shift in damped systems
Incorrect adjustment of phase constant in damped scenarios
Overlooking the relationship between damping and angular frequency

rules.title: Verify Initial Conditions for SHM Systems
rules.description: Initial conditions, such as initial displacement and velocity, determine the phase constant and amplitude in SHM equations.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that initial conditions are correctly applied to determine the phase constant φ and amplitude A. Verify that x(0) and v(0) are consistent with the given equations.
common_errors: Incorrectly calculating phase constant from initial conditions
Ignoring initial velocity or displacement in calculations
Using inconsistent initial conditions in equations

rules.title: Verify the resonance condition for driving frequency
rules.description: The resonance condition occurs when the driving frequency matches the natural frequency of the system. For a harmonic oscillator, this is given by ω_d = ω_0, where ω_d is the driving frequency, and ω_0 = sqrt(k/m) is the natural frequency.
rules.check_logic: Check if the driving frequency (ω_d) equals the natural frequency (ω_0 = sqrt(k/m)).
common_errors: Using an incorrect expression for the natural frequency, e.g., forgetting the square root.
Confusing angular frequency (ω) with linear frequency (f) by not using ω = 2πf.
Not accounting for the mass (m) or spring constant (k) in ω_0.

rules.title: Verify the equation of motion for damped oscillations
rules.description: The equation of motion for damped oscillations is m(d²x/dt²) + b(dx/dt) + kx = 0, where b is the damping coefficient.
rules.check_logic: Verify the presence and correct expression of the inertial force (m(d²x/dt²)), damping force (b(dx/dt)), and restoring force (kx).
common_errors: Omitting the damping term (b(dx/dt)).
Using incorrect sign conventions (e.g., wrong signs for forces).
Failing to include the mass (m) in the inertial term.

rules.title: Verify boundary and initial conditions for oscillations
rules.description: Ensure the initial displacement and velocity are correctly applied to the solution of the damped or driven oscillation equation.
rules.check_logic: Check if initial conditions (e.g., x(0) and dx/dt|_(t=0)) are correctly substituted into the differential equation solution.
common_errors: Using incorrect or arbitrary initial conditions.
Misinterpreting the initial velocity as initial displacement.
Failing to consistently apply initial conditions across all terms.

rules.title: Verify energy dissipation in damped oscillations
rules.description: In damped oscillations, total mechanical energy decreases over time due to the damping force. The energy at any time is E(t) = (1/2)m(dx/dt)² + (1/2)kx², decreasing monotonically.
rules.check_logic: Ensure E(t) is correctly computed and decreases over time for a damped oscillator.
common_errors: Forgetting to include kinetic or potential energy terms in E(t).
Not accounting for the work done by the damping force.
Using an incorrect sign for energy dissipation.

rules.title: Verify consistent sign conventions for forces and displacements
rules.description: In oscillatory motion, restoring forces oppose displacement and damping forces oppose velocity.
rules.check_logic: Ensure restoring force is -kx and damping force is -b(dx/dt), using negative signs to indicate opposition.
common_errors: Assigning a positive sign to the restoring force.
Reversing the direction of the damping force.
Inconsistent sign conventions across terms in the equation.

rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency of equations
rules.description: Confirm that all terms in the equation have dimensions of force (ML/T²). Check m(d²x/dt²), b(dx/dt), and kx.
rules.check_logic: Verify that each term has dimensions of force. Mass should be M, damping coefficient should be ML/T, and spring constant should be ML/T².
common_errors: Using incorrect units for mass, damping coefficient, or spring constant.
Failing to ensure consistency between angular frequency and linear frequency.
Neglecting the time squared factor in acceleration terms.

rules.title: Verify validity conditions for resonance and damping equations
rules.description: Ensure assumptions like small oscillations, linear restoring forces, and negligible perturbations hold.
rules.check_logic: Check if oscillations are small, restoring force follows Hooke's Law, and nonlinear effects are minimal.
common_errors: Applying equations to large oscillations where linearity fails.
Neglecting external non-conservative forces affecting the system.
Assuming Hooke's Law holds for non-linear springs.

rules.title: Verify calculation of the quality factor (Q)
rules.description: The quality factor (Q) quantifies resonance sharpness, given by Q = ω_0/(2β), where β = b/(2m).
rules.check_logic: Calculate Q using Q = ω_0/(2β), ensuring β = b/(2m).
common_errors: Using an incorrect formula for damping coefficient β.
Confusing damping constant b with coefficient per unit mass.
Failing to relate Q to resonance sharpness.

rules.title: Verify equation of motion consistency for coupled systems
rules.description: Ensure that the equations of motion for each oscillator in the coupled system are correctly derived using Newton’s second law or the Lagrangian method. The coupling force should be properly included.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the second-order differential equations correctly include restoring forces, coupling forces, and damping (if specified). Ensure that the spring constants, masses, and displacements match the problem setup and that the coupling force is derived based on relative displacements.
common_errors: Omitting the coupling force in the equations of motion.
Incorrect sign for the restoring force or coupling terms.
Forgetting to account for the displacement of both masses in the coupling term.

rules.title: Check validity of superposition principle
rules.description: In normal modes, displacements are assumed to be linear combinations of eigenfunctions. This principle applies only when the system is linear and the coupling forces follow Hooke's Law.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the problem setup specifies linear restoring forces and that no nonlinear terms (e.g., cubic or higher-order terms) are introduced in the equations of motion. Verify that the coupling forces are proportional to displacement.
common_errors: Using superposition principle in a nonlinear system.
Including cubic or higher-order terms in the coupling or restoring forces, which invalidates normal mode analysis.

rules.title: Verify normal mode frequencies are correctly determined
rules.description: The frequencies of the normal modes are the eigenvalues of the system matrix derived from the equations of motion. These must be calculated correctly using a determinant or matrix diagonalization technique.
rules.check_logic: Check that the determinant of the matrix (Mω² - K) is set to zero for eigenvalue calculation. Ensure that the square root of eigenvalues is taken to find angular frequencies and that the units of mass and spring constants are consistent.
common_errors: Forgetting to set the determinant to zero.
Incorrectly calculating the eigenvalues of the system matrix.
Using incorrect units or dimensions for mass or spring constants, leading to wrong frequency values.

rules.title: Check adherence to sign conventions for displacement and force directions
rules.description: Ensure that all displacements, forces, and coupling terms follow a consistent sign convention. For example, a displacement to the right should correspond to a positive restoring force to the left.
rules.check_logic: Verify that force terms in the equations of motion have the correct signs based on the chosen coordinate system and direction of displacement. Ensure consistency across all oscillators in the system.
common_errors: Using inconsistent sign conventions for different oscillators.
Forgetting to reverse the sign of the force when the displacement is in the opposite direction.
Ignoring the effect of the coupling spring, leading to mismatched signs in the coupling term.

rules.title: Verify proper application of initial conditions
rules.description: Initial conditions (initial displacements and velocities) should be applied consistently to solve for the time-dependent motion of the system. These conditions determine the amplitudes and phases of the modes.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the initial conditions are substituted into the general solution correctly to solve for constants of integration. Verify that the initial conditions are applied to all oscillators in the system.
common_errors: Forgetting to apply initial conditions to both oscillators in a coupled system.
Incorrect substitution of initial displacement or velocity values into the general solution.
Mistaking the initial phase for initial velocity or vice versa.

rules.title: Check geometric constraints in coupled oscillator systems
rules.description: Some systems have geometric constraints (e.g., fixed total length of a string or rod). These constraints must be incorporated into the equations of motion.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the sum of displacements satisfies the geometric constraint, if specified (e.g., x1 + x2 = constant for a fixed-length system). Ensure that the constraint is used to reduce the number of independent variables in the system.
common_errors: Ignoring the geometric constraint altogether.
Misinterpreting the constraint equation, leading to incorrect coupling terms.
Forgetting to reduce the number of independent variables based on the constraint.

rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of all terms
rules.description: Ensure that all terms in the equations of motion and derived quantities (frequencies, displacements) have consistent dimensions. For example, frequencies must have dimensions of [T^-1].
rules.check_logic: Verify unit consistency in each term of the equations of motion. Check that frequencies are derived with proper units based on the spring constant and mass. Ensure that all derived quantities maintain dimensional consistency.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for spring constants (e.g., N/m vs. N/mm).
Forgetting to convert mass or displacement units, leading to incorrect frequency calculations.
Failing to ensure all terms in the equation of motion are dimensionally consistent.

rules.title: Verify mode orthogonality
rules.description: In coupled oscillation systems, the eigenvectors (modes) should be orthogonal with respect to the mass matrix. This property arises from the symmetry of the system.
rules.check_logic: Check that the dot product of eigenvectors (using the mass matrix as a weighting factor) is zero for distinct modes. Ensure that the system matrix is symmetric or Hermitian, as required for orthogonality.
common_errors: Incorrectly calculating the eigenvectors, leading to loss of orthogonality.
Omitting the mass matrix in the orthogonality check.
Assuming orthogonality in a non-symmetric or non-Hermitian system, where it may not hold.

rules.title: Verify energy consistency in normal modes
rules.description: The total energy of the system should be conserved in the absence of damping. The energy should be correctly distributed among kinetic and potential components for each mode.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the total energy (sum of kinetic and potential energy) remains constant over time for undamped systems. Verify that the energy expressions for each mode are consistent with the displacements and velocities.
common_errors: Forgetting to include both kinetic and potential energy terms.
Incorrectly calculating the potential energy due to coupling forces.
Failing to verify energy conservation in undamped systems.

rules.title: Verify Hooke's Law Application
rules.description: Hooke's Law states that the restoring force (F) is proportional to the displacement (x) within the elastic limit of the material, given by F = -kx, where k is the spring constant. This applies only when the material is within its elastic limit.
rules.check_logic: Verify that F = -kx is applied correctly, ensuring the material deformation is within the elastic limit. Confirm that the spring constant (k) is appropriate for the material and that the negative sign is used to indicate the restoring direction.
common_errors: Using Hooke's Law beyond the elastic limit.
Forgetting the negative sign in F = -kx indicating the restoring direction.
Incorrect or mismatched units for k, x, and F.

rules.title: Verify Stress and Strain Calculations
rules.description: Stress is the force per unit area (σ = F/A), and strain is the relative deformation (ε = ΔL/L). These quantities are related through the elastic modulus (E) as σ = Eε.
rules.check_logic: Ensure stress and strain are calculated using the correct definitions. Verify that the relationship σ = Eε holds for the given material and that the elastic modulus used matches the material's properties.
common_errors: Confusing stress and strain definitions.
Incorrectly calculating cross-sectional area in stress formula.
Using the wrong elastic modulus for the material.

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional and Unit Consistency
rules.description: The units of force, displacement, spring constant, stress, strain, and elastic modulus must be consistent. For example, [k] = N/m, [σ] = N/m², [ε] is dimensionless, and [E] = N/m².
rules.check_logic: Verify that all quantities have consistent units in equations, particularly when converting between systems (e.g., SI to CGS). Ensure that strain is treated as a dimensionless ratio.
common_errors: Using strain with units instead of a dimensionless ratio.
Mixing up units of stress and elastic modulus.
Failing to convert units of force or displacement when required.

rules.title: Check for Geometric Constraints in Deformation
rules.description: Ensure that the deformation (strain) does not exceed the elastic limit or lead to unrealistic geometrical results. For example, strain should remain small (ε << 1) for linear elasticity to be valid.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the strain calculated is within reasonable bounds for the material, typically less than a few percent for most solids. Confirm that the deformation does not imply unrealistic geometry or exceed the elastic limit.
common_errors: Calculating strain values that imply large deformations beyond the elastic limit.
Ignoring the geometric implications of length changes in strain calculations.

rules.title: Verify Hooke's Law Validity Conditions
rules.description: Hooke's Law applies only within the elastic limit of a material. Beyond this limit, plastic deformation occurs, and the relationship between stress and strain is no longer linear.
rules.check_logic: Check that the stress or strain does not exceed the yield point of the material. Verify that the linear relationship σ = Eε holds only within the elastic region and that the material is not undergoing plastic deformation.
common_errors: Applying Hooke's Law to materials undergoing plastic deformation.
Using the elastic modulus (E) for non-linear regimes.

rules.title: Verify Elastic Potential Energy Calculation
rules.description: The elastic potential energy stored in a spring is given by U = 1/2 kx², where x is the displacement from the equilibrium position.
rules.check_logic: Ensure U = 1/2 kx² is correctly used, with consistent units (energy in joules). Confirm that the displacement used is the extension or compression from equilibrium, not the total length.
common_errors: Neglecting the 1/2 factor in the energy formula.
Using the wrong value for displacement (e.g., total length instead of extension).
Mismatched units for k and x leading to incorrect energy units.

rules.title: Check Sign Conventions for Forces and Displacement
rules.description: The sign convention for forces and displacements in Hooke's Law is critical. The restoring force opposes displacement, leading to a negative sign in F = -kx.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the direction of the restoring force is opposite to the direction of displacement and that the negative sign is correctly applied in F = -kx.
common_errors: Omitting the negative sign in Hooke's Law.
Incorrectly assigning force direction relative to displacement.

rules.title: Validate Material Properties Consistency
rules.description: Ensure the correct material constants (spring constant k, elastic modulus E, yield strength, etc.) are used and are consistent with the given material.
rules.check_logic: Cross-check the values of material constants with standard values provided or the context of the problem. Ensure that external factors like temperature or pressure are considered if they affect material properties.
common_errors: Using incorrect values for spring constants or modulus of elasticity.
Failing to account for temperature or other conditions affecting material properties.

rules.title: Verify Behavior Under Dynamic Loading
rules.description: Hooke's Law and elasticity principles assume static or quasi-static conditions. Under dynamic loading, additional factors like damping and resonance may need to be considered.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the problem context involves static or quasi-static conditions. If dynamic loading is present, verify that appropriate corrections (e.g., damping coefficients) are applied.
common_errors: Applying static elasticity principles to dynamic scenarios without considering additional effects.
Ignoring resonance or damping in dynamic systems.

topics.name: Center of Mass and Motion of Extended Bodies

rules.title: Verify the definition of center of mass
rules.description: The center of mass for a system of particles is calculated using the weighted average of the positions of all particles, where the weights are their respective masses. For a continuous object, integration must be used.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the formula \( \vec{R}_{com} = \frac{\sum m_i \vec{r}_i}{\sum m_i} \) or \( \vec{R}_{com} = \frac{\int \vec{r} \, dm}{\int dm} \) is correctly applied. Verify the correct placement of the center of mass within the object's boundaries.
common_errors: Forgetting to divide by the total mass.
Using incorrect limits or integrand when integrating for continuous systems.
Mixing up vector and scalar quantities.

rules.title: Check application of Newton's Second Law to center of mass motion
rules.description: The motion of the center of mass of a system is governed by Newton's Second Law: the net external force acting on the system equals the total mass of the system times the acceleration of the center of mass.
rules.check_logic: Verify that \( \sum \vec{F}_{ext} = M \vec{a}_{com} \) is applied, where \( M \) is the total mass of the system. Ensure internal forces are ignored for the net external force calculation.
common_errors: Ignoring internal forces, which do not affect the motion of the center of mass.
Using incorrect mass or acceleration values.

rules.title: Ensure coordinate system consistency for center of mass calculations
rules.description: The center of mass position must be calculated using a consistent coordinate system. If the coordinate system is shifted or rotated, the positions of the particles must be transformed accordingly.
rules.check_logic: Check that all position vectors \( \vec{r}_i \) are calculated in the same coordinate system. Verify consistency of transformation equations if the coordinate system is altered.
common_errors: Mixing coordinates from different reference frames.
Forgetting to transform vectors when switching coordinate systems.

rules.title: Validate center of mass position in rigid bodies with symmetry
rules.description: For rigid bodies with symmetry, the center of mass lies along the axis or plane of symmetry. For example, in a uniform circular disk, it is at the geometric center.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the center of mass is correctly identified at symmetry points for symmetric rigid bodies. Confirm that symmetry is correctly interpreted in diverse situations.
common_errors: Incorrectly placing the center of mass outside the symmetric axis/plane.
Failing to recognize symmetry in the given problem.

rules.title: Verify angular momentum about the center of mass
rules.description: For a system of particles, the total angular momentum about the center of mass is the sum of the angular momentum of the center of mass motion and the angular momentum of motion relative to the center of mass.
rules.check_logic: Ensure \( \vec{L} = \vec{R}_{com} \times M \vec{v}_{com} + \sum \vec{r}'_i \times m_i \vec{v}'_i \) is correctly computed, where \( \vec{r}'_i \) and \( \vec{v}'_i \) are positions and velocities relative to the center of mass. Validate each vector product term.
common_errors: Omitting the relative angular momentum term.
Using incorrect relative positions or velocities.

rules.title: Check moment of inertia calculation about the center of mass
rules.description: The moment of inertia of a body about its center of mass is calculated using \( I_{com} = \int r'^2 dm \), where \( r' \) is the perpendicular distance from the center of mass to the element of mass.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the integral \( \int r'^2 dm \) or equivalent summation for discrete systems is correctly set up relative to the center of mass. Cross-verify calculations involving any similar axis transformations.
common_errors: Using distances not measured from the center of mass.
Forgetting to square the distance \( r' \).
Incorrectly applying the parallel axis theorem.

rules.title: Verify application of the parallel axis theorem
rules.description: When calculating the moment of inertia about an axis other than the center of mass, the parallel axis theorem must be used: \( I = I_{com} + Md^2 \), where \( d \) is the distance between the two axes.
rules.check_logic: Ensure \( I \) is calculated correctly using \( I_{com} \) and \( Md^2 \). Confirm \( d \) is the correct perpendicular distance and the theorem applicability aligns with the problem setup.
common_errors: Forgetting to add \( Md^2 \) term.
Using incorrect distance \( d \).
Applying the theorem in cases where the axis does not pass through the center of mass.

rules.title: Perform dimensional consistency checks for center of mass equations
rules.description: All terms in equations related to center of mass must have consistent dimensions. For example, the center of mass position must have dimensions of length, and forces must have dimensions of mass times acceleration.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the dimensions of all terms in the equations match those expected (e.g., \([L]\) for position, \([M][L]/[T]^2\) for force). Validate consistency across different unit systems if applicable.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for mass, length, or time.
Mixing scalar and vector quantities improperly.

rules.title: Verify Newton’s Second Law for the Center of Mass
rules.description: The total external force acting on a system of particles equals the mass of the system multiplied by the acceleration of its center of mass. This applies to systems where forces are clearly identified as internal or external.
rules.check_logic: Verify if F_ext = M*a_cm, where F_ext is the vector sum of all external forces, M is the total mass of the system, and a_cm is the acceleration of the center of mass.
common_errors: Forgetting to distinguish between internal and external forces.
Incorrect calculation of total mass (M) of the system.
Omitting acceleration components in vector form.

rules.title: Conservation of Linear Momentum
rules.description: If the net external force acting on a system of particles is zero, the total linear momentum of the system remains constant.
rules.check_logic: Verify if the vector sum of external forces is zero (F_ext = 0). If true, check whether the initial total momentum of the system equals the final total momentum.
common_errors: Neglecting to check for external forces.
Incorrect calculation of momentum (P = mv for each particle).
Not accounting for vector nature of momentum.

rules.title: Check Torque and Angular Momentum Relationship
rules.description: The rate of change of angular momentum of a system about a point is equal to the net external torque about that point.
rules.check_logic: Verify if dL/dt = τ_ext, where L is the angular momentum and τ_ext is the net external torque.
common_errors: Using incorrect pivot point for calculation of torque.
Confusing internal and external torques.
Ignoring rotational inertia in angular momentum calculations.

rules.title: Confirm Validity of the Center of Mass Motion Equation
rules.description: The center of mass motion equation assumes that the system is not relativistic and that the particles within the system do not experience significant relativistic effects.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the velocities involved are much less than the speed of light (v << c) and that there is no significant mass variation due to relativistic effects.
common_errors: Applying the center of mass motion equation to a relativistic system.
Neglecting mass variation in cases where particles are added or lost.

rules.title: Ensure Proper Use of Sign Conventions and Coordinate Systems
rules.description: The choice of coordinate system and sign conventions must be consistent throughout the analysis of a system of particles.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all forces, displacements, velocities, and accelerations are resolved into the same coordinate system, and that consistent signs are assigned based on the chosen convention.
common_errors: Mixing coordinate systems without clear transformation.
Inconsistent sign conventions for vector components.
Incorrect resolution of forces into components.

rules.title: Account for Constraints in the System
rules.description: Geometric and kinematic constraints (e.g., rigid body motion, inextensible strings, etc.) must be properly incorporated into the equations describing the system.
rules.check_logic: Verify if constraint equations are included (e.g., for rigid bodies, relative distances between particles remain constant) and check their impact on the system.
common_errors: Neglecting to include the constraint forces in the free-body diagram.
Incorrectly defining or solving constraint equations.
Overlooking constraints in motion due to rigid connections or links.

rules.title: Dimensional and Unit Consistency Check
rules.description: Ensure that all quantities in dynamic equations have consistent units and dimensions (e.g., force in Newtons, mass in kilograms, acceleration in m/s²).
rules.check_logic: Verify that equations balance dimensionally and that units are consistent across all terms.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units (e.g., mass in grams instead of kilograms).
Forgetting to convert velocities or accelerations into standard units before substitution.
Mismatched units in torque and angular momentum.

rules.title: Verify Conservation of Energy in the System
rules.description: If no non-conservative external forces (e.g., friction) do work, the total mechanical energy (kinetic + potential) of the system should remain constant.
rules.check_logic: Check if the work done by non-conservative forces is zero. If true, ensure that the initial and final mechanical energy are equal.
common_errors: Ignoring the work done by non-conservative forces like friction or air resistance.
Incorrectly calculating potential energy for systems with multiple particles.
Omitting rotational kinetic energy for systems involving rotation.

rules.title: Verify Coriolis force equation
rules.description: The Coriolis force is given by the vector equation F_c = -2m(ω × v), where ω is the angular velocity vector of the rotating frame, and v is the velocity of the object relative to the rotating frame. This force arises in rotating reference frames.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the Coriolis force is calculated using F_c = -2m(ω × v), where m is the object's mass, ω is the angular velocity vector, and v is the relative velocity vector. Confirm that the cross product is computed correctly.
common_errors: Forgetting the factor of 2 in the Coriolis force equation.
Incorrect vector cross product calculation.
Using the wrong direction for the angular velocity vector ω.
Neglecting the negative sign in the equation.

rules.title: Check sign convention in Coriolis force
rules.description: The direction of the Coriolis force is determined by the right-hand rule for the cross product of ω and v, with a negative sign applied. This ensures the force points in the correct direction relative to the rotation.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the direction of the Coriolis force is determined by F_c = -2m(ω × v) and follows the right-hand rule for the cross product. Confirm that the negative sign is applied to the result.
common_errors: Using the left-hand rule instead of the right-hand rule for the cross product.
Neglecting the negative sign, leading to an incorrect force direction.

rules.title: Verify coordinate system consistency
rules.description: The Coriolis force calculation requires a consistent coordinate system. Typically, a rotating frame's axes must be clearly defined, with the angular velocity vector ω aligned with the axis of rotation.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the coordinate system used is clearly defined and consistent, and that ω aligns with the axis of rotation as per the problem setup. Confirm that any transformations between coordinate systems are correctly applied.
common_errors: Not aligning the angular velocity vector ω with the rotation axis.
Switching between coordinate systems without proper transformation.

rules.title: Check geometric constraints for rotational motion
rules.description: The Coriolis force only applies to objects moving relative to the rotating frame. Objects at rest in the rotating frame (v = 0) do not experience this force.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the velocity vector v is non-zero relative to the rotating frame for the Coriolis force to exist. Confirm that the velocity is measured relative to the rotating frame and not an inertial frame.
common_errors: Applying the Coriolis force to objects at rest in the rotating frame.
Using the velocity relative to an inertial frame instead of the rotating frame.

rules.title: Verify validity conditions for Coriolis force
rules.description: The Coriolis force is only valid in non-inertial, rotating reference frames. If the problem is analyzed from an inertial frame, the Coriolis force should not be included.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the reference frame is explicitly stated to be rotating, and confirm that the Coriolis force is not applied in inertial frame analyses. Verify that the problem setup specifies the type of reference frame.
common_errors: Applying the Coriolis force in an inertial reference frame.
Failing to specify whether the reference frame is rotating or inertial.

rules.title: Validate dimensional consistency of Coriolis force
rules.description: The Coriolis force has the units of force (e.g., N in SI). It depends on mass (kg), angular velocity (rad/s), and velocity (m/s), hence the dimensional formula should be [M][L][T^-2].
rules.check_logic: Verify that the computed Coriolis force has consistent dimensions of force ([M][L][T^-2]). Ensure that the units of mass, angular velocity, and velocity are consistent.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for angular velocity ω or velocity v.
Incorrectly calculating the cross product, leading to incorrect dimensions.

rules.title: Account for Earth's rotation in Coriolis force
rules.description: For problems involving Earth's rotation, the angular velocity vector ω points along the Earth's axis of rotation, with magnitude ω = 2π / T (where T is the sidereal day).
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the angular velocity of Earth is correctly calculated and points in the correct direction (towards the North Pole in the northern hemisphere). Verify that the sidereal day is used for the calculation.
common_errors: Using the wrong value for Earth's angular velocity ω.
Pointing ω in the wrong direction (e.g., away from the North Pole).

rules.title: Consider latitude dependence of Coriolis force
rules.description: The Coriolis force depends on the latitude on Earth, as only the component of ω perpendicular to the surface contributes to the force. At the equator, the Coriolis force is zero.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the latitude angle is used to calculate the effective component of ω, and ensure that F_c is zero at the equator. Confirm that the sine of the latitude angle is used to determine the effective component.
common_errors: Ignoring the latitude dependence of the Coriolis force.
Applying the Coriolis force at the equator where it should be zero.

rules.title: Account for time variation in angular velocity
rules.description: If the angular velocity of the rotating frame varies with time, the Coriolis force calculation must account for this variation.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the angular velocity vector ω is treated as time-dependent if specified in the problem. Ensure that the time derivative of ω is considered if necessary.
common_errors: Assuming a constant angular velocity when it is time-dependent.
Neglecting the time derivative of ω in problems with variable rotation rates.

rules.title: Verify Coulomb's Law formula usage
rules.description: Ensure that the formula F = k * (|q1 * q2|) / r^2 is used correctly. This equation calculates the magnitude of the force between two point charges, where k is Coulomb's constant, q1 and q2 are the charges, and r is the distance between the charges.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the force is calculated using F = k * |q1 * q2| / r^2 and that all variables are correctly substituted. Ensure that the absolute value of the product of charges is used, the distance is squared, and the correct value of Coulomb's constant is applied.
common_errors: Forgetting to square the distance (r^2)
Using q1 * q2 instead of |q1 * q2|, thus missing the absolute value
Using an incorrect value for Coulomb's constant (k)

rules.title: Verify Electric Field formula usage
rules.description: Ensure that the electric field is calculated using E = F / q or E = k * |q| / r^2, where E is the electric field, F is the force experienced by a test charge q, and r is the distance from the source charge.
rules.check_logic: Check if the electric field magnitude is calculated using E = k * |q| / r^2 or derived from E = F / q. Verify that the absolute value of the charge is used, the distance is squared, and the correct relationships between force, charge, and field are applied.
common_errors: Forgetting to divide by q when using E = F / q
Not using the absolute value of the charge in the formula
Forgetting to square the distance in E = k * |q| / r^2

rules.title: Ensure correct sign conventions for forces and fields
rules.description: Verify that the direction of the electric force and field is consistent with the charges' nature: like charges repel, and opposite charges attract. Ensure vector directions are assigned correctly in the coordinate system.
rules.check_logic: Check if the electric field vector points away from positive charges and toward negative charges. Ensure the electric force aligns with the field for positive charges and opposes it for negative charges. Confirm that the directions are consistent with the problem's coordinate system.
common_errors: Incorrect force direction for repulsion/attraction
Electric field vector pointing toward positive charges instead of away
Forgetting to consider vector directions in calculations

rules.title: Verify consistency of coordinate system in vector representation
rules.description: Make sure all electric force and field vectors are expressed in a consistent coordinate system (Cartesian, spherical, etc.), with proper consideration of components and angles.
rules.check_logic: Verify that vector components (e.g., x, y, z) are consistent with the chosen coordinate system and that angles are measured correctly relative to the axes. Ensure that conversions between coordinate systems, if any, are performed accurately.
common_errors: Mixing coordinate systems (e.g., Cartesian with spherical)
Incorrect calculation of vector components
Using angles in degrees when radians are required or vice versa

rules.title: Ensure geometric constraints are satisfied
rules.description: Confirm that the distance r between charges is positive and matches the stated configuration. Verify that charges are treated as point charges unless specified otherwise.
rules.check_logic: Check if r > 0 and consistent with the given geometry. Ensure charges are sufficiently small to approximate as point charges if Coulomb's Law is applied. Verify that the physical arrangement of charges matches the problem's description.
common_errors: Using a zero or negative distance in calculations
Applying Coulomb's Law to extended charges without proper treatment
Incorrect interpretation of the charges' physical arrangement

rules.title: Verify validity conditions for Coulomb's Law application
rules.description: Ensure Coulomb's Law is applied only under the assumption of stationary point charges in a vacuum or sufficiently low-medium dielectric constant environment.
rules.check_logic: Check if charges are stationary and point-like, and that the medium is either vacuum or has a specified permittivity ε consistent with the problem. Ensure that magnetic effects are not ignored if charges are moving.
common_errors: Applying Coulomb's Law to moving charges without considering magnetic effects
Using Coulomb's Law in a medium without adjusting for permittivity
Using it for non-point charges without additional approximations

rules.title: Verify dimensional and unit consistency
rules.description: Ensure that all terms in the equations have consistent units and dimensions. For Coulomb's Law, force (F) must have units of Newtons (N), charge (q) in Coulombs (C), distance (r) in meters (m), and k in N·m²/C².
rules.check_logic: Check if the units of the calculated force or electric field match the expected result based on the input quantities. Verify that all input quantities are converted to SI units before substitution.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for distance (e.g., cm instead of m)
Forgetting to convert charge values from microcoulombs to coulombs
Incorrect unit for Coulomb's constant

rules.title: Verify application of superposition principle
rules.description: Ensure that the net electric field or force is calculated by vector addition of individual contributions from multiple charges, using E_net = ΣE_i or F_net = ΣF_i.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the contributions from all charges are calculated separately and summed as vectors, considering both magnitude and direction. Ensure that vector addition is performed correctly, including handling angles and components.
common_errors: Adding magnitudes instead of vectors when determining net field or force
Omitting contributions from one or more charges
Incorrect vector addition due to sign or angle errors

rules.title: Verify boundary conditions for electric fields
rules.description: Ensure that boundary conditions, such as the behavior of electric fields at the surface of conductors or at infinity, are correctly applied.
rules.check_logic: Check if the electric field inside a conductor is zero and that the field at the surface is perpendicular to the surface. Verify that the field approaches zero at infinity unless specified otherwise.
common_errors: Incorrect assumption about the electric field inside a conductor
Forgetting that the electric field is perpendicular to the surface of a conductor
Incorrect treatment of the field at infinity

rules.title: Verify Electric Potential Definition
rules.description: Electric potential at a point is the work done per unit charge in bringing a positive test charge from infinity to that point without acceleration. It is defined as V = W/q, where V is the potential, W is work done, and q is the charge.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the electric potential is calculated using V = W/q, where W is the work done and q is the charge, consistently applying the unit volt (V = J/C).
common_errors: Using incorrect formula for potential
Not accounting for work done by conservative electrostatic forces only

rules.title: Verify Electric Potential Energy Formula
rules.description: Electric potential energy (U) between two point charges is U = k * q1 * q2 / r, where k is Coulomb's constant, q1 and q2 are the charges, and r is the separation distance.
rules.check_logic: Ensure U is calculated using U = k * q1 * q2 / r correctly, verify unit consistency with joules (J), and confirm r is the correct distance.
common_errors: Incorrect distance 'r' usage
Confusing potential energy with electric potential

rules.title: Check Sign Convention in Electric Potential
rules.description: Electric potential and potential energy are positive when work is done against the electric field (e.g., bringing like charges together) and negative when work is done by the electric field.
rules.check_logic: Verify potential and potential energy signs correctly depending on system conditions; positive for repulsion in like charges and negative for attraction in unlike charges.
common_errors: Incorrectly assigned signs for potential and potential energy
Ignoring convention for direction of electric field forces

rules.title: Coordinate System Consistency
rules.description: Electric field vectors and calculations often use spherical or Cartesian coordinates. Consistency is crucial for calculating electric potential.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all potential and electric field calculations adhere to the chosen coordinate system and respect symmetry conditions.
common_errors: Mixing spherical and Cartesian coordinate systems
Ignoring radial symmetry in spherical coordinates

rules.title: Check Conditions for Electrostatic Equations
rules.description: Electrostatic equations apply in the absence of magnetic fields and assume charges are stationary or moving very slowly.
rules.check_logic: Confirm all scenarios involve stationary charges or those moving sufficiently slowly; ensure no significant time-variant magnetic fields are present.
common_errors: Using electrostatic equations for high-velocity charge systems
Ignoring the influence of time-changing magnetic fields

rules.title: Verify Geometric Constraints in Charge Configurations
rules.description: Charge distributions affect electric field and potential calculations; symmetry must be considered, such as with line charges or planes of charge.
rules.check_logic: Ensure symmetry is considered for charge distributions, correctly affecting field line orientation and potential differences.
common_errors: Neglecting symmetry in field and potential calculations
Incorrectly assuming uniform field without symmetry basis

rules.title: Dimensional and Unit Consistency
rules.description: Ensure physical quantities have correct dimensions: electric potential (V) in volts (J/C) and potential energy (U) in joules (J).
rules.check_logic: Verify all calculations respect dimensional consistency and correct unit conversions, maintaining J/C for electric potential and J for potential energy.
common_errors: Incorrect unit conversion between systems
Using inconsistent dimensions in equations

rules.title: Verify Reference Point in Electric Potential Calculations
rules.description: The reference point for electric potential is often taken at infinity, but it should be clearly defined for each specific problem or configuration.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the reference point for potential calculations is explicitly stated and correctly used in the computations.
common_errors: Omitting reference point definition
Assuming incorrect reference points without specification

rules.title: Verify application of Gauss's Law equation
rules.description: Gauss's Law states that the electric flux through a closed surface is equal to the enclosed charge divided by the permittivity of free space. This is expressed as Φ = Q_enc/ε₀.
rules.check_logic: Check if the student correctly applies Gauss's Law, using Φ = ∮E·dA = Q_enc/ε₀. Ensure the surface is closed and the integration is performed correctly.
common_errors: Misapplying Gauss's Law to non-closed surfaces
Forgetting to divide by ε₀
Incorrect integration of E·dA

rules.title: Check sign convention for electric field
rules.description: The electric field vector should point outward for positive charges and inward for negative charges when calculating net electric flux.
rules.check_logic: Verify the direction of the electric field vectors relative to the enclosed charge. Ensure the sign of the charge is correctly accounted for in determining the field direction.
common_errors: Incorrect direction of field vectors
Ignoring the influence of charge sign on field direction

rules.title: Determine applicability of Gauss's Law
rules.description: Gauss's Law is best applied to problems with high symmetry (spherical, cylindrical, planar). Ensure the environment complies with these conditions before application.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the problem exhibits spherical, cylindrical, or planar symmetry suitable for Gauss's Law. Verify that the symmetry simplifies the calculation of the electric field.
common_errors: Applying Gauss's Law to asymmetric charge distributions
Not recognizing symmetry to simplify calculations

rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of calculations
rules.description: Ensure dimensionally consistent equations by verifying units of electric flux (N·m²/C) and charge (C).
rules.check_logic: Verify that all terms are dimensionally consistent with N·m²/C for flux and C for charge. Check intermediate steps for unit consistency.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for electric flux
Mixing up charge and electric field units

rules.title: Ensure correct use of coordinate systems
rules.description: Students should correctly choose and apply spherical, cylindrical, or Cartesian coordinates based on the symmetry and geometry of the charge or field.
rules.check_logic: Verify the appropriate coordinate system is used and correctly implemented based on the problem's symmetry. Ensure the limits of integration match the chosen coordinate system.
common_errors: Selecting inappropriate coordinate systems
Miscalculating due to coordinate system misapplication

rules.title: Evaluate surface choice for Gauss's Law application
rules.description: Choose surfaces that simplify calculations, typically spheres for point charges, cylinders for line charges, and planes for sheet charges.
rules.check_logic: Examine the selection of Gaussian surfaces to ensure they facilitate calculation based on enclosed symmetry. Verify that the chosen surface aligns with the charge distribution.
common_errors: Complicating calculations with arbitrary surface selections
Ignoring simpler symmetrical surface choices

rules.title: Validate assumption of electrostatic condition
rules.description: Gauss's Law assumes stationary charges. Verify the problem involves electrostatics, not electrodynamics.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the charge configuration is static or changes slowly enough to treat as electrostatic. Verify that no time-varying magnetic fields are present.
common_errors: Applying Gauss's Law in non-static scenarios
Not verifying electrostatic assumptions prior to application

rules.title: Verify boundary conditions at interfaces
rules.description: Ensure correct application of boundary conditions for electric fields at the interface of two materials with different permittivities.
rules.check_logic: Check that the perpendicular component of the electric field accounts for the discontinuity in charge density, and the parallel component remains continuous across the boundary.
common_errors: Ignoring discontinuity in the perpendicular component of the electric field
Incorrectly assuming the parallel component of the field is discontinuous

rules.title: Validate use of superposition principle
rules.description: Ensure that the principle of superposition is correctly applied when multiple charge distributions are present.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the net electric field or flux is calculated as the vector sum of contributions from all charge distributions.
common_errors: Failing to account for all charge distributions
Incorrectly summing vector components

rules.title: Apply Capacitance Formula for Parallel Plate Capacitors
rules.description: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is given by C = ε * A / d, where ε is the permittivity of the material between the plates, A is the area of one plate, and d is the separation between the plates.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the area (A) and separation (d) are correctly used in the formula for parallel plate capacitors, and ensure the permittivity (ε) corresponds to the material between the plates.
common_errors: Using incorrect formula for parallel plate capacitors
Confusing the area with the separation distance
Ignoring the permittivity of the dielectric material

rules.title: Calculate Energy Stored in Capacitor Correctly
rules.description: The energy stored in a capacitor is given by U = 1/2 * C * V^2, where C is the capacitance and V is the voltage across the capacitor.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the energy is calculated using the correct formula, with accurate values for capacitance (C) and voltage (V). Verify that the 1/2 factor is included.
common_errors: Omitting the 1/2 factor in the formula
Using resistance instead of capacitance
Using an incorrect voltage value for the calculation

rules.title: Account for Dielectric Constant in Capacitance
rules.description: The introduction of a dielectric increases the capacitance by a factor of the dielectric constant k, modifying the equation to C = k * ε₀ * A / d, where ε₀ is the permittivity of free space.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the presence of a dielectric is accounted for in the capacitance calculation, and verify that the dielectric constant (k) is applied correctly.
common_errors: Ignoring the increase in capacitance due to the dielectric
Applying the dielectric constant to an incorrect variable
Confusing the dielectric constant (k) with the permittivity (ε)

rules.title: Maintain Correct Sign Conventions for Potential Differences
rules.description: Voltage is defined as the potential difference where the positive terminal is at a higher potential. Correct sign conventions are crucial for determining current flow direction and energy calculations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that potential differences are used with the correct sign conventions, and ensure polarity is assigned accurately based on the electric field direction.
common_errors: Reversing the potential difference sign
Incorrectly assigning polarity
Ignoring the direction of the electric field

rules.title: Ensure Unit Consistency in Capacitance Calculations
rules.description: Capacitance has units of farads (F), equivalent to coulomb/volt. Dimensional consistency ensures accurate calculations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all terms in capacitance calculations use consistent units, such as meters for area dimensions, volts for voltage, and farads for capacitance.
common_errors: Mixing up area units (e.g., cm² vs m²)
Using incorrect units for the dielectric constant
Miscalculating due to voltage in incorrect units (e.g., V vs mV)

rules.title: Apply Correct Rules for Capacitors in Series or Parallel
rules.description: Capacitors in series have a reciprocal capacitance sum, while those in parallel directly add: 1/C_total = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + ... for series; C_total = C₁ + C₂ + ... for parallel.
rules.check_logic: Verify the configuration of capacitors (series or parallel) and ensure the correct formula is applied for the total capacitance calculation.
common_errors: Confusing series and parallel formulae
Incorrectly summing reciprocal quantities
Misidentifying circuit sections as series or parallel

rules.title: Verify Ideal Conditions for Capacitance Calculations
rules.description: Capacitance equations assume ideal conditions: perfectly conductive plates, uniform electric field, and negligible edge effects.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that physical assumptions hold true, such as ignoring fringing effects or non-uniform fields, and verify that the plates are assumed to be perfectly conductive.
common_errors: Considering edge effects without applying corrections
Assuming a uniform field in non-ideal cases
Incorrectly applying the perfect plate assumption

rules.title: Account for Temperature Effects on Capacitance
rules.description: Capacitance can vary with temperature due to changes in the dielectric material's properties. This is particularly important for materials with high temperature coefficients.
rules.check_logic: Verify whether temperature effects on the dielectric constant or material properties are significant and accounted for in calculations.
common_errors: Ignoring temperature dependence of the dielectric constant
Assuming constant capacitance in varying temperature conditions
Failing to use temperature-corrected material properties

rules.title: Verify Ohm's Law Application
rules.description: Ohm's Law defines the relationship between current (I), voltage (V), and resistance (R): V = IR. It applies only to materials or components with linear, ohmic behavior (constant resistance).
