rules.title: Determine correct sign for latent heat
rules.description: The sign of latent heat depends on the direction of the phase transition; positive for endothermic (e.g., melting) and negative for exothermic (e.g., freezing).
rules.check_logic: Identify the nature of the phase transition and verify that the sign of latent heat is correctly applied based on the transition direction.
common_errors: Using positive latent heat for exothermic transitions
Confusing the thermodynamic sign convention
Not defining the transition type clearly

rules.title: Consider constraints during critical phase transitions
rules.description: Critical points and phase transitions often involve boundary constraints such as volume, pressure, or temperature that require special consideration.
rules.check_logic: Ensure calculations respect constraints specific to critical points, such as finite volume changes and constant temperature conditions.
common_errors: Ignoring boundary conditions at critical points
Misapplying constraints, leading to impossible physical states
Assuming linear behavior near critical transitions

rules.title: Verify phase diagram appropriateness
rules.description: Phase diagrams are only valid for well-characterized substances under equilibrium and standard conditions. Ensure assumptions match diagram representation.
rules.check_logic: Confirm phase diagram use fits documented equilibrium conditions and the material's properties.
common_errors: Using phase diagrams beyond their valid temperature-pressure range
Misinterpreting phase boundaries that have pressure-temperature dependencies
Assuming universal applicability without verification

rules.title: Check constraints for melting and boiling points
rules.description: Ensure temperature and pressure are controlled based on the material's melting and boiling points under specified conditions.
rules.check_logic: Verify melting/freezing and boiling/condensation calculations are performed with correct material data and consider standard atmospheric conditions where applicable.
common_errors: Assuming melting/boiling points at non-standard pressures or temperatures
Ignoring pressure variations in boiling calculations
Misusing ideal conditions when real data is required

rules.title: Verify conditions at the triple point
rules.description: The triple point is the unique set of conditions where three phases coexist in equilibrium. Test assumptions and data against this particular state.
rules.check_logic: Ensure calculations and assumptions adhere to the specific temperature and pressure of a substance's triple point.
common_errors: Applying inappropriate conditions that deviate from the triple point's defined state
Misunderstanding the coexistence of phases at the triple point
Overlooking the exactness of triple point conditions in calculations

rules.title: Verify Correct Usage of Specific Heat Capacity Equation
rules.description: The specific heat capacity equation is Q = m*c*ΔT, where Q is the heat added, m is the mass, c is the specific heat capacity, and ΔT is the change in temperature.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the equation Q = m*c*ΔT is correctly applied with the appropriate variables in the computation. Verify that all variables are substituted correctly and that the equation is used in the proper context.
common_errors: Incorrectly substituting mass (m) or specific heat capacity (c)
Confusing units of temperature change ΔT (use degrees Celsius or Kelvin consistently)

rules.title: Check Dimensional Consistency in Heat Capacity Calculations
rules.description: In calculations involving specific heat capacities, units must be consistent across the variables involved: Joules (J) for heat, kilograms (kg) for mass, and degrees Celsius (or Kelvin) for temperature.
rules.check_logic: Verify that dimensions match correctly: [Q] = Joules, [m] = kg, [c] = J/(kg·°C), [ΔT] = °C or K. Ensure proper unit conversions if necessary.
common_errors: Using calories instead of joules without conversion
Mismatch of units for mass or temperature
Mixing Kelvin and Celsius inconsistently

rules.title: Ensure Correct Sign Convention for Heat Flow
rules.description: Heat absorbed by the system should be positive, and heat released by the system should be negative.
rules.check_logic: Check whether heat energy Q is assigned the correct sign based on the flow direction. Verify that endothermic and exothermic processes are correctly identified.
common_errors: Using incorrect sign for heat absorbed/released
Confusing endothermic and exothermic processes

rules.title: Ensure Valid Application of Constant Specific Heat
rules.description: Specific heat capacity is often assumed constant over small temperature changes. This assumption breaks down over larger ranges or near phase transitions.
rules.check_logic: Verify if the assumption that specific heat capacity is constant is valid for the given temperature range. Check for any phase transitions that may invalidate this assumption.
common_errors: Incorrect assumption of constant specific heat capacity over a large temperature range
Ignoring phase transitions

rules.title: Check for Conditions of Adiabatic Process
rules.description: An adiabatic process involves no heat exchange with the surroundings; only changes in internal energy occur.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that Q = 0 in adiabatic processes and focus on changes in pressure, volume, and internal energy. Verify that the first law of thermodynamics is applied correctly.
common_errors: Incorrectly adding heat in adiabatic processes
Misinterpreting adiabatic conditions

rules.title: Verify Applicability of Heat Capacity Ratio (γ)
rules.description: The heat capacity ratio, γ = Cp/Cv, applies specifically to ideal gases under adiabatic processes.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that γ is used only for ideal gases and is linked to the relation between specific heats under adiabatic conditions. Verify that Cp and Cv are correctly identified and used.
common_errors: Using γ in non-ideal gas scenarios
Misapplying Cp for Cv
Using γ in non-adiabatic processes

rules.title: Ensure Correct Conditions for Phase Transition Heat Calculations
rules.description: During phase transitions, specific latent heat (e.g., heat of fusion or vaporization) must be used instead of specific heat capacity.
rules.check_logic: Check if latent heat calculations are correctly applied during phase transitions. Ensure that the heat added or removed corresponds to the latent heat of the substance.
common_errors: Using specific heat capacity instead of latent heat
Ignoring heat absorbed or released during phase change

rules.title: Verify Conservation of Energy in Heat Capacity Problems
rules.description: Energy conservation principles require that energy added to a system equals the change in internal energy plus any work done by the system.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the correct application of conservation laws in calculations involving heat capacity and thermodynamic processes. Verify that all energy flows are accounted for.
common_errors: Neglecting work done or changes in internal energy
Misinterpreting energy flow paths
Ignoring heat losses to the surroundings

rules.title: Ensure Valid Temperature Range for Material Properties
rules.description: Material properties such as specific heat capacity and latent heat are valid only within certain temperature ranges.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the temperature range of the problem is within the valid range for the material's specific heat capacity or latent heat. Check for deviations near extreme temperatures or phase transitions.
common_errors: Using material properties outside their valid temperature range
Ignoring temperature-dependent variations in specific heat capacity

rules.title: Verify Correct Heat Transfer Mode in Calculations
rules.description: Heat transfer can occur via conduction, convection, or radiation, and the mode must be correctly identified and applied.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the correct heat transfer mode is used in calculations. Verify that the equations for conduction, convection, or radiation are applied appropriately.
common_errors: Using conduction equations for convective heat transfer
Ignoring radiative heat transfer in high-temperature scenarios
Mixing heat transfer modes without justification

rules.title: Correct entropy calculation in the microcanonical ensemble
rules.description: In the microcanonical ensemble, entropy (S) is related to the total number of accessible microstates (Ω) by S = k_B * ln(Ω), where k_B is the Boltzmann constant. This equation applies only when the system is isolated, energy is conserved, and the number of particles is fixed.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the entropy is calculated using S = k_B * ln(Ω), that Ω represents the total number of accessible microstates, and that the units of entropy are J/K. Confirm that the system is isolated and energy conservation holds.
common_errors: Forgetting to include the Boltzmann constant (k_B) in the equation.
Using Ω as a probability instead of the total number of microstates.
Using an incorrect base for the logarithm (must be natural logarithm).
Applying the formula to a non-isolated system.

rules.title: Correct use of the canonical partition function
rules.description: In the canonical ensemble, the partition function Z = Σ e^(-E_i / k_B T), where the sum is over all microstates, is the central quantity from which thermodynamic properties are derived. This applies to systems in thermal equilibrium at constant temperature T.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the partition function is calculated as the sum of e^(-E_i / k_B T) across all microstates, that energy units are consistent with temperature (i.e., E_i and k_B T have the same units), and that the system is in thermal equilibrium at constant T.
common_errors: Omitting one or more microstates in the summation.
Using an incorrect temperature or energy scale (e.g., forgetting to convert to Kelvin).
Neglecting the negative sign in the exponent.
Applying the canonical ensemble to a system not in thermal equilibrium.

rules.title: Correct expression of the grand canonical potential
rules.description: In the grand canonical ensemble, the grand potential Φ is given by Φ = -k_B T ln(Ξ), where Ξ is the grand partition function. This is valid for systems with variable particle numbers at constant temperature and chemical potential.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the grand potential is calculated using Φ = -k_B T ln(Ξ), that Ξ is correctly derived as Ξ = Σ e^[(μN - E_i) / k_B T], summing over all states, and that the system satisfies the conditions of constant T, μ, and variable particle numbers.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming the grand canonical potential equals internal energy.
Using the partition function Z instead of the grand partition function Ξ.
Forgetting to account for the chemical potential (μ) in Ξ.
Applying the grand canonical ensemble to a system with fixed particle numbers.

rules.title: Check thermodynamic consistency of derived quantities
rules.description: Derived quantities like energy, entropy, pressure, and chemical potential must satisfy thermodynamic consistency relations (e.g., ⟨E⟩ = -∂lnZ/∂β for the canonical ensemble).
rules.check_logic: Confirm that derived quantities are consistent with their respective ensemble relations, that partial derivatives are correctly evaluated, and that all parameters (e.g., temperature, chemical potential) are accounted for.
common_errors: Miscalculating partial derivatives.
Using incorrect ensemble relations (e.g., applying canonical ensemble relations in a grand canonical system).
Forgetting to account for temperature or other parameters when differentiating.

rules.title: Correct sign convention for energy and work
rules.description: In all ensembles, ensure the correct sign convention for energy: energy input to the system is positive, and work done by the system is negative. This is essential for correctly formulating energy expressions.
rules.check_logic: Check whether energy and work terms follow the convention (e.g., in the first law of thermodynamics: dU = dQ - dW). Verify that the signs are consistent across all calculations.
common_errors: Using the wrong sign for work terms in energy calculations.
Confusing energy input with output (e.g., treating heat lost as positive).
Inconsistent application of the first law of thermodynamics.

rules.title: Ensure dimensional consistency of ensemble equations
rules.description: All derived equations in statistical ensembles must be dimensionally consistent. For example, entropy must have units of J/K, and partition functions should yield dimensionless quantities when used in logarithms.
rules.check_logic: Verify that each term in the equations has consistent and appropriate units (e.g., temperature in Kelvin, energy in Joules, and partition functions dimensionless).
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for temperature or energy (e.g., Celsius instead of Kelvin).
Forgetting to convert Boltzmann constant (k_B) to appropriate units.
Using dimensional quantities in logarithmic expressions without normalization.

rules.title: Check validity conditions for the microcanonical ensemble
rules.description: The microcanonical ensemble assumes an isolated system with fixed energy, volume, and number of particles. This ensemble is not valid for systems that exchange energy or particles with the surroundings.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the system is isolated and that energy, volume, and particle number constraints are explicitly stated and satisfied. Confirm that no energy or particle exchange occurs with the surroundings.
common_errors: Applying microcanonical ensemble to a system in thermal equilibrium with a heat bath.
Neglecting to check if energy conservation holds.
Ignoring particle number conservation.

rules.title: Check validity conditions for the grand canonical ensemble
rules.description: The grand canonical ensemble applies to systems in thermal and chemical equilibrium with a reservoir. The temperature (T), volume (V), and chemical potential (μ) must be constant.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the system satisfies the conditions of thermal and chemical equilibrium, with fixed T, V, and μ. Confirm that the system can exchange particles and energy with the reservoir.
common_errors: Applying the grand canonical ensemble to a system with fixed particle numbers.
Neglecting equilibrium conditions with the reservoir.
Assuming variable temperature or chemical potential.

rules.title: Check equivalence of ensembles in the thermodynamic limit
rules.description: In the thermodynamic limit (large number of particles and volume), the predictions of the microcanonical, canonical, and grand canonical ensembles should converge for bulk properties.
rules.check_logic: Verify that derived quantities (e.g., energy, pressure, entropy) from different ensembles converge in the thermodynamic limit. Ensure that finite-size effects are negligible.
common_errors: Ignoring finite-size effects in small systems.
Assuming equivalence of ensembles without verifying the thermodynamic limit.

rules.title: Verify correct definition of the partition function
rules.description: The partition function Z is defined as the sum over all states of the system, where each state's Boltzmann factor is exp(-E_i / kT). It serves as the basis for calculating thermodynamic quantities.
rules.check_logic: Ensure Z = Σ(exp(-E_i / kT)) is used, where the summation covers all possible states of the system.
common_errors: Omitting some states in the summation.
Using an incorrect Boltzmann factor, such as exp(E_i / kT) or exp(-kT / E_i).
Confusing the partition function for a probability distribution.

rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of the partition function
rules.description: The partition function Z must be dimensionless since it is a ratio of probabilities, ensuring compatibility with thermodynamic and statistical physics principles.
rules.check_logic: Verify that E_i is in units of energy, k is the Boltzmann constant, and T is in absolute temperature (Kelvin). Confirm Z is a dimensionless quantity.
common_errors: Using non-energy units for E_i, such as momentum or force.
Incorrect units for k or T, leading to a non-dimensionless Z.
Forgetting to convert temperature to Kelvin when required.

rules.title: Ensure probability normalization using the partition function
rules.description: The probabilities of individual states, P_i = exp(-E_i / kT) / Z, must sum to 1 over all states. This ensures proper normalization in statistical mechanics.
rules.check_logic: Check whether Σ(P_i) = 1, where P_i = exp(-E_i / kT) / Z and the summation spans all states.
common_errors: Forgetting to divide by the partition function Z.
Failing to include all states in the summation for normalization.
Incorrect exponentiation in the Boltzmann factor.

rules.title: Verify thermodynamic quantities derived from the partition function
rules.description: Thermodynamic quantities like internal energy (U), entropy (S), and Helmholtz free energy (F) are derived using derivatives of the partition function. For example, U = -∂(ln Z) / ∂(1/kT).
rules.check_logic: Ensure the derivatives are correctly computed and consistent with the definitions of the thermodynamic quantities.
common_errors: Incorrect derivative of ln Z with respect to 1/kT.
Mixing up signs in the expressions for thermodynamic quantities.
Applying the derivative with respect to an incorrect variable (e.g., T instead of 1/kT).

rules.title: Check partition function behavior in the high-temperature limit
rules.description: In the high-temperature limit (T → ∞), the Boltzmann factor exp(-E_i / kT) approaches 1, and the partition function Z becomes approximately the total number of states.
rules.check_logic: Verify that Z ≈ total number of states for T → ∞.
common_errors: Incorrect asymptotic behavior of Z in high-temperature conditions.
Ignoring the contribution of all states when summing in the high-temperature limit.

rules.title: Check partition function behavior in the low-temperature limit
rules.description: In the low-temperature limit (T → 0), the Boltzmann factor exp(-E_i / kT) is dominated by the ground state (lowest energy state). Thus, Z ≈ exp(-E_0 / kT).
rules.check_logic: Verify that Z is dominated by the ground state contribution for T → 0.
common_errors: Failing to prioritize the ground state in the low-temperature limit.
Ignoring the behavior of the Boltzmann factor as T → 0.

rules.title: Verify validity conditions for using the partition function
rules.description: The partition function assumes the system is in thermal equilibrium and that the states are distinguishable and non-degenerate unless otherwise stated.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the system is in thermal equilibrium and that the assumptions (e.g., distinguishability of states) are explicitly stated and valid.
common_errors: Applying the partition function to non-equilibrium systems.
Failing to account for degeneracy in the states when calculating Z.
Assuming indistinguishable particles without appropriate corrections.

rules.title: Verify relationship between Helmholtz free energy and partition function
rules.description: The Helmholtz free energy F is related to the partition function by F = -kT ln Z. This relationship connects statistical mechanics with thermodynamics.
rules.check_logic: Ensure F = -kT ln Z is used correctly, with Z being dimensionless.
common_errors: Using a non-dimensionless Z in the logarithmic function.
Incorrect sign in the expression for F.
Using an incorrect base for the natural logarithm (e.g., log10 instead of ln).

rules.title: Verify Energy Expression for Degrees of Freedom
rules.description: Equipartition theorem states that each degree of freedom contributes (1/2)kT to the internal energy of a system at thermal equilibrium.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the energy associated with each degree of freedom is expressed as (1/2)kT, where k is the Boltzmann constant and T is the absolute temperature. Verify that the factor (1/2) is not omitted and that the degrees of freedom are correctly identified.
common_errors: Using incorrect factor, e.g., forgetting (1/2) factor
Misinterpreting degrees of freedom count

rules.title: Check Temperature Influence on Energy
rules.description: The equipartition theorem relates the energy of a system directly to its temperature; energy per degree of freedom linearly increases with temperature.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the energy calculated by the equipartition theorem is directly proportional to the absolute temperature (in Kelvin). Ensure that no non-linear dependencies are introduced.
common_errors: Ignoring the linear dependency on temperature
Using non-absolute temperature scales

rules.title: Validate Equipartition Application Conditions
rules.description: Equipartition theorem applies to classical systems where energy is quadratic with coordinate and momentum, and assumes ideal conditions without quantum restrictions.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the system is classical, the temperature is sufficiently high to avoid quantum effects, and the degrees of freedom involve quadratic energy dependencies. Verify that quantum systems or systems with non-quadratic energy terms are excluded.
common_errors: Applying equipartition theorem to quantum systems improperly
Applying to systems with non-quadratic energy dependencies

rules.title: Verify Positive Energy Contributions
rules.description: Energy contributions from degrees of freedom should be positive as temperature and Boltzmann constant are inherently positive.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that all energy contributions calculated from kT are positive. Verify that no negative values arise due to miscalculation of temperature or incorrect sign assignment.
common_errors: Negative energy due to miscalculation of temperature or incorrect sign assignment

rules.title: Check Dimensional Consistency of Energy and Temperature Variables
rules.description: The energy given by the equipartition theorem must have correct units, with kT yielding units of energy.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the units of kT align with the units of energy (e.g., Joules in SI units). Ensure that the Boltzmann constant and temperature are expressed in compatible units.
common_errors: Confusing units of temperature (Kelvin vs other scales)
Incorrect unit assignment for Boltzmann constant leading to dimensional inconsistencies

rules.title: Validate Degree of Freedom Count in the System
rules.description: The total energy contribution depends on correctly identifying the number of degrees of freedom relevant to the system being considered.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the degree of freedom count matches the physical setup of the system (e.g., 3 for translational per particle, additional for rotations and vibrations). Verify that all relevant degrees of freedom are included and none are omitted.
common_errors: Neglecting rotational or vibrational degrees of freedom
Incorrectly summing degrees of freedom across molecules

rules.title: Check Kinematic Constraints Affecting Degrees of Freedom
rules.description: Ensure the system's geometry or constraints do not limit the degrees of freedom expected from theoretical calculations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that kinematic constraints, such as fixed or constrained components, are accounted for. Adjust the effective degrees of freedom accordingly.
common_errors: Overcounting degrees of freedom by ignoring fixed or constrained components
Missing constraints that reduce effective degrees of freedom

rules.title: Evaluate Equipartition Theorem in Limiting Cases
rules.description: Assess application of equipartition theorem in edge cases such as very low temperatures where quantum effects become significant.
rules.check_logic: Check applicability of the theorem in limiting cases where classical assumptions degrade, especially as temperature approaches zero. Ensure that quantum mechanical considerations are applied when necessary.
common_errors: Using classical equipartition in regimes dominated by quantum mechanics
Ignoring quantum restrictions at low temperatures

rules.title: Verify High-Temperature Limit Behavior
rules.description: At very high temperatures, the equipartition theorem should remain valid, and quantum effects should become negligible.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the energy contributions per degree of freedom remain consistent with (1/2)kT at high temperatures. Verify that no deviations occur due to incorrect assumptions.
common_errors: Introducing quantum effects unnecessarily at high temperatures
Incorrectly modifying energy contributions at high temperatures

rules.title: Verify Stefan-Boltzmann Law Application
rules.description: Ensure the formula for the Stefan-Boltzmann Law is correctly stated and applied: P = σAeT^4, where σ is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant, A is the area, e is the emissivity, and T is the temperature in Kelvin.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the power emitted is calculated using P = σAeT^4, with temperature in Kelvin and consideration of emissivity. Ensure all variables are correctly substituted and calculated.
common_errors: Using incorrect formula for power emitted
Confusing temperature units (Celsius instead of Kelvin)
Neglecting the emissivity factor

rules.title: Check Dimensional Consistency in Blackbody Equations
rules.description: Verify that units align correctly: Power emitted (P) should be in Watts.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the output of P = σAeT^4 has units of Watts (W). Confirm that all input variables have consistent units (e.g., area in square meters, temperature in Kelvin).
common_errors: Incorrect unit conversion leading to power not in Watts
Mismatch in units leading to incorrect calculations

rules.title: Ensure Temperature is in Kelvin
rules.description: Confirm that the temperature used in the Stefan-Boltzmann Law is in Kelvin, as this law requires absolute temperature scales.
rules.check_logic: Verify temperature input is in Kelvin before substituting into the Stefan-Boltzmann equation. If temperature is provided in Celsius, ensure it is converted to Kelvin using T(K) = T(°C) + 273.15.
common_errors: Using temperature in Celsius instead of Kelvin
Misconversion of temperature units

rules.title: Verify Wien's Law for Peak Wavelength
rules.description: Ensure Wien's Law is correctly applied to identify peak wavelength λ_peak = b/T, where b is Wien's displacement constant.
rules.check_logic: Verify λ_peak is calculated with λ_peak = b/T, and ensure b is correctly valued as approximately 2.898 × 10^-3 m·K. Confirm that T is in Kelvin.
common_errors: Incorrect calculation of the peak wavelength
Misapplication of Wien's displacement constant
Using temperature in incorrect units

rules.title: Check Validity of Blackbody Assumptions
rules.description: Confirm that the body assumed to be a blackbody is a perfect emitter or sufficiently close, such as stars or furnace cavities.
rules.check_logic: Assess the physical situation to ensure it meets the requirements for treating as a blackbody. Verify that the emissivity is close to 1 for near-perfect blackbodies.
common_errors: Applying blackbody equations to non-blackbody actors
Ignoring the requirement for a blackbody to be a perfect emitter

rules.title: Verify Geometric Area in Stefan-Boltzmann Calculation
rules.description: Ensure that the surface area used in calculations accurately represents the radiating object's geometry.
rules.check_logic: Confirm the surface area (A) is correctly calculated from given geometric parameters before substituting into the equation. For example, use A = 4πr^2 for a sphere.
common_errors: Incorrect calculation or assumption of surface area
Misapplying the geometry of the object in area calculations

rules.title: Validate Emissivity Value and Range
rules.description: Check that emissivity (e) is within the physical range of 0 ≤ e ≤ 1, representing a real material's emissive properties.
rules.check_logic: Confirm emissivity value is within allowable limits before using in Stefan-Boltzmann Law. Ensure emissivity is not confused with reflectivity or absorptivity.
common_errors: Using emissivity values outside the physical range
Confusing emissivity with reflectivity or other optical properties

rules.title: Correct Sign Convention for Heat Transfer
rules.description: Check that the sign convention adheres to the principle that energy emitted by radiation from the surface is considered as positive heat loss.
rules.check_logic: Verify energy flow direction and ensure heat loss is denoted correctly as a negative contribution in energy balance calculations. Confirm that heat gain is treated as positive.
common_errors: Incorrectly stating energy loss as a gain
Misunderstanding the sign convention in heat balance

rules.title: Verify Energy Density of Blackbody Radiation
rules.description: Ensure the energy density of blackbody radiation is calculated correctly using u = (4σ/c)T^4, where c is the speed of light.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the energy density u is calculated using u = (4σ/c)T^4, with T in Kelvin and c as the speed of light in vacuum.
common_errors: Incorrect formula for energy density
Using incorrect value for the speed of light
Temperature not in Kelvin

rules.title: Verify Radiative Flux Calculation
rules.description: Ensure the radiative flux (F) is calculated correctly using F = σT^4 for a perfect blackbody.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the radiative flux is calculated using F = σT^4, with T in Kelvin. For non-perfect blackbodies, ensure emissivity is included as F = eσT^4.
common_errors: Neglecting emissivity for non-perfect blackbodies
Using incorrect formula for radiative flux
Temperature not in Kelvin

rules.title: Verify heat engine efficiency equation
rules.description: The efficiency of a heat engine is given by η = 1 - (Qc/Qh), where Qh is the heat absorbed from the hot reservoir and Qc is the heat rejected to the cold reservoir. This relation assumes a cyclic process.
rules.check_logic: Check if η = 1 - (Qc/Qh) is correctly applied, ensuring Qh > Qc > 0 and all terms are positive.
common_errors: Incorrect placement of Qc and Qh in the formula.
Assigning negative values to Qc or Qh, violating the assumption of heat as a positive quantity.
Calculating η > 1, which is physically impossible.

rules.title: Validate Coefficient of Performance (COP) for refrigerators
rules.description: The COP of a refrigerator is defined as COP = Qc / W, where Qc is the heat extracted from the cold reservoir and W is the work done on the system.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that COP is calculated as COP = Qc/W, where Qc > 0 and W > 0, and verify that the result is physically meaningful (COP > 0).
common_errors: Misinterpreting the formula and using Qh instead of Qc.
Using a negative value for work done (W), which is inconsistent with the definition.
Calculating COP < 0, which is unphysical.

rules.title: Apply the First Law of Thermodynamics
rules.description: The first law states ΔU = Q - W, where ΔU is the change in internal energy, Q is the heat added to the system, and W is the work done by the system. This law must hold for any thermodynamic process.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the energy balance ΔU = Q - W is used, all terms have consistent units, and the sign convention is correctly applied.
common_errors: Forgetting to account for all forms of energy transfer (Q or W).
Incorrect sign convention for work (e.g., using W as work done on the system instead of by the system).
Ignoring ΔU when it is non-zero for non-cyclic processes.

rules.title: Check Carnot efficiency limits
rules.description: The Carnot efficiency is the theoretical maximum efficiency for a heat engine operating between two temperatures, given by η_Carnot = 1 - (Tc/Th), where Tc and Th are the absolute temperatures of the cold and hot reservoirs, respectively.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that η_Carnot = 1 - (Tc/Th) is used, with Tc < Th and temperatures expressed in Kelvin. Verify that η_Carnot ≤ 1.
common_errors: Using temperatures in Celsius instead of Kelvin.
Switching Tc and Th, leading to unphysical negative efficiency.
Calculating η_Carnot > 1, which violates the second law of thermodynamics.

rules.title: Ensure consistent sign conventions for heat and work
rules.description: In thermodynamics, heat (Q) is positive when added to the system, and work (W) is positive when done by the system. Misinterpreting these conventions can lead to incorrect calculations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that Q is positive for heat input and W is positive for work output. For refrigerators, W is positive for work done on the system. Ensure consistency across all calculations.
common_errors: Using opposite sign conventions for Q and W.
Confusing work done by the system with work done on the system.
Neglecting to check signs in cyclic processes.

rules.title: Verify compliance with the Kelvin-Planck statement
rules.description: The Kelvin-Planck statement of the second law of thermodynamics states that it is impossible to construct a heat engine that operates in a cycle and converts all the heat absorbed into work (i.e., W cannot equal Qh).
rules.check_logic: Check if W < Qh for any heat engine operating in a cycle. Ensure that some heat is always rejected to the cold reservoir (Qc > 0).
common_errors: Assuming 100% conversion of heat to work (W = Qh).
Ignoring losses to the cold reservoir (Qc).
Violating the second law by assuming η = 1.

rules.title: Check conditions for reversible processes
rules.description: A thermodynamic process is reversible if it is quasi-static and there are no dissipative forces (e.g., friction, turbulence). Reversible processes are idealized and maximize efficiency.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that processes assumed to be reversible have no dissipative forces, occur quasi-statically, and involve infinitesimally small temperature gradients for heat transfer.
common_errors: Assuming reversibility for real-world processes with friction or turbulence.
Overlooking the need for infinitesimally small temperature gradients for heat transfer.

rules.title: Ensure dimensional and unit consistency
rules.description: In thermodynamic equations, all terms must have consistent units (e.g., Q, W, and ΔU in joules, temperatures in Kelvin). Incorrect units can cause significant errors in calculations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all terms in equations have compatible units (joules for energy, Kelvin for temperature, etc.). Ensure proper unit conversions where necessary.
common_errors: Using Celsius instead of Kelvin in temperature ratios.
Mixing different energy units (e.g., joules and calories) without conversion.
Failing to convert work or heat into consistent energy units.

rules.title: Verify entropy change calculations
rules.description: The change in entropy (ΔS) for a reversible process is given by ΔS = Qrev/T, where Qrev is the reversible heat transfer and T is the absolute temperature. For irreversible processes, ΔS > Q/T.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that ΔS = Qrev/T is used for reversible processes, and verify that ΔS ≥ 0 for all processes, consistent with the second law of thermodynamics.
common_errors: Using Q instead of Qrev for entropy calculations in reversible processes.
Calculating ΔS < 0 for an isolated system, violating the second law.
Ignoring the temperature dependence of entropy changes.

rules.title: Verify the differential form of the Clausius-Clapeyron equation
rules.description: The Clausius-Clapeyron equation in its differential form is written as dP/dT = L / (T * ΔV), where dP/dT is the slope of the phase boundary in a P-T diagram, L is the latent heat of the phase transition, T is the absolute temperature, and ΔV is the change in specific volume between the two phases. This relationship applies at equilibrium between two phases.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the equation is correctly structured as dP/dT = L / (T * ΔV) with all terms properly substituted.
common_errors: Incorrectly swapping ΔV and L in the equation.
Forgetting to use absolute temperature (T) in Kelvin.
Omitting ΔV or using incorrect phase volumes for ΔV.

rules.title: Confirm applicability to first-order phase transitions
rules.description: The Clausius-Clapeyron equation is valid only for first-order phase transitions (e.g., melting, boiling) characterized by a discontinuous change in entropy and volume. It does not apply to second-order transitions or continuous phase changes.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the phase transition is first-order, specifically involving latent heat.
common_errors: Applying the Clausius-Clapeyron equation to second-order phase transitions.
Failure to confirm that the phase transition involves latent heat.

rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of terms
rules.description: Ensure all terms in the Clausius-Clapeyron equation have consistent units: L in J/kg or J/mol, T in Kelvin, ΔV in m³/kg or m³/mol, and dP/dT in Pa/K. Dimensional consistency ensures the equation's validity.
rules.check_logic: Verify consistency of units for L, T, ΔV, and dP/dT throughout the equation.
common_errors: Using Celsius instead of Kelvin for temperature.
Mismatched units between ΔV and L (e.g., mixing specific and molar quantities).
Omitting unit conversion where necessary (e.g., from bar to Pascal).

rules.title: Verify correct sign conventions for ΔV and ΔS
rules.description: Ensure ΔV (change in specific volume) sign matches the phase transition direction. For example, during vaporization, ΔV > 0 (as gas has a larger volume than liquid). Additionally, confirm entropy change ΔS = L/T aligns with heat flow direction.
rules.check_logic: Check that ΔV and ΔS possess the correct signs based on the transition analyzed.
common_errors: Incorrectly assigning ΔV < 0 for vaporization.
Using the wrong sign for ΔS during absorption or release.
Neglecting the physical interpretation of volume changes.

rules.title: Ensure latent heat is temperature-dependent if specified
rules.description: In some scenarios, latent heat (L) can vary with temperature. If specified, ensure the correct form L(T) is used in the Clausius-Clapeyron equation.
rules.check_logic: Confirm whether L is constant or temperature-dependent, using the appropriate form.
common_errors: Assuming constant latent heat when temperature dependence is specified.
Failing to substitute the correct expression for L(T).

rules.title: Confirm the geometric interpretation on a P-T diagram
rules.description: The Clausius-Clapeyron equation describes the slope (dP/dT) of the phase boundary on a pressure-temperature (P-T) diagram. Ensure the correct identification of the phase boundary and accurate slope calculation.
rules.check_logic: Verify slope (dP/dT) accuracy for the appropriate phase boundary.
common_errors: Analyzing incorrect phase boundary (e.g., melting instead of boiling).
Misinterpreting slope direction on the P-T diagram.

rules.title: Verify entropy change relation ΔS = L/T
rules.description: Confirm that the entropy change (ΔS) during a phase transition relates to latent heat (L) as ΔS = L/T, ensuring consistent units and temperature in Kelvin.
rules.check_logic: Validate correct implementation of ΔS = L/T with consistent units.
common_errors: Neglecting Kelvin temperature conversion before calculating ΔS.
Incorrectly presuming ΔS = L without dividing by T.
Mixing units for L and T (e.g., using Celsius for T).

rules.title: Verify Law of Reflection
rules.description: Ensure that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection, measured with respect to the normal at the interface of the reflecting surface.
rules.check_logic: Verify that θ_incidence = θ_reflection, where both angles are measured from the normal to the surface. Ensure proper units (radians or degrees) are used consistently.
common_errors: Measuring angles from the surface instead of the normal
Using incorrect units for angles (e.g., radians vs degrees)
Confusing angle of incidence with angle of reflection

rules.title: Validate Snell's Law
rules.description: Verify that Snell's Law (n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2)) is satisfied at the interface between two media with indices of refraction n1 and n2.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2), where θ1 and θ2 are angles of incidence and refraction measured from the normal. Confirm that trigonometric functions are applied correctly and units are consistent.
common_errors: Incorrectly identifying the media or their refractive indices
Using the wrong trigonometric function (e.g., cosine instead of sine)
Using degrees instead of radians in calculations without proper conversion

rules.title: Check Total Internal Reflection Condition
rules.description: Ensure that total internal reflection occurs only when light travels from a denser to a rarer medium and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.
rules.check_logic: Verify that n1 > n2 and θ_incidence > θ_critical, where θ_critical = arcsin(n2/n1). Ensure that the refractive indices are valid and the critical angle is computed correctly.
common_errors: Incorrect computation of the critical angle
Attempting total internal reflection when light is traveling from a rarer to denser medium
Ignoring the condition θ_incidence > θ_critical

rules.title: Verify Sign Convention for Angles
rules.description: Ensure that all angles (incidence, reflection, refraction) are measured with respect to the normal to the surface and not the surface itself.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that the reference for angle measurement is the normal to the interface. Verify consistency in angle measurement across all calculations.
common_errors: Measuring angles from the surface instead of the normal
Using inconsistent reference directions for different angles
Misidentifying the normal direction in complex geometries

rules.title: Enforce Geometric Constraints for Ray Diagrams
rules.description: Verify that in ray diagrams, incident, reflected, and refracted rays obey geometric constraints such as alignment with the normal and proper angle relationships.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that reflected and refracted rays emerge from the point of incidence and maintain the correct angular relationships with the normal. Confirm that diagrams are consistent with physical laws.
common_errors: Misaligning rays with the point of incidence
Drawing rays that violate the law of reflection or Snell's Law
Incorrectly extending or tracing rays in diagrams

rules.title: Validate Physical Range of Refractive Indices
rules.description: Ensure that the refractive indices (n1, n2) are greater than or equal to 1, as they represent the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to that in the medium.
rules.check_logic: Verify that n1 ≥ 1 and n2 ≥ 1. Confirm that refractive indices are assigned correctly for common materials (e.g., air, water, glass).
common_errors: Using a refractive index less than 1 for a physical medium
Incorrectly assigning refractive indices for air (n ≈ 1) or vacuum (n = 1)
Failing to verify refractive indices for exotic materials

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in Calculations
rules.description: Verify that all quantities in reflection and refraction equations (angles, refractive indices) have consistent and appropriate units.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that angles are in radians (or properly converted), refractive indices are dimensionless, and trigonometric functions are applied correctly. Ensure unit consistency throughout calculations.
common_errors: Using inconsistent angle units (degrees vs radians)
Applying trigonometric functions to values with incorrect units
Failing to confirm that refractive indices are dimensionless

rules.title: Verify Boundary Conditions at Interfaces
rules.description: Ensure that at the interface between two media, the incident, reflected, and refracted rays meet at the same point, and their directions satisfy the laws of reflection and refraction.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the point of incidence is common to all rays and angular relationships follow the laws of reflection and refraction. Confirm that rays are properly aligned in diagrams.
common_errors: Misplacing the point of incidence in ray diagrams
Violating angular relationships at the interface
Failing to align incident, reflected, and refracted rays properly

rules.title: Verify Critical Angle Calculation
rules.description: Ensure that the critical angle is calculated correctly for total internal reflection scenarios.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that the critical angle is computed as θ_critical = arcsin(n2/n1) and is only defined when n1 > n2. Verify that the calculation uses valid refractive indices.
common_errors: Using incorrect formula for critical angle
Attempting to calculate a critical angle when n1 ≤ n2
Failing to use valid refractive indices in the calculation

rules.title: Verify mirror and lens equation usage
rules.description: The mirror and lens equation is given by 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where f is the focal length, v is the image distance, and u is the object distance. This equation applies to both mirrors and lenses, provided the paraxial approximation holds (small angles and rays close to the optical axis).
rules.check_logic: Check if the given distances (u, v, f) satisfy the equation 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. Ensure that the paraxial approximation is valid (small angles and rays close to the optical axis).
common_errors: Forgetting to use the reciprocal values (1/u, 1/v, 1/f) and directly adding distances.
Incorrect substitution of object distance or image distance.
Applying the equation when the paraxial approximation is not valid (large angles or off-axis rays).

rules.title: Verify sign convention adherence for spherical mirrors and lenses
rules.description: The sign convention for mirrors and lenses depends on the Cartesian coordinate system: distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive, and those measured against it are negative. For concave mirrors and converging lenses, focal length is positive; for convex mirrors and diverging lenses, focal length is negative.
rules.check_logic: Check if the signs of u, v, and f are consistent with the sign convention and the type of mirror or lens provided. Verify that the sign convention is applied consistently across all calculations.
common_errors: Using the wrong sign for the focal length of convex mirrors or diverging lenses.
Reversing the sign of object distance and image distance.
Incorrectly assigning positive or negative signs to distances for specific cases.

rules.title: Validate the magnification formula usage
rules.description: The magnification (m) is given by m = -v/u for mirrors and m = v/u for lenses. It represents the ratio of the image height to the object height. This formula holds under the paraxial approximation.
rules.check_logic: Verify if the magnification formula is correctly applied, ensuring the correct formula is used for mirrors versus lenses. Confirm that the sign conventions for v and u are respected.
common_errors: Forgetting the negative sign in the magnification formula for mirrors.
Confusing the formulas for mirrors and lenses.
Improperly calculating the image or object height relative to magnification.

rules.title: Ensure geometric constraints on focal point location
rules.description: The focal point of a mirror or lens must lie at a fixed distance (f) from the mirror's pole or lens' optical center. For mirrors, this is f = R/2, where R is the radius of curvature.
rules.check_logic: Check if the focal length f is consistent with the given radius of curvature R (f = R/2). Ensure that the geometry of the optical system is consistent with the given parameters.
common_errors: Using an incorrect formula for focal length based on radius of curvature.
Confusing radius of curvature (R) with diameter or focal length directly.
Applying the formula for lenses to mirrors or vice versa.

rules.title: Verify application under paraxial approximation
rules.description: The laws of mirrors and lenses (mirror equation, lens equation, magnification formula) are valid only under the paraxial approximation, where incident rays make small angles with the optical axis, and distances are measured close to the axis.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the angles involved are small and the rays are near the optical axis. Check for any mention of large angles, off-axis rays, or aberrations.
common_errors: Applying the mirror or lens equation to situations where the paraxial approximation is violated.
Neglecting the effects of aberrations for large angles or rays far from the optical axis.

rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of optical equations
rules.description: In the mirror and lens equations, all distances (u, v, f) must have the same units, typically in meters or centimeters. Magnification is unitless as it is a ratio of heights or distances.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all distances in the equation have consistent units (e.g., meters or centimeters) and that magnification is dimensionless.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for object distance, image distance, or focal length.
Treating magnification as if it has units.

rules.title: Validate real and virtual image criteria
rules.description: For mirrors and lenses, real images occur when light rays converge, and virtual images occur when they appear to diverge. Real images have positive image distances, while virtual images have negative image distances.
rules.check_logic: Check if the image distance (v) is positive for real images and negative for virtual images, consistent with the type of mirror or lens. Ensure that the interpretation of real and virtual images aligns with the optical system's geometry.
common_errors: Misidentifying the type of image (real or virtual) based on the sign of v.
Confusing the properties of real and virtual images for mirrors versus lenses.

rules.title: Verify ray diagram consistency with optical laws
rules.description: Ray diagrams for mirrors and lenses must follow the laws of reflection or refraction. For example, reflected rays must obey the law of reflection, and refracted rays must adhere to Snell's law at the lens surfaces.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the drawn rays follow the laws of reflection and refraction. Verify that the image location in the diagram matches the calculated one using the lens or mirror equation.
common_errors: Drawing rays that do not pass through the focal point for specific cases.
Violating the law of reflection for mirrors (angle of incidence ≠ angle of reflection).
Not using Snell's law for refracted rays at a lens surface.

rules.title: Check for spherical and chromatic aberrations
rules.description: Spherical aberration occurs when rays far from the optical axis do not converge at the same focal point. Chromatic aberration occurs in lenses due to the dispersion of light, causing different colors to focus at different points.
rules.check_logic: Verify if the optical system accounts for spherical and chromatic aberrations, especially for large apertures or wide-angle lenses. Check if corrective measures (e.g., aspherical lenses or achromatic doublets) are mentioned.
common_errors: Ignoring spherical aberration for wide-aperture systems.
Neglecting chromatic aberration in lenses with significant dispersion.
Failing to mention corrective measures for aberrations in high-precision systems.

rules.title: Apply Lensmaker's Equation for Focal Length
rules.description: The Lensmaker's Equation calculates the focal length of a lens based on its radius of curvature and the refractive index. It applies to thin lenses under the paraxial approximation.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the focal length is calculated using 1/f = (n - 1) * (1/R1 - 1/R2), where R1 and R2 are the radii of curvature of the lens surfaces, and n is the refractive index of the lens material.
common_errors: Using wrong sign for radii of curvature
Incorrect refractive index value in the equation

rules.title: Adhere to Sign Conventions for Lens Formulas
rules.description: In optics, sign conventions dictate the positive or negative assignment for distances. For converging lenses, distances measured against the direction of incident light (left to right) are negative.
rules.check_logic: Verify that object distances, image distances, and focal lengths adhere to the sign conventions based on lens type and orientation. For example, for a converging lens, focal length is positive, and for a diverging lens, it is negative.
common_errors: Incorrect sign for object distance when using lens formulas
Wrong sign in focal length application in calculations

rules.title: Calculate Magnification Correctly
rules.description: Magnification for optical instruments is defined as the ratio of the image height to the object height. Ensure calculations reflect this definition.
rules.check_logic: Calculate magnification using M = -di/do for lenses and telescopes, ensuring the negative sign indicates inverted images. For microscopes, ensure the total magnification is the product of the objective and eyepiece magnifications.
common_errors: Forgetting to include negative sign for inverted images
Misinterpreting object and image distances
Omitting the contribution of the eyepiece in total magnification for microscopes

rules.title: Maintain Geometric Alignment Constraints
rules.description: Geometric alignment in optical instruments is critical to their functioning. Ensure lenses, mirrors, and other components are appropriately aligned.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that all components of the optical instrument are aligned along the principal axis or the intended optical path. Check for tilt, decentering, or misalignment that could cause aberrations or distortions.
common_errors: Misaligned lenses causing distortion
Improper orientation of mirrors in telescopes
Failure to align the optical axis with the principal axis

rules.title: Validate Conditions for Ray Optics
rules.description: Ray optics applies when the wavelength is much smaller than the size of the optical elements, allowing simplification using geometric optics equations.
rules.check_logic: Check that the wavelength of light is significantly smaller than the aperture size or lens diameter before applying ray optics principles. If not, wave optics principles should be used instead.
common_errors: Applying ray optics to setups not satisfying wavelength-to-aperture proportion
Using ray optics equations for phenomena requiring wave optics

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in Equations
rules.description: Optical instruments involve several dimensional quantities (distance, height, radius). Ensure units are consistent when substituting into formulas.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all quantities, especially distances, focal lengths, and radii of curvature, are in compatible units (commonly meters or centimeters) before calculations. Perform unit conversions if necessary.
common_errors: Mismatch in units between focal length and object/image distances
Ignoring conversion of units prior to mathematical operations

rules.title: Consider Eyepiece Accommodation in Telescopes
rules.description: The eyepiece of a telescope adjusts the focal points for viewing. Ensure calculations consider the influence of eyepiece characteristics.
rules.check_logic: Check if the telescope's eyepiece focal length is used correctly in image formation and determining overall magnification. Ensure the eye relief distance is accounted for in practical setups.
common_errors: Overlooking the effect of eye relief distance
Inaccurate use of eyepiece focal length causing miscalculation of magnification

rules.title: Apply Object-Image Distance Equation Correctly
rules.description: For optical instruments, the relation 1/f = 1/do + 1/di governs the relationship between object and image distances with focal length.
rules.check_logic: Verify that object distance (do) and image distance (di) are correctly placed in the equation and solved for their respective values. Ensure proper unit consistency during calculations.
common_errors: Mixing up object and image distances when substituting into the equation
Improper conversion of units resulting in incorrect solution

rules.title: Account for Optical Aberrations
rules.description: Optical aberrations such as spherical aberration, chromatic aberration, and astigmatism can affect image quality. Ensure these are minimized in design and calculations.
rules.check_logic: Check if the lens or mirror design accounts for aberrations. For chromatic aberration, verify if an achromatic doublet or similar correction is used. For spherical aberration, ensure the lens shape is optimized.
common_errors: Ignoring chromatic aberration in multi-wavelength setups
Failure to account for spherical aberration in high-precision instruments

rules.title: Consider Diffraction Limit in Resolution
rules.description: The resolution of optical instruments is limited by diffraction, which depends on the aperture size and wavelength of light.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the resolution calculation considers the diffraction limit using the formula θ = 1.22 * λ/D, where λ is the wavelength and D is the aperture diameter.
common_errors: Overestimating resolution by ignoring diffraction effects
Using incorrect aperture size in diffraction limit calculations

rules.title: Verify correct application of Snell's Law equation
rules.description: Snell's Law states that n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2), where n1 and n2 are the refractive indices of the first and second media, and θ1 and θ2 are the angles of incidence and refraction, respectively. This law applies when light passes between two transparent media.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the equation n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2) is used correctly with proper substitution of values for n1, n2, θ1, and θ2.
common_errors: Using incorrect values for refractive indices (n1 or n2).
Using degrees instead of radians in trigonometric functions.
Misinterpreting θ1 or θ2 as complementary angles.

rules.title: Validate formula for critical angle
rules.description: The critical angle (θc) occurs when light is incident from a denser medium to a less dense medium, and total internal reflection occurs. The formula for the critical angle is θc = arcsin(n2 / n1), where n1 > n2.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the critical angle is calculated using θc = arcsin(n2 / n1) and that n1 > n2 is satisfied.
common_errors: Using n1 < n2 when applying the formula for critical angle.
Forgetting to use arcsin or incorrectly calculating it.
Calculating the critical angle for an incorrect medium pair.

rules.title: Check angle sign convention
rules.description: Angles of incidence and refraction are always measured relative to the normal to the interface. Positive angles should be used for both θ1 and θ2.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that θ1 and θ2 are measured relative to the normal and are positive values.
common_errors: Measuring angles from the surface instead of the normal.
Using negative angles for θ1 or θ2.

rules.title: Verify conditions for total internal reflection (TIR)
rules.description: Total internal reflection occurs only when light travels from a medium with a higher refractive index (n1) to a medium with a lower refractive index (n2), and the angle of incidence (θ1) exceeds the critical angle (θc).
rules.check_logic: Check if n1 > n2 and θ1 > θc before concluding total internal reflection.
common_errors: Applying TIR when n1 < n2.
Using TIR incorrectly when θ1 is less than or equal to θc.
Confusing TIR with refraction.

rules.title: Check physical constraints on refractive indices
rules.description: Refractive indices (n) must always be greater than or equal to 1, as n = c/v, where c is the speed of light in a vacuum and v is the speed of light in the medium.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that n1 and n2 are ≥ 1 for all calculations involving Snell's Law or the critical angle.
common_errors: Using refractive indices less than 1.
Mixing up speed of light in the medium with speed of light in a vacuum.

rules.title: Ensure dimensional consistency of trigonometric functions
rules.description: The arguments of trigonometric functions (sin, cos, tan) must be dimensionless. Angles should be either in radians or degrees, depending on the calculator or system setup.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that arguments passed to sin(θ1) and sin(θ2) are dimensionless and consistent with the chosen unit system (radians or degrees).
common_errors: Using angles with incorrect units or dimensions.
Mixing radians and degrees in the same calculation.

rules.title: Check validity conditions for applying Snell's Law
rules.description: Snell's Law is valid only for isotropic, homogeneous, and transparent media. It does not apply to scattering, absorption, or birefringent media.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the media involved are isotropic, homogeneous, and transparent before applying Snell's Law.
common_errors: Applying Snell's Law to anisotropic or birefringent materials.
Ignoring scattering or absorption effects in the medium.

rules.title: Validate geometric constraints at the interface
rules.description: The angles of incidence and refraction must satisfy the boundary geometry, such that they lie on opposite sides of the normal at the interface.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that θ1 and θ2 are measured in accordance with the boundary geometry and lie on opposite sides of the normal.
common_errors: Placing θ1 and θ2 on the same side of the normal.
Misidentifying the normal or interface geometry.

rules.title: Verify critical angle calculation
rules.description: The critical angle is determined using Snell's Law when light moves from a medium with a higher refractive index to one with a lower refractive index. The critical angle is given by sin(θ_critical) = n2/n1, where n1 > n2.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that sin(θ_critical) = n2/n1, verify that n1 > n2, and confirm that the angle is calculated in consistent units (radians or degrees).
common_errors: Swapping n1 and n2 in the formula.
Using n1 < n2, which makes total internal reflection impossible.
Forgetting to ensure angles are in radians or degrees consistently.

rules.title: Confirm Snell's Law application before total internal reflection
rules.description: Snell's Law states that n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2). Verify that this relationship holds for angles below the critical angle.
rules.check_logic: Check if n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2) for θ1 < θ_critical. Ensure that trigonometric functions are applied correctly and that refractive indices are accurate.
common_errors: Incorrectly applying Snell's Law when θ1 > θ_critical.
Using incorrect trigonometric functions (e.g., using cos instead of sin).
Miscalculating the angle or refractive indices.

rules.title: Verify angle of incidence exceeds critical angle
rules.description: Total internal reflection only occurs when the angle of incidence (θ1) is greater than the critical angle (θ_critical).
rules.check_logic: Confirm that θ1 > θ_critical before assuming total internal reflection occurs. Ensure the critical angle is calculated correctly beforehand.
common_errors: Assuming total internal reflection when θ1 < θ_critical.
Not calculating or verifying the critical angle before analyzing the situation.

rules.title: Check refractive index constraints for total internal reflection
rules.description: Total internal reflection is only possible if light passes from a medium with a higher refractive index (n1) into a medium with a lower refractive index (n2).
rules.check_logic: Ensure that n1 > n2. If n1 <= n2, total internal reflection cannot occur. Verify the direction of light propagation.
common_errors: Applying total internal reflection when light moves from a lower refractive index medium to a higher refractive index medium.
Neglecting to specify the direction of light propagation.

rules.title: Verify energy conservation during total internal reflection
rules.description: During total internal reflection, no energy is transmitted into the second medium, and all the light is reflected back into the first medium. This implies total reflectance.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that the transmitted intensity is zero and reflected intensity equals the incident intensity. Ensure no energy is lost during the process.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming partial transmission occurs during total internal reflection.
Failing to equate reflected intensity to incident intensity.

rules.title: Check for phase shift during total internal reflection
rules.description: During total internal reflection, a phase shift occurs at the boundary, depending on polarization and angle of incidence. This phase shift does not affect energy conservation.
rules.check_logic: Verify that a phase shift is considered when analyzing reflected waves during total internal reflection. Ensure the phase shift is not confused with energy loss.
common_errors: Ignoring the phase shift introduced during reflection.
Confusing phase shift with energy loss, which does not occur.

rules.title: Confirm dimensional consistency in equations
rules.description: Ensure that all terms in equations related to total internal reflection have consistent dimensions or units. For example, angles should be in radians or degrees consistently, and refractive indices are dimensionless.
rules.check_logic: Verify that sin(θ), n1, and n2 are dimensionless and angle units are consistent. Ensure no unit mismatches in calculations.
common_errors: Mixing radians and degrees when calculating angles.
Using refractive indices with incorrect or inconsistent dimensions.

rules.title: Verify geometric path consistency
rules.description: The geometry of the incident and reflected rays must satisfy boundary conditions. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection during total internal reflection.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that θ_incidence = θ_reflection and that the reflected ray lies entirely within the first medium. Confirm that the geometry aligns with total internal reflection principles.
common_errors: Setting θ_incidence ≠ θ_reflection.
Placing the reflected ray in the second medium, which contradicts total internal reflection.

rules.title: Verify polarization effects during total internal reflection
rules.description: During total internal reflection, the polarization of light can affect the phase shift and intensity distribution. This is particularly important for polarized light.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that polarization effects are considered, especially for s-polarized and p-polarized light. Verify that the phase shift is calculated correctly for each polarization type.
common_errors: Ignoring the impact of polarization on phase shift.
Failing to distinguish between s-polarized and p-polarized light.

rules.title: Verify wavefront continuity equation
rules.description: Huygens' Principle states that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical wavelets, and the new wavefront is the tangential surface to these secondary wavelets. Verify that the wavefront equation matches this principle.
rules.check_logic: Check if the secondary wavelets are drawn as spherical or plane waves (based on medium properties) and whether the tangent to these wavelets forms the next wavefront. Ensure that the wavelets are spaced consistently with the speed of propagation in the medium.
common_errors: Not drawing the secondary wavelets at all.
Incorrect tangent drawn to wavelets misrepresenting the wavefront.
Wavelets not spaced consistently with the speed of propagation in the medium.

rules.title: Check wavefront propagation speed consistency
rules.description: The speed at which wavefronts propagate depends on the properties of the medium (e.g., refractive index). Verify that the wavefront speed is consistent with the equation v = c/n, where n is the refractive index of the medium.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the wavefront spacing corresponds to v = c/n, where c is the speed of light in vacuum and n is the refractive index. Confirm that the refractive index used matches the medium described in the problem.
common_errors: Incorrect wavefront spacing relative to medium speed.
Using the wrong refractive index for the specified medium.
Forgetting that c is only valid in vacuum and not adjusting for n.

rules.title: Verify applicability of Huygens' Principle
rules.description: Huygens' Principle is valid for isotropic and homogeneous media. It cannot be directly applied to anisotropic or inhomogeneous media without modifications. Ensure that the problem context satisfies these conditions.
rules.check_logic: Check if the medium is isotropic (properties same in all directions) and homogeneous (properties constant throughout the medium). If the medium is anisotropic or inhomogeneous, verify that appropriate modifications to Huygens' Principle are applied.
common_errors: Applying Huygens' Principle to anisotropic media without justification.
Ignoring inhomogeneities in the medium that affect wavefront propagation.
Assuming medium properties are constant when they are explicitly variable.

rules.title: Ensure dimensional consistency in wavefront equations
rules.description: In the equations governing wavefronts, such as v = c/n or relationships between wavelength and frequency, all terms must have consistent units. Ensure that dimensions match for speed, refractive index, and other quantities.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the units of speed, refractive index, and wavelength-frequency relations are consistent across calculations. Ensure that derived quantities, such as wavefront spacing, are dimensionally correct.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for speed (e.g., mixing m/s with cm/s).
Forgetting that refractive index is unitless.
Mismatched wavelength and frequency units causing errors in derived values.

rules.title: Verify wavefront geometry based on source type
rules.description: Wavefronts from a point source are spherical, while wavefronts from a distant source are planar. Ensure that the wavefront geometry matches the source description.
rules.check_logic: Check if the wavefronts are spherical for point sources and planar for distant sources, or conform to any specific source geometry mentioned in the problem. Verify that the curvature of spherical wavefronts is consistent with the distance from the source.
common_errors: Drawing planar wavefronts for a nearby point source.
Incorrect curvature of spherical wavefronts.
Ignoring the wavefront geometry in calculations.

rules.title: Verify wavefront bending at boundaries
rules.description: When a wavefront passes from one medium to another, it bends according to Snell's Law. Verify that the bending of the wavefront at the boundary satisfies the relationship n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2).
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the angles of incidence and refraction follow Snell's Law and that the wavefront orientation changes accordingly. Verify that the refractive indices used correspond to the respective media.
common_errors: Incorrect calculation of refraction angles.
Ignoring the refractive index difference between media.
Wavefronts drawn at incorrect angles post-refraction.

rules.title: Check for wavefront diffraction at obstacles
rules.description: Wavefronts bend around obstacles, creating diffraction effects. Ensure that the wavefronts are drawn bending into the region of the geometric shadow when diffraction is significant.
rules.check_logic: Verify that wavefronts are not drawn as straight lines extending through an obstacle and correctly represent bending at edges. Confirm that the extent of diffraction matches the size of the obstacle and the wavelength of the wave.
common_errors: Ignoring diffraction effects entirely.
Drawing wavefronts as straight lines through the obstacle.
Incorrect representation of wave bending at sharp edges.

rules.title: Ensure consistency in coordinate system and sign conventions
rules.description: In problems involving wavefronts and Huygens' Principle, ensure that the coordinate system and sign conventions (e.g., positive directions for angles and distances) are consistently applied.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all angles, distances, and directions are consistently measured with respect to the chosen coordinate system. Ensure that sign conventions are explicitly stated and followed throughout the solution.
common_errors: Switching between different coordinate systems mid-solution.
Using inconsistent sign conventions for angles or distances.
Confusion between clockwise and counterclockwise angle directions.

rules.title: Verify wavefront superposition in overlapping regions
rules.description: When wavefronts from multiple sources overlap, the resulting wavefront is determined by the principle of superposition. Ensure that the combined wavefront is correctly represented.
rules.check_logic: Check if the resultant wavefront is drawn as the constructive or destructive interference of overlapping wavefronts, depending on their phase relationship.
common_errors: Ignoring the effects of superposition in overlapping regions.
Incorrectly representing constructive or destructive interference.
Failing to account for phase differences between overlapping wavefronts.

rules.title: Verify Young's Double-Slit Equation
rules.description: Ensure the equation for determining constructive and destructive interference in Young's Double-Slit experiment is correctly used: d*sin(θ) = m*λ for constructive interference and d*sin(θ) = (m+1/2)*λ for destructive interference. Here, d is the slit separation, θ is the angle to the maxima/minima, m is the order of the fringe, and λ is the wavelength.
rules.check_logic: Check if d*sin(θ) is equal to m*λ for constructive interference or (m+1/2)*λ for destructive interference. Ensure all variables are defined, consistent, and correctly substituted.
common_errors: Using m*λ for destructive interference instead of (m+1/2)*λ.
Incorrect substitution of slit separation (d) or wavelength (λ).
Forgetting to calculate the sine of the angle θ.

rules.title: Check Path Difference for Interference
rules.description: Verify that the path difference between the two waves is correctly calculated as ΔL = d*sin(θ). This path difference determines whether the interference is constructive or destructive.
rules.check_logic: Check if the path difference ΔL is computed as d*sin(θ) and used consistently in subsequent calculations. Ensure the relationship between ΔL and interference type is correctly applied.
common_errors: Path difference calculated incorrectly, e.g., using d*cos(θ) instead of d*sin(θ).
Missing or wrong sign conventions for angles in the calculation.
Not accounting for the order of the fringe (m).

rules.title: Verify Phase Shift in Thin Film Interference
rules.description: In thin-film interference, ensure that the phase shift of π (or λ/2 path difference) is correctly applied when light reflects off a medium of higher refractive index. This phase shift affects whether constructive or destructive interference occurs.
rules.check_logic: Check if a phase shift of λ/2 is added when reflection occurs at a higher refractive index boundary and validate its impact on the interference condition. Ensure the phase shifts for both reflections are correctly accounted for.
common_errors: Ignoring the phase shift when light reflects off a higher refractive index medium.
Incorrectly applying the phase shift for both reflections.
Misinterpreting the conditions for constructive and destructive interference due to phase shift.

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in Interference Equations
rules.description: Verify that all terms in the equations for interference (e.g., d*sin(θ) = m*λ) have consistent units: d and λ should be in the same unit (e.g., meters), and sin(θ) is dimensionless.
rules.check_logic: Check that slit separation (d) and wavelength (λ) are expressed in the same units and that the sine function has no units. Ensure any unit conversions are correctly performed.
common_errors: Using inconsistent units for d and λ (e.g., meters for d and nanometers for λ).
Forgetting to convert angles to radians if required for trigonometric functions.

rules.title: Validate Geometric Constraints in Young's Experiment
rules.description: Ensure that the geometric constraints of the experimental setup are adhered to, such as the screen distance (L) being much greater than the slit separation (d) for the small angle approximation (sin(θ) ≈ tan(θ) ≈ y/L) to hold.
rules.check_logic: Verify that L >> d and that the small angle approximation is applied only when θ is small (θ < 15 degrees approximately). Ensure that y (fringe displacement on the screen) and L are correctly calculated.
common_errors: Using sin(θ) ≈ tan(θ) when θ is not small.
Incorrectly calculating θ or y (fringe displacement on the screen).
Ignoring the condition L >> d.

rules.title: Validate Use of Refractive Indices in Thin Film Interference
rules.description: In thin-film interference, ensure that the refractive indices (n1, n2, n3) are correctly used to determine the effective wavelength within the medium (λ_medium = λ/n).
rules.check_logic: Check if the wavelength in the medium (λ/n) is correctly calculated using the medium's refractive index and if it is consistent with the interference conditions. Ensure the correct refractive index is used for each medium.
common_errors: Forgetting to modify the wavelength in the medium using λ/n.
Using the wrong refractive index for the medium.
Misinterpreting which medium is associated with which refractive index.

rules.title: Check Validity Conditions for Interference Equations
rules.description: Verify that the conditions for interference are met: the light source must be coherent and monochromatic, and the slits or thin film must allow for consistent path differences.
rules.check_logic: Check if the problem explicitly states or implies coherent and monochromatic light. Ensure that the slits or thin film are properly aligned and uniform. Verify that the experimental setup supports stable interference patterns.
common_errors: Attempting to use interference equations for incoherent or non-monochromatic light.
Ignoring misalignment or non-uniformity of the slits or thin film.

rules.title: Verify Sign Conventions for Path Differences
rules.description: Ensure that the path difference ΔL is correctly signed based on the geometry of the problem. The positive or negative sign of ΔL determines the type of interference (constructive or destructive).
rules.check_logic: Check if ΔL is correctly signed based on the relative path lengths of the two waves and if the sign convention is used consistently in calculations. Ensure the relationship between ΔL and interference type is clearly stated.
common_errors: Incorrectly assigning the sign of ΔL based on the geometry.
Using inconsistent sign conventions across multiple calculations.
Misinterpreting the relationship between path difference and interference type.

rules.title: Account for Multiple Reflections in Thin Film Interference
rules.description: Ensure that multiple reflections within the thin film are considered when calculating the overall interference pattern, especially for thicker films.
rules.check_logic: Verify if the problem accounts for additional phase shifts and path differences caused by multiple reflections within the thin film. Ensure that these contributions are included in the interference condition.
common_errors: Ignoring the effects of multiple reflections in thicker films.
Incorrectly summing the contributions of multiple reflected waves.
Overlooking phase shifts introduced by additional reflections.

rules.title: Verify the diffraction angle equation for single slit
