rules.title: Verify correct sign conventions for antiparticles
rules.description: Antiparticles have opposite quantum numbers (like charge, baryon number, lepton number) compared to their corresponding particles. Correctly account for these sign differences in calculations.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the quantum numbers assigned to antiparticles are the negation of their particle counterparts (e.g., positron has +1 charge, electron has -1).
common_errors: Assigning the same sign for charge or quantum numbers to particles and antiparticles.
Misidentifying the charge of neutral antiparticles like anti-neutrons.

rules.title: Check kinematic constraints for particle reactions
rules.description: Certain reactions or decays are forbidden if they violate kinematic constraints (e.g., insufficient energy, conservation of momentum). Verify if the reaction is energetically and kinematically allowed.
rules.check_logic: Calculate the rest energy and kinetic energy of all particles before and after the reaction. Ensure the total available energy is sufficient to produce the final state particles.
common_errors: Allowing reactions that require more energy than available.
Ignoring threshold energy requirements for pair production.
Neglecting the momentum conservation requirement.

rules.title: Verify applicability of conservation laws
rules.description: Some conservation laws (e.g., parity conservation, CP symmetry) apply only under specific conditions. Verify whether the situation allows the use of these conservation laws.
rules.check_logic: Check the nature of the interaction (e.g., strong, weak, electromagnetic) and ensure the chosen conservation law applies to that interaction type.
common_errors: Applying parity conservation to weak interactions (where it is violated).
Assuming CP symmetry holds universally without exceptions.

rules.title: Verify Einstein Field Equations (EFE) Consistency
rules.description: Check if Einstein Field Equations (EFE) are expressed correctly as Gμν = (8πG/c^4) Tμν, where Gμν is the Einstein tensor, G is Newton's gravitational constant, c is the speed of light, and Tμν is the stress-energy tensor.
rules.check_logic: Ensure Gμν is calculated as Rμν - 1/2(Rgμν), where Rμν is the Ricci tensor, R is the Ricci scalar, and gμν is the metric tensor. Verify that Tμν is appropriately defined for the given physical scenario, including energy density, momentum, and stress components.
common_errors: Incorrect or missing components of the Einstein tensor.
Forgetting the factor of 8πG/c^4 in the equation.
Misidentifying or incorrectly defining the stress-energy tensor for the system under analysis.

rules.title: Check Metric Sign Convention
rules.description: Ensure that the chosen metric follows a consistent sign convention. The most common conventions are (-+++), used in general relativity, or (+---).
rules.check_logic: Verify that the metric tensor components have the correct signs depending on the chosen convention and ensure consistency throughout the calculation.
common_errors: Mixing different sign conventions in a single calculation.
Incorrectly assigning the sign to the time component of the metric.
Failing to document the chosen convention explicitly.

rules.title: Validate Friedmann Equations
rules.description: The Friedmann equations describe the expansion of the universe and are derived from Einstein's Field Equations assuming a homogeneous and isotropic universe. Check if they are expressed as (a'/a)^2 = 8πGρ/3 - k/a^2 + Λ/3 and a''/a = -4πG(ρ + 3p)/3 + Λ/3.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the terms for density (ρ), curvature (k), pressure (p), and cosmological constant (Λ) are included, correctly positioned, and have consistent units. Ensure the equations are applied to a homogeneous and isotropic universe.
common_errors: Omitting the curvature (k) term in a spatially non-flat universe.
Incorrect placement or sign of the cosmological constant (Λ).
Using improper units for density or pressure.
Failing to account for time-dependent scale factor (a).

rules.title: Ensure Redshift Definition and Calculation are Correct
rules.description: Redshift (z) is defined as z = (λ_observed - λ_emitted) / λ_emitted. It quantifies the stretching of light due to the universe's expansion.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the formula for redshift is consistent and is used within the context of the Doppler effect or cosmological expansion. Verify that λ_observed and λ_emitted are measured or calculated correctly.
common_errors: Confusing redshift with blueshift (negative z for blueshift).
Using incorrect wavelengths for λ_observed or λ_emitted.
Applying redshift formula in scenarios where it is not appropriate, such as local systems.

rules.title: Verify Geodesic Equation for Particle Motion
rules.description: The geodesic equation describes the motion of particles in curved spacetime: d^2x^μ/dτ^2 + Γ^μ_νσ (dx^ν/dτ)(dx^σ/dτ) = 0. Check if this equation is used properly.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the Christoffel symbols Γ^μ_νσ are calculated correctly for the given metric and substituted appropriately. Verify that the equation is applied to the correct spacetime geometry.
common_errors: Omitting Christoffel symbols in curved spacetime.
Incorrect calculation of Christoffel symbols for the given metric.
Assuming straight-line motion in non-flat spacetime.
Failing to account for proper time (τ) in the equation.

rules.title: Check Dimensional Consistency in Cosmological Equations
rules.description: Ensure that all terms in equations (e.g., Einstein Field Equations, Friedmann Equations) have consistent physical dimensions.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all terms match the dimensions of curvature, energy density, or other relevant physical quantities. Ensure proper inclusion of factors like c, G, or Λ where necessary.
common_errors: Mismatching units for energy density (ρ) or pressure (p).
Forgetting to include factors of c, G, or Λ where necessary.
Using inconsistent units for time, length, or mass.

rules.title: Validate Hubble's Law Application
rules.description: Hubble's Law relates the recession velocity of galaxies to their distance: v = H0 × d, where H0 is the Hubble constant.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the correct value of H0 is used and that the relationship is applied only to galaxies within the observable universe. Verify relativistic corrections for high redshift galaxies if necessary.
common_errors: Using an outdated or incorrect value for the Hubble constant.
Applying Hubble's Law to local (non-expanding) systems.
Neglecting relativistic corrections for high redshift galaxies.

rules.title: Confirm Spatial Curvature Constraints
rules.description: The curvature term (k) in cosmology determines the geometry of the universe: k = 0 (flat), k > 0 (closed), k < 0 (open). Ensure its value is consistent with the given observations or model.
rules.check_logic: Verify that k is correctly identified and used in equations like the Friedmann equations. Ensure observational data is interpreted correctly to determine k.
common_errors: Using the wrong curvature sign for the described universe geometry.
Omitting the curvature term entirely in non-flat models.
Misinterpreting observational data to determine k.

rules.title: Verify Application of the Cosmological Principle
rules.description: The cosmological principle assumes that the universe is homogeneous and isotropic on large scales. Ensure this assumption is valid for the given analysis.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the assumption of homogeneity and isotropy is consistent with the scale of the analysis. Check if deviations from this principle are accounted for in smaller-scale models.
common_errors: Applying the cosmological principle to scales where inhomogeneities dominate.
Failing to account for anisotropies or local deviations in smaller-scale models.
Misinterpreting observational data to support homogeneity or isotropy.

rules.title: Verify correct formula application for absolute, relative, and percentage errors
rules.description: The relationships between absolute error, relative error, and percentage error are fundamental. Absolute error is the difference between the measured and true values. Relative error is the ratio of the absolute error to the true value, while percentage error is the relative error multiplied by 100.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the student uses: Relative Error = Absolute Error / True Value and Percentage Error = Relative Error * 100. Verify that the true value is not zero to avoid division errors.
common_errors: Confusing relative error and absolute error formulas
Omitting the multiplication by 100 for percentage error
Using measured value instead of true value in relative error calculation
Dividing by zero when true value is zero

rules.title: Check sign conventions in error calculation
rules.description: Errors are always positive by convention, as they represent the magnitude of deviation. Subtraction to calculate errors must not yield a negative result.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all reported error values are positive, regardless of whether the measured value is higher or lower than the true value. If a negative value is reported, ensure it is corrected to its absolute value.
common_errors: Reporting negative values for absolute error
Incorrect sign when subtracting true value from measured value

rules.title: Ensure validity of error analysis assumptions
rules.description: Error analysis assumes that the true value is known or reasonably estimated, and that the measurement process is unbiased and repeatable. These conditions must be satisfied for the calculated errors to be meaningful.
rules.check_logic: Check if the problem provides a true value or a reliable estimate. If not, errors cannot be computed. Verify that the measurement process is described as unbiased and repeatable.
common_errors: Computing relative error or percentage error without a true value
Ignoring the need for repeatability in measurements
Assuming a biased measurement process is valid for error analysis

rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency in error formulas
rules.description: Absolute error, relative error, and percentage error have specific dimensional requirements. Absolute error must have the same units as the quantity being measured. Relative error and percentage error are dimensionless.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that absolute error has the same units as the measured value, and relative and percentage errors are unitless. Verify that unit conversions, if any, are correctly applied.
common_errors: Using mismatched units for absolute error and measured value
Reporting relative or percentage errors with units
Failing to convert units when necessary for consistency

rules.title: Check error propagation rules for addition and multiplication
rules.description: When combining quantities with errors, specific rules apply: for addition/subtraction, absolute errors are added; for multiplication/division, relative errors are added.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that for addition/subtraction, the total error is the sum of absolute errors. For multiplication/division, the total error is the sum of relative errors. Verify that the correct error type is used for the operation.
common_errors: Using relative errors for addition/subtraction
Using absolute errors for multiplication/division
Forgetting to convert relative error to percentage error or vice versa when required

rules.title: Verify the significance of percentage error
rules.description: Percentage error quantifies the significance of the error relative to the true value. A high percentage error implies low accuracy, while a low percentage error indicates high accuracy.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the student interprets percentage error correctly in terms of accuracy and significance. Verify that percentage error is compared to a benchmark or threshold for meaningful interpretation.
common_errors: Misinterpreting a high percentage error as high accuracy
Failing to compare percentage error to a benchmark or threshold for significance

rules.title: Ensure error values are consistent with the coordinate system
rules.description: When dealing with vector quantities, errors in different components (e.g., x, y, z) must be treated independently unless combined to find total error using geometric addition.
rules.check_logic: Verify that errors in vector components are combined using the Pythagorean theorem when calculating total error. Ensure that directional components are not ignored in vector error analysis.
common_errors: Adding vector component errors directly without squaring and summing
Ignoring directional components in vector error analysis

rules.title: Check for appropriate rounding in error reporting
rules.description: Errors should be reported with an appropriate number of significant figures, usually matching the precision of the measurement instrument.
rules.check_logic: Ensure errors are rounded to the same decimal place or significant figure as the original measurement. Verify that rounding is consistent across all reported values.
common_errors: Over-reporting precision in error values
Rounding errors inconsistently with the original data
Using different rounding rules for similar measurements

rules.title: Ensure proper format for error reporting
rules.description: Errors should be reported in a clear and standardized format, typically as ± the error value alongside the measured value.
rules.check_logic: Verify that errors are reported in the format: Measured Value ± Error. Ensure that the error value is appropriately rounded and matches the precision of the measured value.
common_errors: Reporting errors without the ± symbol
Inconsistent formatting of error values
Mismatch between the precision of the error and the measured value

rules.title: Verify correct application of uncertainty propagation formula
rules.description: Ensure that the formula for uncertainty propagation is correctly used: for functions f(x, y, ...), the uncertainty is calculated as sqrt((df/dx * Δx)^2 + (df/dy * Δy)^2 + ...). This applies to measurements where uncertainties in variables contribute independently.
rules.check_logic: Check if the partial derivatives of the function are correctly calculated, squared, and summed correctly.
common_errors: Omitting a term in the uncertainty propagation formula.
Using addition instead of summing squares and taking the square root.
Incorrect calculation of partial derivatives.

rules.title: Ensure correct sign conventions in uncertainty propagation
rules.description: Uncertainty propagation does not depend on the sign of the partial derivatives but only on their magnitudes. Use absolute values where necessary.
rules.check_logic: Verify if the absolute values of partial derivatives are used in uncertainty propagation.
common_errors: Incorrectly incorporating the sign of a derivative into the uncertainty calculation.
Failing to apply absolute value to the derivative terms.

rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency in propagated uncertainties
rules.description: Ensure that the units of the propagated uncertainty match the units of the function output, making the uncertainties physically meaningful.
rules.check_logic: Check if the units of the propagated uncertainty align with the units of the function output.
common_errors: Mismatch between the units of the propagated uncertainty and the function output.
Failing to account for unit conversions in complex functions.

rules.title: Check independence assumption for uncertainty propagation
rules.description: Uncertainty propagation assumes variables are independent. If variables are correlated, include a covariance term.
rules.check_logic: Verify if covariance terms are included when variables are not independent.
common_errors: Applying the standard uncertainty propagation formula to correlated variables without including covariance terms.
Incorrectly assuming independence in a system where variables are coupled.

rules.title: Ensure geometric constraints are respected in uncertainty calculations
rules.description: In geometric measurements (e.g., angles, lengths), propagate uncertainty respecting any geometric constraints (e.g., sum of angles in a triangle).
rules.check_logic: Check if the propagated uncertainties respect geometric constraints such as angles summing to 180 degrees in a triangle.
common_errors: Neglecting to apply geometric constraints to the uncertainty results.
Failing to consider fixed relationships among variables in uncertainty propagation.

rules.title: Verify significance of propagated uncertainty
rules.description: Ensure uncertainty values remain significant relative to the measurement values. Excessively large uncertainties may indicate lack of precision.
rules.check_logic: Compare the uncertainty to the magnitude of the measured quantity. Flag cases where the uncertainty is disproportionately large.
common_errors: Failing to flag cases where uncertainties dominate the measurement.
Overlooking the need to re-evaluate measurement precision.

rules.title: Check validity of linear approximation in uncertainty propagation
rules.description: Uncertainty propagation uses a linear approximation valid only when uncertainties are small relative to the function's scale.
rules.check_logic: Evaluate whether relative uncertainties in variables are small enough to justify using a linear approximation.
common_errors: Applying uncertainty propagation formulas when relative uncertainties are too large.
Failing to verify linearity of the function in the range of uncertainties.

rules.title: Ensure correct combination of relative and absolute uncertainties
rules.description: When combining different uncertainties (e.g., relative and absolute), ensure correct methods are used for addition or propagation.
rules.check_logic: Check if relative uncertainties are converted to absolute uncertainties (or vice versa) where necessary before combination.
common_errors: Adding relative and absolute uncertainties directly without conversion.
Failing to distinguish between relative and absolute uncertainties when combining.

rules.title: Preserving Significant Figures in Addition/Subtraction
rules.description: Ensure that the result of an addition or subtraction retains the least number of decimal places of any number involved in the calculation. This rule helps maintain the precision of the measurement.
rules.check_logic: Identify the number with the fewest decimal places in the operation and round the result to match that precision. Ensure intermediate calculations do not introduce additional decimal places.
common_errors: Using more decimal places than warranted by the least precise number
Incorrectly rounding off intermediate calculations

rules.title: Preserving Significant Figures in Multiplication/Division
rules.description: Ensure the result of a multiplication or division retains the smallest number of significant figures of any number involved in the calculation.
rules.check_logic: Identify the number with the least significant figures in the operation and round the result to match that precision. Avoid introducing additional significant figures during intermediate steps.
common_errors: Using more significant figures than warranted
Ignoring significant figures in intermediate calculations

rules.title: Correct Rounding of Significant Figures
rules.description: Apply proper rounding rules when a calculated result needs adjustment to match the required number of significant figures, ensuring no bias over multiple operations.
rules.check_logic: Round up if the digit past the last significant figure is 5 or greater, round down otherwise. Ensure rounding is applied consistently across all steps of the calculation.
common_errors: Rounding all digits up without considering specific rounding thresholds
Incorrectly rounding leading to precision loss

rules.title: Dimensional and Unit Consistency Check
rules.description: Ensure that units are consistent and correctly maintained in a calculation involving significant figures, and that the final result retains proper physical meaning.
rules.check_logic: Verify units before applying significant figures rules to ensure dimensional correctness. Perform unit conversions where necessary before applying significant figure rules.
common_errors: Applying significant figure rules without checking unit consistency
Ignoring unit conversions affecting significant figures

rules.title: Validity of Significant Figures Application
rules.description: Check whether significant figures are applicable depending on whether the parameters originate from measured data or pure mathematical constants.
rules.check_logic: Only apply significant figures rules to measured data, not to exact numbers or defined constants. Ensure constants are treated with their full precision unless otherwise specified.
common_errors: Applying significant figures to exact or defined numbers erroneously
Ignoring significant figures in measured data inputs

rules.title: Truncation Error Analysis
rules.description: Determine if truncation has led to significant loss of precision and whether significant figures have been correctly applied.
rules.check_logic: Assess if truncation has changed the result significantly when compared to more precise calculations. Avoid premature truncation in intermediate steps.
common_errors: Excessive truncation leading to significant loss of information
Disregarding small contributions by prematurely truncating digits

rules.title: Propagation of Error in Significant Figures
rules.description: Analyze how errors in significant figures propagate through multi-step calculations and ensure that the resulting significant figures reflect the compounded effect.
rules.check_logic: Modify significant figures based on the propagation rules and cumulative effect from sequential calculations. Ensure the final result reflects the compounded uncertainty.
common_errors: Ignoring error propagation effect in multi-step calculations
Misapplying rules leading to underestimated error impacts

rules.title: Significant Figures in Geometric Constraints
rules.description: Ensure geometric constraint calculations accurately reflect changes in significant figures depending on dimensional considerations.
rules.check_logic: Assess and maintain dimensional precision according to constraints set by geometry and measurement scales. Ensure that derived quantities (e.g., area, volume) reflect the correct significant figures based on input measurements.
common_errors: Failing to recognize significant figure changes due to geometric relationships
Overlooking dimensional impacts on precision

rules.title: Significant Figures in Logarithmic and Exponential Calculations
rules.description: Ensure that significant figures are correctly applied in logarithmic and exponential calculations, where the number of significant figures in the result depends on the precision of the input.
rules.check_logic: For logarithms, the number of decimal places in the result should match the number of significant figures in the input. For exponentials, the number of significant figures in the result should match the precision of the input.
common_errors: Incorrectly determining the number of decimal places in logarithmic results
Failing to match significant figures in exponential results to input precision

rules.title: Ensure Correct Data Transformation for Logarithmic Scales
rules.description: Logarithmic scales require data that is positive and spans several orders of magnitude. The transformation typically involves the logarithm (base 10 or natural log) of the original data values.
rules.check_logic: Verify all data points are positive and span several orders of magnitude before applying a logarithmic transformation. Confirm the appropriate choice of logarithm base (common or natural).
common_errors: Attempting to log-transform zero or negative values
Choosing an incorrect base for the logarithm transformation

rules.title: Verify Unit Consistency in Graphical Representation
rules.description: Units must remain consistent throughout the dataset, and correct units should be represented on the axes. For logarithmic scales, ensure logs of dimensionless quantities or ratios are consistent.
rules.check_logic: Check that units on axes are consistent and appropriately labeled. Ensure dimensionless variables or correctly dimensioned ratios are used in logarithmic transformations.
common_errors: Mislabeling axes with incorrect units
Logarithm of a variable with dimensions not appropriately handled

rules.title: Validate Linear Regression Application
rules.description: Linear regression should only be applied when data naturally forms a straight line or can be transformed to do so. Inspect for linear trends and absence of systematic deviations.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the dataset's behavior suggests a linear relationship, either intrinsically or through suitable transformations. Examine residuals for systematic deviations.
common_errors: Incorrect assumption of linear relationship in inherently nonlinear data
Ignoring residuals that indicate poor fit

rules.title: Ensure Validity for Logarithmic Plot Usage
rules.description: Logarithmic plots are suited for data following power laws, exponential growth, and other multiplicative phenomena. The data must cover several orders of magnitude.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that the dataset spans multiple orders of magnitude and the underlying phenomena justify a logarithmic plot, such as power law or exponential behavior.
common_errors: Using logarithmic plots for data that varies linearly
Failing to confirm phenomenon matches power law or exponential behavior

rules.title: Ensure Proper Axis Sign Convention
rules.description: Axes must properly represent the inherent sign conventions with respect to data. Coordinate systems should be consistently applied and labeled correctly.
rules.check_logic: Ensure axes are labeled with the correct sign conventions and directionality is accurately represented across the plot.
common_errors: Labeling the wrong direction for data trends
Ignoring negative values in contexts where they are valid

rules.title: Check Integration of Error Bars in Graphical Data
rules.description: Error bars indicate measurement uncertainty and must be included for accuracy unless proven negligible. They should give clear visual insight into the reliability of represented data.
rules.check_logic: Confirm error bars are present for datasets where measurement variability exists, and verify their scale and representation are appropriate.
common_errors: Failing to include error bars in graphs
Misrepresenting the scale or size of error bars

rules.title: Conduct Dimensional Analysis on Plotted Parameters
rules.description: All parameters plotted should be dimensionally consistent, ensuring derived quantities follow coherent dimensional rules.
rules.check_logic: Verify dimensional consistency across plotted data and confirm that derived scales, like logarithmic, maintain proper unit coherence.
common_errors: Plotting dimensionally inconsistent quantities against one another
Overlooking units during dimensional transformation (especially logarithmic)

rules.title: Address Zero Handling in Logarithmic Plots
rules.description: Logarithmic transformations cannot handle zero values. Ensure data preprocessing addresses any zero values appropriately, such as using log1p or adding small offsets.
rules.check_logic: Verify that zero values are handled correctly before log transformation through methods like adding a constant or using log1p for natural logs.
common_errors: Applying logarithmic transformation directly to zero values
Neglecting to preprocess zero values in datasets

rules.title: Ensure the regression model matches the expected equation form
rules.description: Verify that the chosen regression model (linear, quadratic, exponential, etc.) aligns with the physical principles governing the underlying experimental data. For example, linear regression is suitable for a linear trend, while exponential regression is appropriate for decay processes.
rules.check_logic: Check if the functional form of the regression model matches the anticipated theoretical or experimental relationship, referencing existing literature or theoretical models.
common_errors: Using a linear model for non-linear data trends.
Choosing a higher-order polynomial unnecessarily, leading to overfitting.
Ignoring the underlying physics to select the regression model.

rules.title: Verify unit consistency in regression parameters
rules.description: Ensure that the coefficients and constants in the regression equation have physically consistent units when interpreting the model or equation. The units of the dependent variable must match the computed units from the regression equation.
rules.check_logic: Verify the dimensional consistency of terms in the regression equation by performing unit analysis.
common_errors: Assigning unitless coefficients to terms with units.
Mismatching units due to inconsistent data scaling or transformations.
Failing to check the units of derived regression constants.

rules.title: Analyze residuals to ensure model adequacy
rules.description: Residuals should be randomly distributed around zero. If they exhibit non-random patterns (e.g., systematic trends or clustering), it indicates the model is inadequate for the data.
rules.check_logic: Perform a residual plot analysis and check for randomness by examining whether residuals show systematic deviations or patterns.
common_errors: Interpreting systematic patterns as noise.
Ignoring large residuals that indicate poor model fitting.
Failing to examine residuals in nonlinear models.

rules.title: Evaluate goodness-of-fit metrics
rules.description: Verify the model's fit to the data using metrics such as R-squared, adjusted R-squared, or reduced chi-squared, ensuring they meet the acceptable thresholds without being artificially inflated by overfitting.
rules.check_logic: Compute and interpret goodness-of-fit metrics. Ensure they indicate a sufficient fit by evaluating them alongside residual analysis.
common_errors: Misinterpreting R-squared as a sole indicator of fit quality.
Relying on adjusted R-squared without considering residual analysis.
Overfitting the model to maximize R-squared.

rules.title: Ensure correct data transformations
rules.description: Verify that any transformations (e.g., logarithmic, reciprocal) applied to the data are appropriate and consistent with the underlying physics.
rules.check_logic: Validate that the transformation is justified by the theoretical model or experimental setup. Cross-examine transformations with the expected outcomes.
common_errors: Applying transformations without justification.
Failing to revert transformations when interpreting results.
Using inconsistent transformation methods for different variables.

rules.title: Account for measurement uncertainties in regression
rules.description: Ensure that measurement uncertainties in the dependent and independent variables are incorporated into the regression analysis, where applicable. Consider weighted regression if uncertainties are non-uniform.
rules.check_logic: Ensure uncertainties are included in the regression analysis and that weights are applied correctly based on uncertainty quantification.
common_errors: Ignoring measurement uncertainties in fitting.
Incorrectly weighting data points with smaller uncertainties.
Failing to propagate errors through transformed variables.

rules.title: Check boundary and limiting conditions
rules.description: Verify that the regression model satisfies known boundary or limiting cases of the physical system. For example, a linear model should pass through the origin if the system requires it.
rules.check_logic: Compare the regression model's behavior at boundaries with the expected behavior based on theory or previous experimental data.
common_errors: Forgetting to enforce boundary conditions in the model.
Using regression models that yield non-physical results at limits.
Ignoring known asymptotic behavior in the data.

rules.title: Ensure proper sign conventions and coordinate system usage
rules.description: Verify that the regression analysis respects the sign conventions and coordinate systems defined in the experimental setup. Misaligned conventions can lead to incorrect parameter interpretation.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that regression parameters align with the selected coordinate system and sign conventions, ensuring consistency across the analysis.
common_errors: Misinterpreting the sign of slope or intercept in a linear regression.
Ignoring coordinate system transformations before fitting the data.
Failing to standardize sign conventions across all variables.

rules.title: Check for multicollinearity in regression analysis
rules.description: Verify that the independent variables in the regression model are not excessively correlated, as multicollinearity can affect the reliability of the parameter estimates.
rules.check_logic: Identify and assess multicollinearity using variance inflation factors or correlation coefficients among independent variables.
common_errors: Overlooking multicollinearity among predictors that can inflate standard errors.
Interpreting correlation without accounting for combined predictive effects.
Failing to diagnose multicollinearity in complex models with multiple predictors.

rules.title: Ensure measurement equation consistency
rules.description: Verify if the equation or formula used aligns with the measurement being conducted. For example, using a ruler to measure length aligns with linear distance measurements, while a stopwatch applies to time.
rules.check_logic: Check if the chosen method or device corresponds to the physical quantity being measured (e.g., mass measured with a balance, length measured with a ruler or caliper). Ensure the measurement method is appropriate for the physical property being quantified.
common_errors: Using a stopwatch to measure distance directly
Using a balance to determine volume without converting mass and density.

rules.title: Ensure unit and dimensional consistency
rules.description: Verify that all physical quantities and derived results follow dimensional consistency. Units for length, time, and mass must correspond to their respective SI or chosen systems.
rules.check_logic: For any derived result, verify that the dimensions match the expected outcome (e.g., velocity = length/time, density = mass/volume). Ensure unit conversions are performed correctly when necessary.
common_errors: Adding or subtracting quantities with different units
Forgetting to convert units to a common system before solving.
Reporting time in meters or mass in seconds.

rules.title: Check adherence to sign conventions
rules.description: Ensure proper sign conventions are followed, especially when using coordinate systems or directional measurements (e.g., positive direction for length or displacement).
rules.check_logic: Verify if measurements taken in opposite directions are assigned opposite signs in the coordinate system (e.g., left as negative, right as positive). Ensure the reference point or coordinate origin is clearly defined.
common_errors: Assigning the same sign to measurements in opposite directions
Ignoring the reference point or coordinate origin.

rules.title: Verify precision and accuracy adherence
rules.description: Check if the measurement tool used has adequate precision for the required measurement and if the results are within expected tolerances.
rules.check_logic: Verify if the instrument error or least count is recorded and if the measurement's uncertainty is accounted for in the final result. Ensure results are not rounded off prematurely.
common_errors: Ignoring the least count of measurement tools
Rounding off results before the final step of calculation
Exceeding the precision limit of the instrument.

rules.title: Account for environmental conditions
rules.description: Ensure that environmental factors such as temperature, pressure, and humidity, which may affect the measurement, are controlled or accounted for.
rules.check_logic: Check if the experimental setup mentions controlling or accounting for environmental variables that can impact the measurement (e.g., thermal expansion affecting length measurements). Verify if corrections for environmental effects are applied where necessary.
common_errors: Ignoring thermal expansion in metal rulers
Neglecting air buoyancy corrections for mass measurements
Performing measurements at varying temperatures without noting the change.

rules.title: Verify instrument calibration
rules.description: Check if the measurement instruments are calibrated correctly before use. Calibration ensures the instrument provides accurate readings.
rules.check_logic: Verify if calibration procedures are mentioned and applied (e.g., zeroing a balance, calibrating a stopwatch). Ensure calibration is performed at regular intervals or before critical measurements.
common_errors: Using uncalibrated equipment for precise measurements
Ignoring the need to zero the instrument before measurement.

rules.title: Check for repeated trials and averaging
rules.description: Verify if measurements were taken multiple times and averaged to minimize random errors.
rules.check_logic: Check if the experiment states repeated trials and if the final result is an average value. Ensure the number of trials is sufficient to reduce random errors significantly.
common_errors: Relying on a single measurement without replication
Not averaging multiple trials to reduce error.

rules.title: Ensure geometric constraints in measurement
rules.description: Confirm that the geometric alignment of the measurement tool aligns with the property being measured (e.g., placing a ruler properly along the object).
rules.check_logic: Check if the tool orientation matches the required measurement (e.g., perpendicular placement of a caliper for diameter, parallel placement of a ruler for length). Ensure corrections are applied for curved or irregular surfaces.
common_errors: Placing the measurement tool at an incorrect angle
Measuring a curved length with a straight ruler without correction.

rules.title: Ensure proper data recording and documentation
rules.description: Verify that all measurements are recorded systematically and with sufficient detail to allow reproducibility.
rules.check_logic: Check if the recorded data includes units, uncertainty, and conditions under which the measurement was taken. Ensure no data points are omitted or misrepresented.
common_errors: Failing to record units alongside measurements
Omitting uncertainty or environmental conditions in the data
Recording data in an inconsistent or unclear format.

rules.title: Verify dynamic measurement techniques
rules.description: Ensure that appropriate methods are used for measurements involving moving objects or changing conditions.
rules.check_logic: Check if the measurement technique accounts for motion or time-dependent changes (e.g., using high-speed cameras for fast events, or averaging over time for fluctuating quantities).
common_errors: Using static measurement tools for dynamic systems
Ignoring time-dependent variations in the measurement.

topics.name: Use of Vernier Calipers and Micrometers

rules.title: Verify zero error in Vernier Calipers
rules.description: Ensure that the Vernier calipers are checked for zero error before taking any measurements. Zero error can be positive or negative, depending on whether the zero of the Vernier scale aligns with or deviates from the main scale zero.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the student has recorded the zero error by observing the alignment of the Vernier and main scale zeros. Ensure the necessary correction (subtract positive zero error or add negative zero error) is applied to the final measurement.
common_errors: Not checking for zero error before measuring.
Incorrectly identifying the type of zero error (positive vs negative).
Forgetting to apply the zero error correction to the final measurement.

rules.title: Validate least count calculation for Vernier Calipers
rules.description: The least count of Vernier calipers is determined by the difference in values between one main scale division and one Vernier scale division. It is typically calculated as LC = MSD - VSD.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the least count is correctly calculated using the provided scale divisions (e.g., MSD = 1 mm, VSD = 0.9 mm) and verify that it is consistently factored into all measurements.
common_errors: Using incorrect formula for least count.
Confusing the main scale division (MSD) with the Vernier scale division (VSD).
Forgetting to use the least count in the final measurement.

rules.title: Verify zero error in Micrometer Screw Gauge
rules.description: Check whether the micrometer screw gauge is free of zero error. Zero error occurs if the zero mark on the thimble scale does not align with the zero mark on the main scale when the screw is fully closed.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the student has checked for zero error by observing the alignment of the thimble and main scale zeros. Ensure the necessary correction (subtract positive zero error or add negative zero error) is applied to the final measurement.
common_errors: Not checking for zero error before measuring.
Misinterpreting the direction of zero error (positive vs negative).
Failing to apply zero error correction to the measurement.

rules.title: Ensure correct least count for Micrometer Screw Gauge
rules.description: The least count of a micrometer is given by LC = Pitch / Number of divisions on the circular scale, where the pitch is the distance moved by the spindle per full rotation.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the least count is calculated correctly using the pitch and the number of divisions on the circular scale. Ensure it is consistently used in all measurements.
common_errors: Incorrectly calculating the pitch or divisions on the circular scale.
Using an incorrect formula for the least count.
Not using the least count in the final measurement.

rules.title: Check unit consistency in measurements
rules.description: All measurements, corrections, and calculations made using Vernier calipers or micrometers should maintain consistent units, typically millimeters (mm) or centimeters (cm).
rules.check_logic: Verify that all measurements and corrections use consistent units throughout the process. Ensure proper conversion between units (e.g., mm to cm) when necessary.
common_errors: Mixing units like cm and mm without conversion.
Reporting the final result without specifying the units.
Incorrectly converting between units (e.g., mm to cm).

rules.title: Verify measurements adhere to geometric constraints
rules.description: Ensure that the physical dimensions being measured fall within the range and constraints of the Vernier calipers or micrometer. For example, the jaws of Vernier calipers must fully encompass the object being measured.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the object being measured fits within the range of the instrument and is properly aligned. Ensure no excessive force is applied that could deform the object or damage the instrument.
common_errors: Measuring an object that exceeds the range of the Vernier calipers or micrometer.
Improper alignment of the object with the instrument.
Applying excessive force, leading to deformation of the object.

rules.title: Ensure no parallax error in readings
rules.description: Parallax error occurs if the observer's eye is not perpendicular to the scale when taking a reading. This leads to an incorrect interpretation of the scale markings.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the student has explicitly mentioned avoiding parallax error by aligning their eye perpendicular to the scale during measurement.
common_errors: Not aligning the eye perpendicular to the scale.
Recording incorrect scale readings due to parallax error.
Failing to mention parallax error avoidance in the procedure.

rules.title: Ensure correct sign convention in corrections
rules.description: Zero error corrections should follow the standard sign convention: subtract positive zero error and add negative zero error to the measured value.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the student has applied the correct sign convention when correcting for zero error. Ensure the correction is consistent with the identified type of zero error.
common_errors: Adding positive zero error instead of subtracting.
Subtracting negative zero error instead of adding.
Ignoring the sign of the zero error entirely.

rules.title: Ensure proper handling of instruments
rules.description: Improper handling of Vernier calipers or micrometers can lead to inaccurate measurements or damage to the instrument.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the student has handled the instrument correctly, avoiding excessive force, ensuring smooth movement of the jaws or spindle, and properly securing the object being measured.
common_errors: Using excessive force while closing the jaws or spindle.
Not ensuring smooth movement of the instrument components.
Failing to secure the object properly during measurement.

rules.title: Account for environmental factors affecting measurements
rules.description: Environmental factors such as temperature changes can affect the accuracy of measurements, especially for precision instruments.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the student has considered environmental factors, such as ensuring the instrument and object are at room temperature and avoiding measurements in unstable conditions.
common_errors: Ignoring the effects of temperature on the instrument or object.
Taking measurements in unstable or vibrating environments.
Failing to mention environmental considerations in the procedure.

rules.title: Verify voltage and time scale settings
rules.description: Ensure the voltage (vertical) and time (horizontal) scales are correctly set to display the signal without clipping or excessive zoom. This allows the waveform to be properly analyzed within the oscilloscope's display range.
rules.check_logic: Check if the peak-to-peak voltage of the signal fits within the vertical scale range (without clipping at the top or bottom) and ensure the waveform's period fits within the horizontal scale range.
common_errors: Setting voltage scale too small, causing the signal to be clipped.
Setting time scale too narrow, making only part of the waveform visible.
Setting voltage or time scale too large, zooming out unnecessarily and losing detail.

rules.title: Ensure proper trigger settings for a stable waveform
rules.description: Proper trigger settings stabilize the display of repetitive waveforms. Ensure the oscilloscope is successfully stabilizing the signal display.
rules.check_logic: Verify the trigger source is correctly selected (e.g., correct channel or external trigger), the trigger level is within the signal's amplitude range, and the correct trigger edge (rising or falling) is chosen for signal stabilization.
common_errors: Forgetting to select the correct trigger source.
Setting the trigger level outside the signal amplitude range, resulting in instability.
Using the wrong trigger edge for the signal type.

rules.title: Validate frequency and period calculations
rules.description: The frequency of a periodic signal is the reciprocal of its period. Check for consistency between the calculated frequency and the displayed signal.
rules.check_logic: Measure the waveform's period using the horizontal scale and calculate frequency using f = 1/T. Verify the calculated frequency matches the signal's displayed frequency.
common_errors: Incorrectly measuring the time period between peaks or troughs.
Forgetting the frequency and period's reciprocal relationship.
Not applying the time scale factor when measuring the period.

rules.title: Verify AC/DC coupling settings
rules.description: Ensure the correct coupling mode (AC or DC) is used based on the signal's nature to prevent distortion or inaccurate representation.
rules.check_logic: Verify AC coupling is used for signals with a DC offset to block it and prevent distortion from low frequencies, and use DC coupling for full signal representation including DC offsets.
common_errors: Using AC coupling for low-frequency signals, resulting in distortion.
Using DC coupling and incorrectly interpreting the DC offset as part of the signal.
Not comprehending the difference between AC and DC coupling effects.

rules.title: Ensure signal integrity and noise minimization
rules.description: Verify the displayed signal's integrity by minimizing noise and distortion through proper grounding and probe settings.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the probe is correctly grounded, check the probe attenuation matches the oscilloscope's settings, and confirm the probe bandwidth supports the signal's frequency.
common_errors: Failing to ground the probe correctly, leading to noise.
Mismatch between probe attenuation and oscilloscope settings.
Using a probe that lacks the required bandwidth for high-frequency signals.

rules.title: Ensure dimensional and unit consistency
rules.description: Verify that voltage, time, and frequency measurements are reported in correct units and dimensionally consistent throughout calculations.
rules.check_logic: Confirm voltage is in volts (V), time in seconds (s), and frequency in hertz (Hz). Ensure consistent units in calculations involving f = 1/T.
common_errors: Using incorrect units such as millivolts instead of volts.
Mixing units (e.g., milliseconds without converting to seconds).
Failing to convert units as needed for calculations.

rules.title: Check waveform symmetry and shape
rules.description: For periodic signals, compare the waveform shape and symmetry with the expected signal type such as sinusoidal or square.
rules.check_logic: Evaluate the displayed waveform's shape against expected patterns. Verify symmetry, such as equal peaks for sinusoidal waves, and inspect for distortions.
common_errors: Overlooking distortion or waveform clipping.
Misjudging waveform shape due to wrong time or voltage scales.
Neglecting waveform asymmetry caused by circuit issues or external interference.

rules.title: Ensure oscilloscope bandwidth is sufficient
rules.description: The oscilloscope's bandwidth should be at least five times the highest frequency component of the signal to capture accurate waveforms.
rules.check_logic: Verify the oscilloscope's bandwidth exceeds five times the highest signal frequency. Check and adjust the bandwidth limit setting as necessary.
common_errors: Using an oscilloscope that lacks sufficient bandwidth, leading to loss of details.
Enabling bandwidth limiting without understanding its impact.
Neglecting limited bandwidth effects on signal accuracy.

rules.title: Verify probe calibration
rules.description: Ensure that the oscilloscope probes are properly calibrated for accurate signal measurements.
rules.check_logic: Perform probe compensation by connecting the probe to the oscilloscope's calibration signal and adjusting until the displayed waveform (usually a square wave) is properly square and stable.
common_errors: Failing to perform probe calibration leading to inaccurate readings.
Improper adjustment causing waveform distortion.
Ignoring regular calibration checks as part of routine maintenance.

rules.title: Ensure calibration curve follows the correct mathematical model
rules.description: The calibration curve relates the instrument output (e.g., voltage, reading) to the true physical quantity being measured. Verify that the chosen mathematical model (linear, polynomial, logarithmic, etc.) fits the expected physical relationship and experimental data.
rules.check_logic: Use statistical methods, such as linear regression or non-linear curve fitting techniques, to compare experimental data points to the selected model and evaluate goodness-of-fit using measures like R² (coefficient of determination).
common_errors: Using an incorrect model for the calibration curve (e.g., linear instead of exponential).
Not verifying the goodness-of-fit of the model to the data.

rules.title: Verify consistency in sign conventions for physical quantities
rules.description: Ensure that the sign conventions for all physical quantities (e.g., positive/negative voltage, displacement, current) are consistent throughout the calibration process. This is especially important for measurements involving directional quantities.
rules.check_logic: Check that all measurements respect the defined sign convention for the experiment, and conduct a review for consistency across all phases of calibration (e.g., upward voltage is positive, leftward displacement is negative).
common_errors: Inverting the sign of measurements.
Using different conventions for the same quantity in different parts of the calculation.

rules.title: Ensure proper alignment and positioning of the instrument during calibration
rules.description: For accurate calibration, the instrument must be properly aligned with the reference standard or source. Misalignment introduces systematic errors.
rules.check_logic: Use geometric tools such as spirit levels, laser alignment devices, or computer-aided alignment systems to verify that the instrument is aligned (e.g., level, perpendicular, or at the correct angle) per the setup requirements.
common_errors: Instrument not leveled properly.
Angle of incidence not matching the setup requirements.

rules.title: Verify operating range of the instrument
rules.description: Ensure that the instrument is calibrated within its specified operating range (e.g., voltage, temperature, pressure). Operating outside this range can cause non-linear responses or damage.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that the calibration data points lie within the manufacturer's specified range for the instrument, consulting technical specifications to determine appropriate parameters.
common_errors: Calibrating the instrument outside its operational range.
Assuming linearity beyond the specified range.

rules.title: Check dimensional consistency of calibration equation
rules.description: The calibration equation must respect dimensional consistency. For example, if the input is a length (m) and the output is a force (N), the calibration constant should have appropriate dimensions.
rules.check_logic: Use dimensional analysis to ensure that all terms in the calibration equation balance dimensionally, and inspect units for compatibility across all calculations.
common_errors: Ignoring the units of the calibration constant.
Mixing units inconsistently (e.g., mm with m).

rules.title: Evaluate uncertainty in calibration measurements
rules.description: Calibration should include an evaluation of the uncertainties associated with both the instrument being calibrated and the standard/reference. This includes random and systematic errors.
rules.check_logic: Calculate uncertainty using standard propagation of uncertainty formulas, identify all significant sources of uncertainty, and ensure it is within acceptable limits for the application.
common_errors: Neglecting to calculate uncertainty in calibration.
Ignoring systematic errors in the uncertainty calculation.

rules.title: Verify the accuracy of the reference standard
rules.description: The reference standard used for calibration must itself be calibrated and traceable to a recognized metrological standard (e.g., NIST).
rules.check_logic: Confirm that the reference standard has a valid calibration certificate and document its traceability to a national or international standard, reviewing certificates for expiration dates and recent upgrades.
common_errors: Using an uncalibrated or expired reference standard.
Not verifying traceability of the reference standard.

rules.title: Ensure environmental conditions are within acceptable limits
rules.description: Calibration must be conducted under controlled environmental conditions (e.g., temperature, humidity) as specified by the instrument manufacturer to avoid errors.
rules.check_logic: Use environmental monitoring equipment to check that the environmental parameters during calibration are within the specified range for the instrument and document any fluctuations.
common_errors: Calibrating in an environment with significant temperature or humidity fluctuations.
Ignoring the effects of environmental drift during calibration.

rules.title: Ensure consistency through repeated measurements
rules.description: Conduct multiple measurements across different trials to assess variability and ensure reliability and consistency in calibration results.
rules.check_logic: Perform repeated measurements and analyze resultant data for variance or deviation, standard deviation can be used as a consistency metric.
common_errors: Failure to perform repeat measurements leading to increased uncertainty.
Ignoring outliers or discrepancies across trials and datasets.

rules.title: Ensure correctness of fundamental statistical equations
rules.description: Verify the proper use of fundamental statistical equations such as mean ([3mbc = a3x/N[0m), standard deviation ([3mc3 = sqrt(a3(x-bc)^2/N)[0m), and variance ([3mc3�b2 = a3(x-bc)^2/N[0m). These equations form the basis of statistical analysis in experimental physics.
rules.check_logic: Check if the student used the correct formula for mean, variance, or standard deviation. Ensure all terms (e.g., N, x, bc) are properly defined and consistently used. Verify whether the equations are applied to the correct dataset (e.g., population vs. sample).
common_errors: Dividing by N-1 instead of N for population statistics
Using a3x^2 instead of a3(x-bc)^2 when calculating variance
Forgetting to take the square root when calculating standard deviation from variance

rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency in statistical calculations
rules.description: Ensure that all the quantities in statistical computations maintain consistent units. For example, if the data points x are measured in meters, then the mean and standard deviation must also have units of meters.
rules.check_logic: Check if the units of output (mean, standard deviation) match the units of the input dataset. Verify that unit conversions, if any, are performed correctly.
common_errors: Failing to include units in final results
Mixing incompatible units (e.g., adding meters to seconds)
Incorrect unit conversions during intermediate steps

rules.title: Verify adherence to sign conventions in error analysis
rules.description: In experimental error analysis, absolute errors are always positive, while signed deviations can be either positive or negative depending on the direction of the deviation from the true value.
rules.check_logic: Check if absolute errors are always reported as positive values and if signed deviations respect the proper sign convention relative to the reference value. Ensure clarity in distinguishing between absolute and percentage errors.
common_errors: Reporting absolute errors as negative
Misinterpreting the direction of deviation (e.g., swapping the sign of signed errors)
Mixing absolute error and percentage error without proper clarity

rules.title: Check validity of curve fitting models
rules.description: Ensure that the chosen curve fitting model appropriately represents the data based on the underlying physical principles and the type of data distribution (e.g., linear for straight-line trends, exponential for decay processes).
rules.check_logic: Check if the student justifies the choice of the fitting model based on data characteristics. Verify if the residuals are randomly distributed, indicating a good fit. Ensure that overfitting or underfitting is avoided.
common_errors: Applying a linear fit to non-linear data without justification
Ignoring residual analysis to validate the fit
Using an over-complicated model (e.g., higher-order polynomial) for simple data trends

rules.title: Validate proper application of error propagation rules
rules.description: Error propagation must follow specific rules depending on the operations: addition/subtraction (94z = sqrt(94x^2 + 94y^2)) and multiplication/division (94z/z = sqrt((94x/x)^2 + (94y/y)^2)).
rules.check_logic: Check if the correct error propagation equations are applied for the given operations and ensure consistency with the data's uncertainty values. Verify that intermediate steps in calculations also account for propagated errors.
common_errors: Using incorrect formulas for error propagation in non-linear operations
Forgetting to propagate uncertainties for intermediate calculations
Mixing relative and absolute uncertainties without proper conversion

rules.title: Ensure correct calculation and interpretation of correlation coefficient
rules.description: The correlation coefficient (r) quantifies the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two variables. It ranges from -1 to +1. Ensure that students use the correct formula and interpret the result appropriately.
rules.check_logic: Check if the correlation coefficient is calculated correctly using r = a3((x-bcx)(y-bcy))/(Nc3xc3y) and if its value is within the range [-1, 1]. Verify that the interpretation of r aligns with the data's characteristics.
common_errors: Incorrectly computing the mean or standard deviation during calculation
Reporting a correlation coefficient outside the valid range [-1, 1]
Misinterpreting the value of r (e.g., confusing strong negative correlation with no correlation)

rules.title: Check methodology for outlier detection
rules.description: Outliers are data points that deviate significantly from the rest of the dataset. Ensure that the student uses appropriate statistical methods (e.g., Z-scores, IQR method) to identify and justify the treatment of outliers.
rules.check_logic: Check if the student calculates Z-scores (Z = (x-bc)/c3) or uses the IQR method (outliers are 1.5�d7IQR beyond Q1 and Q3). Verify if the treatment of outliers is justified and documented.
common_errors: Failing to define thresholds for identifying outliers
Arbitrarily removing outliers without statistical justification
Confusing measurement errors with genuine outliers

rules.title: Verify normalization of histograms
rules.description: Normalized histograms represent probability distributions and should integrate to 1. Ensure that students normalize the histogram if presenting it as a probability density function.
rules.check_logic: Check if the sum of the histogram bin heights multiplied by bin widths equals 1 for normalized histograms. Verify that bin widths are consistent or appropriately accounted for.
common_errors: Presenting unnormalized histograms as probability distributions
Using inconsistent bin widths without adjusting bin heights
Incorrectly calculating the total area under the histogram

rules.title: Check for sampling bias in data collection
rules.description: Ensure that the dataset used for analysis is representative of the population being studied. Identify and address any potential sampling biases that could affect the validity of the results.
rules.check_logic: Check if the sampling method is described and justified. Verify that the sample size is sufficient and that the data is not skewed due to selection bias or other systematic errors.
common_errors: Using a sample that is not representative of the population
Failing to account for systematic errors in data collection
Ignoring the impact of small sample sizes on statistical reliability

topics.name: Design of Experiments and Hypothesis Testing

rules.title: Correct Equation Selection for Hypothesis Testing
rules.description: Ensure the use of the correct statistical equation for hypothesis testing, such as z-tests, t-tests, chi-squared tests, based on the data characteristics and sample size.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the choice of statistical test aligns with the data type (continuous, categorical), sample size, and distribution assumptions (e.g., normality for t-tests).
common_errors: Using a t-test for large samples when z-test should be used
Applying chi-squared test on continuous data without categorization
Using parametric tests without verifying distribution assumptions

rules.title: Coordinate System Integrity
rules.description: In an experiment, ensure all measurements are consistent with the stated coordinate system. This often applies to direction conventions or sign conventions relevant to measurements like velocity or displacement.
rules.check_logic: Check if all reported measurements maintain consistency in sign and direction relative to the declared coordinate system. Verify transformations between coordinate systems are explicitly stated and correctly applied.
common_errors: Inverting sign for vector components
Applying multiple systems without transformation explanations
Misinterpreting coordinate system origin or axes orientation

rules.title: Verification of Geometric Constraints
rules.description: When designing experiments, ensure any geometric constraints imposed by the setup are adhered to, such as alignment of optical components in a laser experiment.
rules.check_logic: Check if the setup conforms to geometric constraints like parallel alignment, correct angular displacement, or specified distances between components.
common_errors: Ignoring beam diameter impacting optical alignment
Misalignment of equipment leading to errors in measurements
Failure to account for thermal expansion affecting alignment

rules.title: Application Validity Conditions
rules.description: Ensure the laws applied within the experimental design hold under the given conditions, such as assuming linear response for small perturbations.
rules.check_logic: Verify if the application conditions (e.g., small angle approximation, ideal gas conditions, linearity assumptions) are satisfied before applying specific laws. Document any deviations and their potential impact on results.
common_errors: Using small angle approximation for angles >15 degrees
Applying ideal gas law without low density considerations
Assuming linear response in a nonlinear regime

rules.title: Dimensional Consistency Verification
rules.description: Ensure all equations and calculations used in the experiment are dimensionally consistent, adhering to the principle that physical laws must hold regardless of unit systems.
rules.check_logic: Check the dimensional consistency of all derived equations and ensure units match expected dimensions when substituting specific values. Verify unit conversions are correctly applied.
common_errors: Mismatch in units leading to erroneous dimension analysis
Incorrect conversion between unit systems
Failure to verify derived equations for dimensional consistency

rules.title: Selection of Appropriate Test Statistic
rules.description: Choose the appropriate test statistic for evaluating hypotheses based on the experimental design and data type, such as ANOVA for comparing more than two groups.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the test statistic matches the structure of hypothesis, data type, number of groups or conditions, and experimental design (e.g., paired vs unpaired data).
common_errors: Confusion between one-way and two-way ANOVA
Inappropriate use of tests for paired vs unpaired data
Using parametric tests without verifying assumptions like homogeneity of variance

rules.title: Comprehensive Error Analysis
rules.description: Include detailed error analysis in experiment design, accounting for systematic, random, and human-induced errors.
rules.check_logic: Verify if error analysis covers all possible error sources, quantifies their impact, and includes strategies for mitigation or acknowledgment. Ensure error propagation is calculated where applicable.
common_errors: Ignoring human measurement error in precision experiments
Failure to account for environmental variations impacting results
Omitting error propagation in derived quantities

rules.title: Sampling Strategy Verification
rules.description: Ensure the sampling strategy is appropriate for the experimental goals, data type, and population characteristics.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the sampling method (e.g., random, stratified, systematic) aligns with the experimental objectives and minimizes bias. Check if the sample size is sufficient for statistical power.
common_errors: Using a biased sampling method leading to unrepresentative data
Insufficient sample size for detecting meaningful effects
Failure to account for population heterogeneity in sampling

rules.title: Control Variable Management
rules.description: Ensure all relevant control variables are identified and managed to isolate the effect of the independent variable.
rules.check_logic: Verify that control variables are explicitly stated, consistently maintained, and monitored throughout the experiment. Check for unintended confounding variables.
common_errors: Failure to identify critical control variables
Inconsistent application of control conditions
Overlooking confounding variables impacting results

rules.title: Verify dimensional consistency of the equation
rules.description: Ensure that all terms in the equation have the same dimensions. Dimensional consistency is a required condition for the physical validity of an equation.
rules.check_logic: Compare the dimensions of all terms across the equation, ensuring the left-hand side matches the right-hand side. Utilize fundamental dimensions (M, L, T, etc.) for this comparison.
common_errors: Adding or equating quantities with incompatible dimensions (e.g., length added to time)
Using incorrect units for physical constants like gravitational constant or speed of light
Forgetting to account for derived quantities, like velocity (L/T) or acceleration (L/T^2)

rules.title: Validate correct unit conversions
rules.description: Ensure that proper unit conversions are applied when switching between different unit systems (e.g., SI and CGS).
rules.check_logic: Verify that all quantities are consistently converted using accurate conversion factors (e.g., 1 m = 100 cm).
common_errors: Incorrectly converting units, such as using an inverse factor (e.g., 1/100 instead of 100)
Mixing unit systems without applying conversion factors
Failing to square or cube unit conversions for area or volume (e.g., 1 m^2 ≠ 100 cm^2)

rules.title: Verify correctness of derived dimensions
rules.description: Ensure that derived quantities (e.g., velocity, force, energy) are expressed correctly in terms of fundamental dimensions (M, L, T).
rules.check_logic: Validate that the derived dimensions reflect the expected relationships, such as velocity = L/T, force = M·L/T^2.
common_errors: Misidentifying the dimensions of a derived quantity (e.g., treating energy as L·T instead of M·L^2/T^2)
Confusing related quantities (e.g., mistaking force for momentum)

rules.title: Verify scaling relations using dimensional analysis
rules.description: Ensure that a scaling relation between quantities derived via dimensional analysis remains dimensionally consistent and matches the physical scenario.
rules.check_logic: Assess the proportionality constants and exponents in the scaling relation to confirm their dimensions are compatible with the system's parameters.
common_errors: Using incorrect exponents in the scaling relation
Excluding dimensionless constants where appropriate
Deriving incorrect relations by disregarding system constraints or symmetry

rules.title: Ensure consistency of coordinate systems
rules.description: Verify that the chosen coordinate system aligns with the physical geometry of the problem and that all components respect the defined axes and sign conventions.
rules.check_logic: Verify vector components align with the coordinate axes, and confirm conversions between coordinate systems (e.g., Cartesian to polar) are accurately executed.
common_errors: Misinterpreting the direction of vector components
Using incorrect sign conventions for specific axes
Mixing coordinate systems without proper transformations

rules.title: Check dimensional homogeneity of physical constants
rules.description: Ensure that physical constants used in equations have consistent dimensions within their specific context.
rules.check_logic: Verify dimensions of constants like G (gravitational constant), c (speed of light) are appropriately used within the equation.
common_errors: Using incorrect dimensions for constants (e.g., treating G as L^3/T^2 instead of M^-1L^3T^-2)
Applying constants in inappropriate contexts without checking dimensions

rules.title: Validate the equation against limiting cases
rules.description: Analyze whether the equation remains valid in extreme or limiting cases (e.g., as a variable approaches zero or infinity).
rules.check_logic: Substitute extreme values into the equation and verify whether the results are dimensionally consistent and conceptually reasonable.
common_errors: Creating equations that fail in limiting cases (e.g., neglecting terms that dominate at small or large values)
Overlooking dimensionless parameters' limits (e.g., Reynold's number in fluid dynamics)

rules.title: Verify geometric constraints in scaling problems
rules.description: Ensure that properties like length, area, and volume scale appropriately with changes in system size.
rules.check_logic: Verify that geometric properties scale correctly with length, area, and volume dimensions (e.g., area scales as length^2, volume scales as length^3).
common_errors: Using incorrect scaling factors (e.g., assuming volume scales linearly with length)
Ignoring dimensional changes when scaling (e.g., treating 2D and 3D objects interchangeably)

rules.title: Ensure validity of dimensionless quantities and numbers
rules.description: Check that dimensionless quantities derived within equations are valid and serve their intended comparative function.
rules.check_logic: Verify that dimensionless numbers such as coefficients or ratios (e.g., Reynolds number, Pi term) are correctly derived and applied.
common_errors: Incorrect calculation or definition of dimensionless numbers
Misapplication of dimensionless quantities that leads to invalid comparisons

rules.title: Ensure Appropriate Safety Equipment Use
rules.description: Verify that the proper safety equipment, such as goggles, gloves, and lab coats, is used consistently to protect against chemical spills, biological exposure, or mechanical hazards.
rules.check_logic: Ensure safety equipment is mentioned and used according to the type of experiment being conducted. Verify that the equipment is appropriate for the specific hazards involved.
common_errors: Failure to mention eye protection when handling chemicals.
Not wearing gloves when handling biological samples.
Omitting lab coat usage in hazardous experiments.
Using inappropriate safety equipment for the specific hazard (e.g., thin gloves for handling corrosive chemicals).

rules.title: Verify Correct Sign Conventions
rules.description: Make sure laboratory settings align with standard sign conventions for vector quantities, such as force, velocity, and acceleration, based on the chosen coordinate system.
rules.check_logic: Ensure forces, velocities, and accelerations are labeled with the correct sign based on the chosen coordinate system. Verify consistency between experimental setup, data collection, and analysis.
common_errors: Using incorrect sign for vector quantities like force or acceleration.
Misalignment between reported results and coordinate system orientation.
Failure to document the chosen coordinate system clearly.

rules.title: Check Spatial and Geometric Constraints
rules.description: Experimental setups must adhere to geometric constraints such as angles, distances, and alignments for precision measurements.
rules.check_logic: Verify experiment layout ensures angles, alignments, and distances conform to the protocol specifications. Ensure that any deviations are documented and accounted for in the analysis.
common_errors: Misalignment of optical components in laser experiments.
Incorrect distance setup for parallax error minimization.
Failure to calibrate alignment tools before setup.

rules.title: Ensure Kinematic Constraint Adherence
rules.description: Verify moving parts in experimental setups do not violate expected motion constraints, ensuring accurate data collection.
rules.check_logic: Ensure all moving components are constrained as per experiment design (e.g., linear vs. rotational motion). Verify that unexpected motion (e.g., vibrations or unintended rotations) is minimized or accounted for.
common_errors: Incorrect interpretation of sliding vs. rolling motion.
Ignoring constraints leading to erroneous velocity measurements.
Failure to account for unintended vibrations or oscillations.

rules.title: Ensure Validity Condition Compliance
rules.description: Confirm that experiments are conducted within conditions required by applicable laws and equations, such as temperature, pressure, or vacuum levels.
rules.check_logic: Verify environment conditions match the assumptions for theoretical models used. Ensure that deviations from ideal conditions are documented and accounted for in the analysis.
common_errors: Ignoring temperature limits in thermodynamic experiments.
Applying laws of motion in non-inertial reference frames without adjustments.
Failure to monitor and record environmental conditions during the experiment.

rules.title: Verify Dimensional and Unit Consistency
rules.description: Ensure that all measurements and equations maintain dimensional consistency and unit correctness throughout the experiment.
rules.check_logic: Check that units are consistently applied in calculations, maintaining dimensional consistency. Verify that unit conversions are correctly performed where necessary.
common_errors: Using mismatched units without proper conversion.
Calculating derived quantities with dimensionally inconsistent equations.
Failure to document units clearly in data logs and reports.

rules.title: Check Energy Conservation Application
rules.description: Verify conservation of energy principle is correctly applied in experiments involving mechanical systems, accounting for friction, air resistance, and other dissipative forces.
rules.check_logic: Ensure energy calculations account for all forms of energy input and output, including dissipative forces. Verify that energy losses are measured or estimated where applicable.
common_errors: Neglecting energy lost to friction or heat.
Incorrectly summing kinetic and potential energy contributions.
Failure to account for energy dissipation in non-ideal systems.

rules.title: Ensure Accurate Data Recording
rules.description: Verify that all experimental data is collected and recorded with precision, including units, time stamps, and environmental conditions, ensuring reproducibility and analysis accuracy.
rules.check_logic: Confirm data sheets and logs contain all necessary information for analysis, with appropriate uncertainty estimates. Verify that data is recorded in real-time and that calibration states of equipment are documented.
common_errors: Omitting critical environmental conditions from data logs.
Incorrectly estimated uncertainty or failure to record equipment calibration states.
Failure to record data in real-time, leading to potential loss of information.

rules.title: Perform Comprehensive Uncertainty Analysis
rules.description: Ensure that all measurements and derived quantities include an uncertainty estimate, and that the sources of uncertainty are identified and minimized where possible.
