rules.check_logic: Verify that uncertainty estimates are calculated for all measurements and derived quantities. Ensure that sources of uncertainty are documented and minimized where feasible.
common_errors: Failure to include uncertainty estimates in reported results.
Ignoring systematic errors in uncertainty analysis.
Using inappropriate methods to calculate uncertainty.

rules.title: Verify Equipment Calibration
rules.description: Ensure that all measurement instruments are properly calibrated before use, and that calibration records are maintained.
rules.check_logic: Confirm that all instruments are calibrated according to manufacturer specifications or experimental requirements. Verify that calibration records are up-to-date and accessible.
common_errors: Using uncalibrated instruments for critical measurements.
Failure to document calibration procedures and results.
Ignoring calibration drift over time.

rules.title: Define and Maintain Control Variables
rules.description: Control variables are constants in experimental setups that should remain unaltered to prevent confounding effects. Proper definition and maintenance of these variables is essential for reproducibility.
rules.check_logic: Verify that control variables are explicitly identified and kept constant during all trials to ensure valid results.
common_errors: Failure to define control variables
Accidental variation of control parameters during experiment

rules.title: Check Reproducibility with Independent Replications
rules.description: Reproducibility requires that an experiment can be repeated with consistent results. Using independent replications ensures reliability by reducing errors and inherent biases.
rules.check_logic: Ensure at least three independent replications are conducted with identical methodologies and consistent result reporting.
common_errors: Insufficient number of replications
Discrepancies in methodological approaches across replications

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional and Unit Consistency
rules.description: All measurements should consistently adhere to specified units and dimensions across the experimental setup for clarity and comparability of data.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all physical quantities are reported in consistent units and dimensions, ensuring calculations respect dimensional consistency.
common_errors: Mixing units (e.g., cm with inches)
Omitting units in calculations or results

rules.title: Adhere to Geometric Constraints
rules.description: Geometric constraints influence the organization of elements in an experiment and must be adhered to for accurate interpretation.
rules.check_logic: Check that the experimental setup adheres to geometric constraints related to control variables and measurement instruments to prevent misalignment.
common_errors: Ignoring spatial alignment requirements
Misalignment of measurement tools

rules.title: Observe Kinematic Constraints for Repeatability
rules.description: Kinematic constraints on motion parameters must be consistently applied in repeated experiments to ensure reproducibility.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the movement parameters of any experimental machinery or subject remain consistent across all trials, documenting any necessary alterations.
common_errors: Variable speed in kinematic setups
Changing trajectory without documenting alterations

rules.title: Consistent Application of Sign Conventions
rules.description: Sign conventions should be consistently applied to avoid misinterpretation of results, especially when dealing with vector quantities or directional measurements.
rules.check_logic: Ensure all vector quantities have clearly defined sign conventions that are applied consistently across all trials.
common_errors: Inconsistent sign application for vector directions
Confusion between positive and negative axis identifiers

rules.title: Evaluate Validity Conditions for Experimental Laws
rules.description: Ensure the laws or models applied in the experiment are valid under the specific conditions (e.g., temperature, pressure, environment).
rules.check_logic: Confirm that the experimental conditions align with the assumptions of the theoretical framework or model being used.
common_errors: Applying laws outside their valid range
Ignoring environmental factors that affect law applicability

rules.title: Standardize Data Collection Protocols
rules.description: The procedures followed for data collection should be standardized to ensure repeatability and consistent data acquisition.
rules.check_logic: Verify that data collection methods are clearly defined, standardized, and consistently followed across all trials.
common_errors: Variable data collection techniques
Inconsistent parameters during data acquisition

rules.title: Conduct Thorough Error Analysis
rules.description: Error analysis identifies potential discrepancies or inaccuracies in experimental results, ensuring reliable interpretation.
rules.check_logic: Ensure all potential sources of error are accounted for, documented, and analyzed consistently across experimental trials.
common_errors: Failure to account for measurement error
Inadequate analysis of data variability

topics.name: Use of Multimeters and Circuit Analysis Tools

rules.title: Verify proper multimeter mode for voltage measurement
rules.description: Ensure the multimeter is set to the voltage measurement mode (V) before measuring voltage across a component. This is essential to avoid incorrect readings or damaging the device.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the multimeter is in 'V' mode and connected in parallel with the component being measured. Ensure the voltage range setting is appropriate for the expected measurement.
common_errors: Multimeter set to current or resistance mode instead of voltage mode.
Connecting the multimeter in series instead of parallel for voltage measurement.
Incorrect voltage range setting, leading to inaccurate readings or damage.

rules.title: Verify proper multimeter mode for current measurement
rules.description: Ensure the multimeter is set to current measurement mode (A or mA) and connected in series with the circuit element to measure current. Incorrect connection can damage the multimeter or circuit.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the multimeter is in 'A' or 'mA' mode and connected in series with the circuit. Confirm that the current range setting is appropriate for the expected measurement.
common_errors: Multimeter set to voltage or resistance mode instead of current mode.
Connecting the multimeter in parallel instead of in series for current measurement.
Exceeding the current rating of the multimeter, causing internal fuse damage.

rules.title: Verify proper multimeter mode for resistance measurement
rules.description: Ensure the multimeter is set to resistance mode (Ω) and the component is disconnected from the circuit before measuring resistance to avoid interference from other circuit elements.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the multimeter is in 'Ω' mode and the component is disconnected from the circuit. Ensure the multimeter is zeroed if using an analog device.
common_errors: Measuring resistance without disconnecting the component from the circuit.
Multimeter set to voltage or current mode instead of resistance mode.
Failure to zero the multimeter if using an analog device.

rules.title: Verify application of Ohm's Law
rules.description: Ensure the measured voltage (V), current (I), and resistance (R) satisfy Ohm's Law (V = IR) for resistive elements. This applies only to linear resistors.
rules.check_logic: Verify that V = IR holds true for the measured values. Confirm that the resistor is a linear component and that temperature effects are negligible.
common_errors: Applying Ohm's Law to non-linear components such as diodes or transistors.
Incorrect resistance value due to poor connections or multimeter errors.
Ignoring temperature-based variations in resistance.

rules.title: Verify sign conventions for voltage measurements
rules.description: Ensure the polarity of voltage measurements aligns with the defined positive and negative terminals of the component or circuit. Reverse polarity can lead to incorrect interpretations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the positive terminal of the multimeter is connected to the higher potential side of the component. Confirm that the polarity indicated by the multimeter is correctly interpreted.
common_errors: Reversing the multimeter leads, leading to a negative reading that is misinterpreted as positive.
Forgetting to note the polarity indicated by the multimeter.

rules.title: Verify dimensional and unit consistency in measurements
rules.description: Ensure the measured quantities (voltage, current, resistance) have consistent units and match the expected scale (e.g., mV, A, kΩ). Incorrect unit interpretation can lead to significant errors in calculations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the measured values have appropriate units and are consistent with the circuit's expected operating range. Confirm that unit conversions are applied correctly when necessary.
common_errors: Misinterpreting multimeter readings (e.g., mistaking mA for A or kΩ for Ω).
Using inconsistent units in calculations (e.g., mixing mA and A).
Failing to convert units when required.

rules.title: Verify circuit continuity using multimeter
rules.description: Ensure the multimeter is set to continuity mode and connected across the components or nodes being tested. A beep indicates continuity, confirming an uninterrupted electrical path.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the multimeter is in continuity mode and connected across the correct nodes or component. Ensure the circuit is powered off during the test.
common_errors: Multimeter set to resistance or voltage mode instead of continuity mode.
Testing continuity on a powered circuit, which can damage the multimeter.
Failing to recognize the absence of a beep as a lack of continuity.

rules.title: Verify safety precautions to prevent short circuits
rules.description: Ensure multimeter probes are not shorting adjacent terminals or circuit elements during measurement. Accidental shorts can damage the circuit or multimeter.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the probes are properly placed and do not touch unintended parts of the circuit. Confirm that the probes are in good condition and insulated.
common_errors: Probes touching multiple terminals, causing a short circuit.
Using damaged probes with exposed wires, increasing the risk of short circuits.
Measuring live circuits without proper insulation and precautions.

rules.title: Verify proper multimeter mode for capacitance measurement
rules.description: Ensure the multimeter is set to capacitance mode (if available) and the capacitor is disconnected from the circuit before measurement. This prevents interference from other circuit elements.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the multimeter is in capacitance mode and the capacitor is fully discharged and disconnected from the circuit.
common_errors: Measuring capacitance without disconnecting the capacitor from the circuit.
Multimeter set to an incorrect mode instead of capacitance mode.
Failing to discharge the capacitor before measurement, leading to inaccurate readings or damage.

rules.title: Verify correctness of Planck's law for blackbody radiation
rules.description: Planck's law describes the spectral radiance of electromagnetic radiation emitted by a blackbody in thermal equilibrium as a function of wavelength and temperature. Ensure its correct use when dealing with blackbody radiation measurements.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the equation L(λ,T) = (2hc²/λ⁵) * (1/(e^(hc/λkT) - 1)) is used, with all constants (h, c, k) and variables (λ, T) appropriately substituted and in correct SI units.
common_errors: Using the wrong exponent sign in the exponential factor.
Forgetting to include the factor of 2hc².
Using frequency instead of wavelength without proper conversion.

rules.title: Ensure correct wavelength-frequency conversion
rules.description: The relationship between wavelength (λ) and frequency (f) is given by c = λf, where c is the speed of light. This relationship is essential in converting between spectra measured in wavelength and frequency.
rules.check_logic: Verify that λ = c/f or f = c/λ is used correctly, with consistent units for speed, wavelength, and frequency.
common_errors: Incorrect rearrangement of the formula (e.g., mixing up numerator and denominator).
Using an incorrect value for the speed of light.
Confusing wavelength with frequency in terms of units.

rules.title: Check sign conventions for redshift and blueshift
rules.description: Redshift corresponds to an increase in wavelength (positive shift), while blueshift corresponds to a decrease in wavelength (negative shift). Ensure the correct sign convention is applied when interpreting spectral line shifts.
rules.check_logic: Verify that Δλ/λ0 = v/c is positive for redshift and negative for blueshift, where λ0 is the original wavelength, v is the relative velocity, and c is the speed of light.
common_errors: Assigning the wrong sign to Δλ for redshift or blueshift.
Confusing redshift with blueshift in qualitative descriptions.
Forgetting to normalize Δλ by the original wavelength.

rules.title: Verify photon energy calculation using E = hf
rules.description: The energy of a photon is calculated using E = hf, where h is Planck's constant and f is the frequency. This is crucial when analyzing light in terms of its quantum properties.
rules.check_logic: Ensure E = hf is applied correctly, with consistent units for h (J·s) and f (Hz), and appropriate unit conversion if energy is expressed in electron volts.
common_errors: Using wavelength (λ) instead of frequency (f) without conversion.
Incorrect value for Planck's constant.
Mixing up energy units, e.g., Joules vs. electron volts.

rules.title: Ensure dimensional/unit consistency in spectroscopy equations
rules.description: Equations in spectroscopy involve constants like Planck's constant (h), speed of light (c), and Boltzmann constant (k). Ensure all units are consistent when substituting values into equations.
rules.check_logic: Verify that units on both sides of the equation match; for example, ensure energy (E) in Joules or electron volts matches the provided variables' units, and wavelength (λ) is in meters or nanometers where applicable.
common_errors: Using mismatched units for constants and variables (e.g., h in J·s but λ in nm).
Mixing SI and non-SI units without proper conversion.
Forgetting to convert temperature to Kelvin in thermal equations.

rules.title: Check application of the diffraction grating equation
rules.description: The diffraction grating equation nλ = d·sin(θ) relates the order of diffraction (n), wavelength (λ), grating spacing (d), and diffraction angle (θ). Ensure correct application in spectroscopy experiments.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the equation is applied correctly, with consistent units for wavelength and spacing, and θ expressed in radians if trigonometric functions are used.
common_errors: Using θ in degrees instead of radians without conversion.
Confusing grating spacing (d) with the number of lines per unit length.
Forgetting to account for the order of diffraction (n).

rules.title: Verify application of Beer-Lambert Law
rules.description: Beer-Lambert Law states A = εcl, where A is absorbance, ε is the molar absorptivity, c is the concentration, and l is the path length. This law applies to monochromatic light passing through a medium.
rules.check_logic: Ensure A = εcl is used with ε in L/(mol·cm), c in mol/L, and l in cm, ensuring absorbance (A) is dimensionless.
common_errors: Misinterpreting absorbance (A) as having units.
Confusing ε (molar absorptivity) with extinction coefficient.
Forgetting to use the logarithmic relationship for absorbance (A = -log10(I/I0)).

rules.title: Check validity conditions for applied spectroscopy laws
rules.description: Many spectroscopy principles, such as Beer-Lambert Law and Planck's Law, require specific conditions (e.g., monochromatic light, non-scattering medium). Ensure these conditions are met before applying the laws.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the conditions for applying each law are explicitly stated and satisfied in the problem setup, and check for assumptions like non-scattering medium for Beer-Lambert Law and thermal equilibrium for Planck's Law.
common_errors: Applying Beer-Lambert Law to a scattering medium.
Using Planck’s Law for non-blackbody sources.
Ignoring the requirement for thermal equilibrium in blackbody radiation calculations.

rules.title: Verify Energy Conservation in Calorimetry
rules.description: The principle of conservation of energy applies in calorimetry experiments, where heat lost by one system equals heat gained by another, assuming no heat is lost to the surroundings. This is expressed as Q_lost = Q_gained.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the sum of heat lost by hotter bodies equals the sum of heat gained by colder bodies: ΣQ_lost = ΣQ_gained. Verify that no heat is unaccounted for in the system.
common_errors: Forgetting to include all systems exchanging heat.
Ignoring heat losses to the environment.
Using incorrect signs for heat lost or gained.

rules.title: Ensure Correct Use of Specific Heat Formula
rules.description: The formula Q = mcΔT relates heat transfer (Q) to mass (m), specific heat capacity (c), and change in temperature (ΔT). This is valid for a single phase of the material.
rules.check_logic: Verify that mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature change are correctly substituted into Q = mcΔT. Ensure that the material remains in a single phase during the calculation.
common_errors: Using incorrect units for specific heat capacity, often confusing J/kg·K with J/g·K.
Neglecting to convert ΔT into the correct unit (Celsius or Kelvin).
Using incorrect signs for ΔT (positive for heating, negative for cooling).

rules.title: Verify Heat Transfer During Phase Changes
rules.description: During phase changes (e.g., melting, boiling), heat transfer is calculated using Q = mL, where L is the latent heat. Temperature remains constant during the phase change.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that Q = mL is used only during phase changes, and that the temperature is held constant during the phase transition. Verify that the correct latent heat value (L) is used for the material and phase transition.
common_errors: Using Q = mcΔT instead of Q = mL during phase changes.
Including a temperature change during the phase change.
Forgetting to use the correct value of latent heat (L) for the material and phase transition.

rules.title: Check Correct Sign Convention for Heat Transfer
rules.description: Heat absorbed by a system is positive (Q > 0), while heat lost by a system is negative (Q < 0). This sign convention must be consistently applied.
rules.check_logic: Verify that heat absorbed is marked positive and heat released is marked negative in all calculations. Ensure consistency in sign convention across all systems in the problem.
common_errors: Reversing the sign convention for heat transfer.
Inconsistent sign usage across different systems in a problem.

rules.title: Verify Thermal Equilibrium Conditions
rules.description: Thermal equilibrium is reached when all interacting systems have the same final temperature, assuming no heat is lost to the surroundings.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the final temperature of all systems in thermal contact is the same. Verify that heat losses to the environment are negligible or accounted for.
common_errors: Assigning different final temperatures to systems in equilibrium.
Ignoring heat losses to the environment, leading to incorrect equilibrium conditions.

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in Heat Calculations
rules.description: All quantities in heat transfer equations must have consistent units. For instance, specific heat capacity should be in J/kg·K, and mass in kilograms.
rules.check_logic: Verify that units for heat, mass, specific heat capacity, temperature, and latent heat are consistent in all calculations. Ensure proper unit conversions where necessary.
common_errors: Mixing units such as using grams for mass while specific heat is in J/kg·K.
Failing to convert temperature changes to Kelvin when required.

rules.title: Check Validity Conditions for Heat Transfer Equations
rules.description: Heat transfer equations like Q = mcΔT and Q = mL are valid only under specific conditions: constant specific heat capacity for Q = mcΔT, and phase change without temperature change for Q = mL.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that specific heat capacity is treated as constant over the temperature range for Q = mcΔT. Verify that Q = mL is used only for phase changes, and only at the phase transition temperature.
common_errors: Using Q = mcΔT over a temperature range where c is not constant.
Applying phase change equations outside the phase transition temperature.

rules.title: Account for Heat Loss to the Environment
rules.description: In real experiments, some heat is lost to the environment. This loss must be accounted for to improve accuracy, especially in calorimetry.
rules.check_logic: Verify that heat loss to the environment is either included in the calculations or explicitly stated as negligible. Ensure that corrections for heat loss are applied where necessary.
common_errors: Ignoring heat losses without justification.
Failing to include corrections for heat loss in experimental results.

rules.title: Verify Initial Conditions for Heat Transfer
rules.description: Initial conditions, such as initial temperatures, masses, and material properties, must be accurately measured and used in calculations.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that all initial conditions are correctly recorded and used in calculations. Verify that assumptions about initial states are valid.
common_errors: Using incorrect or imprecise initial temperature values.
Neglecting to account for initial thermal energy of the system.

rules.title: Verify System Isolation in Calorimetry
rules.description: Calorimetry assumes that the system is thermally isolated, meaning no heat is exchanged with the surroundings.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the system is thermally isolated, or account for any heat exchange with the surroundings. Verify that the assumption of isolation is valid for the experiment.
common_errors: Assuming perfect isolation when the system is not well-insulated.
Failing to account for heat exchange with the environment in non-isolated systems.

rules.title: Verify Ideal Gas Law for Vacuum Systems
rules.description: The Ideal Gas Law, PV = nRT, relates pressure, volume, temperature, and the number of moles of gas. It applies under conditions where intermolecular forces are negligible, typically at low pressures and high temperatures.
rules.check_logic: Confirm PV = nRT is used for pressure calculations. Ensure temperature is in Kelvin, and pressure, volume, and the gas constant R are in consistent units.
common_errors: Using Celsius instead of Kelvin for temperature
Incorrect unit conversions for pressure or volume
Using the wrong value of the gas constant R (e.g., mismatched units)

rules.title: Ensure Correct Sign Convention for Gauge and Absolute Pressure
rules.description: Gauge pressure measures pressure relative to atmospheric pressure, while absolute pressure is measured relative to a vacuum. The relation is P_absolute = P_gauge + P_atmosphere.
rules.check_logic: Verify that absolute pressure is calculated by adding atmospheric pressure to gauge pressure. Confirm consistent sign conventions in equations.
common_errors: Confusing gauge pressure with absolute pressure
Forgetting to add atmospheric pressure to gauge pressure
Using negative signs incorrectly when calculating pressures

rules.title: Check Pumping Speed and Vacuum System Constraints
rules.description: Pumping speed (S) relates to the flow rate of gas being removed (Q) and the pressure (P) via the equation Q = S × P. This relationship applies in the molecular flow regime.
rules.check_logic: Ensure Q = S × P is applied only in the molecular flow regime, and confirm the pumping speed is constant for the given system and conditions.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming pumping speed is constant in all regimes
Failing to match units of Q, S, and P
Applying the equation in the viscous flow regime

rules.title: Ensure Dimensional Consistency in Pressure-Related Equations
rules.description: Pressure is typically measured in units such as Pascal (Pa), Torr, or atm. Ensure all equations involving pressure, volume, and temperature use consistent units.
rules.check_logic: Verify pressure units, volume units, and temperature units are consistent with the gas constant R or the applied equations.
common_errors: Mixing units like atm and Pascal without proper conversion
Forgetting to convert temperature to Kelvin
Using mismatched units for volume and pressure

rules.title: Verify Validity of Flow Regime Assumptions
rules.description: Different flow regimes (viscous, transitional, molecular) require different calculations. The Knudsen number (Kn = λ / L) indicates the regime: Kn < 0.01 (viscous), 0.01 < Kn < 10 (transitional), Kn > 10 (molecular).
rules.check_logic: Ensure the flow regime is identified using the Knudsen number, and confirm accuracy when applying corresponding equations for the regime.
common_errors: Using molecular flow equations in the viscous regime
Failing to calculate the Knudsen number when determining the flow regime
Assuming a constant mean free path (λ) without considering pressure changes

rules.title: Check for Leak Rate and System Integrity
rules.description: A vacuum system must be sealed to maintain low pressures. The leak rate is calculated as Q_leak = ΔP × V / Δt.
rules.check_logic: Verify use of the leak rate equation, ensuring ΔP, V, and Δt are measured or calculated with consistent units.
common_errors: Ignoring potential leak paths
Using inconsistent units for ΔP, V, or Δt
Assuming a negligible leak rate without calculation

rules.title: Verify Partial Pressure Calculations for Gas Mixtures
rules.description: The total pressure in a vacuum system with a gas mixture is the sum of the partial pressures of all gases. Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures applies.
rules.check_logic: Ensure the total pressure is calculated as the sum of partial pressures and that mole fractions are used correctly for each gas.
common_errors: Failing to sum partial pressures correctly
Incorrectly calculating mole fractions
Ignoring contributions from trace gases in the mixture

rules.title: Account for Adsorption and Outgassing Effects
rules.description: Outgassing and adsorption affect vacuum pressure over time. Outgassing rates depend on material properties and system conditions.
rules.check_logic: Verify calculations account for outgassing rates and adsorption effects, ensuring inclusion in pressure stabilization analyses.
common_errors: Ignoring outgassing contributions to pressure
Failing to account for adsorption at low temperatures
Assuming instantaneous stabilization of vacuum pressure

rules.title: Ensure entropy decreases with temperature in ideal systems
rules.description: For cryogenics, entropy in a system decreases as the temperature is reduced, following the Third Law of Thermodynamics. This holds unless external entropy sources (e.g., heat influx or system imperfections) are present.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the entropy S approaches zero as the temperature T approaches absolute zero, provided no residual entropy is present. Ensure that any deviations are justified by material-specific properties or external factors.
common_errors: Incorrectly assuming entropy is zero at non-zero temperatures.
Ignoring residual entropy due to material imperfections or quantum effects.

rules.title: Verify thermal conductivity decreases with lower temperatures
rules.description: In cryogenic systems, thermal conductivity of most materials decreases as temperature drops, except for superconductors or specific materials showing anomalous behavior.
rules.check_logic: Check if the thermal conductivity κ decreases with temperature for conventional materials. Ensure exceptions for superconductors and materials with known anomalous behavior are handled correctly.
common_errors: Failing to account for material-specific thermal conductivity behavior.
Applying high-temperature thermal conductivity models to cryogenic ranges.

rules.title: Check dimensionless group consistency in cryogenic equations
rules.description: Many cryogenic equations involve dimensionless quantities, such as Reynolds number, Knudsen number, or Biot number. Ensure consistency in their definitions and application.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the variables in dimensionless groups are correctly substituted and have no dimensional inconsistencies. Ensure that the physical meaning of the dimensionless group is preserved in the context of cryogenic systems.
common_errors: Using incorrect definitions for dimensionless groups.
Mixing incompatible unit systems when calculating dimensionless numbers.

rules.title: Ensure correct handling of liquid-gas transitions at low temperatures
rules.description: During liquid-gas transitions in cryogenic systems, the Clausius-Clapeyron equation governs the relationship between pressure and temperature.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the Clausius-Clapeyron equation is applied correctly for phase transitions, and the latent heat is treated as temperature-dependent. Ensure that vapor pressure changes are accurately modeled at cryogenic temperatures.
common_errors: Assuming latent heat is constant across the temperature range.
Ignoring changes in vapor pressure at cryogenic temperatures.

rules.title: Verify correct sign convention for heat flow
rules.description: In cryogenics, heat flow direction is critical. Heat flow into the system is positive, while heat flow out is negative.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that heat flow terms in equations are consistent with the sign convention. Verify that the direction of heat flow is correctly interpreted in thermal balance equations.
common_errors: Reversing the sign of heat flow when calculating cooling power.
Misinterpreting heat flow direction in thermal balance equations.

rules.title: Check criteria for superfluid transition in helium-4
rules.description: Helium-4 undergoes a superfluid transition at the lambda point (~2.17 K). Verify that equations and models account for the unique properties of superfluid helium below this temperature.
rules.check_logic: Ensure that the temperature is below 2.17 K and superfluid-specific properties (e.g., zero viscosity, quantized vortices, second sound) are considered. Verify that normal fluid dynamics are not applied to superfluid helium.
common_errors: Applying normal fluid dynamics to superfluid helium.
Ignoring the unique heat transport properties of superfluid helium (e.g., second sound).

rules.title: Verify conditions for adiabatic demagnetization cooling
rules.description: Adiabatic demagnetization is used for cooling in cryogenics. The process relies on isolating the system thermally and applying/removing magnetic fields.
rules.check_logic: Check that the system is thermally insulated and the magnetic field variation is slow enough to maintain quasi-equilibrium. Verify that the entropy change corresponds to the expected cooling effect.
common_errors: Ignoring thermal insulation requirements.
Assuming instantaneous magnetic field changes, violating adiabatic conditions.

rules.title: Ensure unit consistency in cryogenic parameters
rules.description: Cryogenic systems often involve parameters like temperature (K), pressure (Pa), and energy (J). Ensure all units are consistent to avoid calculation errors.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all equations use consistent units (SI units are preferred unless specified otherwise). Ensure that unit conversions are correctly applied where necessary.
common_errors: Using temperature in Celsius instead of Kelvin.
Mixing units (e.g., bar for pressure and SI energy units).

rules.title: Verify material property data at cryogenic temperatures
rules.description: Material properties such as specific heat, thermal expansion, and electrical resistivity can vary significantly at cryogenic temperatures. Ensure accurate data is used.
rules.check_logic: Verify that material property data is sourced from reliable cryogenic-specific references. Ensure that temperature-dependent variations are accounted for in calculations.
common_errors: Using room-temperature material properties for cryogenic calculations.
Ignoring temperature-dependent variations in material properties.

rules.title: Ensure proper vacuum insulation in cryogenic systems
rules.description: Vacuum insulation is critical to minimize heat transfer in cryogenic systems. Verify that the vacuum level and insulation design meet the required specifications.
rules.check_logic: Check that the vacuum pressure is sufficiently low to minimize conduction and convection. Verify that insulation materials and designs are appropriate for cryogenic applications.
common_errors: Using inadequate vacuum levels, leading to excessive heat transfer.
Failing to account for material outgassing or thermal bridging in insulation design.

rules.title: Verify consistency with equations of motion
rules.description: Ensure that the measured displacement, velocity, and acceleration in high-speed motion analysis obey the equations of motion under constant acceleration. These include: v = u + at, s = ut + 0.5at^2, and v^2 = u^2 + 2as.
rules.check_logic: Verify if the provided displacement, velocity, and acceleration data satisfy all applicable equations of motion under the assumption of constant acceleration. Ensure that time intervals are correctly accounted for.
common_errors: Incorrect substitution of values in equations
Assuming constant acceleration when it is not valid
Ignoring time intervals during high-speed imaging analysis

rules.title: Check adherence to sign conventions
rules.description: Ensure that the chosen coordinate system and sign conventions (e.g., positive for motion in the rightward or upward direction) are consistently applied throughout the analysis.
rules.check_logic: Verify that all vector quantities (e.g., displacement, velocity, acceleration) have been assigned signs consistently with the chosen coordinate system. Check for consistency across all time intervals and reference frames.
common_errors: Inconsistent use of positive and negative signs for direction
Mixing up coordinate axes for 2D or 3D motion analysis
Forgetting to invert signs when switching reference frames

rules.title: Verify frame rate sufficiency
rules.description: The frame rate of the imaging system must be high enough to capture motion without significant temporal aliasing (i.e., the Nyquist criterion for temporal sampling must be met).
rules.check_logic: Ensure the frame rate is at least twice the highest frequency component of the motion being analyzed. Validate that the frame rate is sufficient to avoid motion blur and aliasing.
common_errors: Using a frame rate that is too low to capture high-speed motion
Ignoring motion blur caused by insufficient temporal resolution

rules.title: Verify geometric constraints in motion paths
rules.description: In high-speed imaging, the motion path must conform to expected geometric constraints (e.g., circular paths for rotating objects, straight-line paths for linear motion).
rules.check_logic: Compare the trajectory derived from the imaging data with the expected geometric constraints (e.g., radius of curvature for circular motion). Account for potential distortions caused by camera misalignment or lens distortion.
common_errors: Assuming perfect straight-line motion when there is curvature
Ignoring deviations from expected geometry due to camera misalignment or distortion
Forgetting to account for 3D motion in projected 2D data

rules.title: Check dimensional and unit consistency
rules.description: Ensure all quantities in the analysis have consistent dimensions and units, particularly for derived quantities like velocity (m/s) and acceleration (m/s^2).
rules.check_logic: Verify that all equations and intermediate steps maintain dimensional consistency and that units are correctly converted where necessary. Ensure that derived quantities are expressed in the correct units.
common_errors: Mixing unit systems (e.g., using cm for displacement and m/s for velocity)
Forgetting to square or cube units in derived quantities
Incorrect conversion between FPS and SI units

rules.title: Verify projection and perspective effects
rules.description: Ensure that the imaging system's perspective (e.g., camera angle, distance) does not distort the measurement of motion parameters, particularly in 3D to 2D projections.
rules.check_logic: Verify if corrections for perspective and projection distortions have been applied to the motion data when required. Check for foreshortening, parallax, and other projection-related distortions.
common_errors: Ignoring foreshortening effects in projected motion
Neglecting the parallax effect in multi-camera setups
Assuming a flat plane for 3D motion without projection corrections

rules.title: Verify appropriate lighting conditions
rules.description: Ensure the lighting conditions during high-speed imaging are sufficient to avoid motion blur and ensure clear object definition in each frame.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the exposure time is short enough relative to the object's speed to avoid motion blur, and that the object is adequately illuminated. Check for uniform lighting across the field of view.
common_errors: Using long exposure times leading to motion blur
Insufficient lighting causing poor object visibility
Ignoring the effect of variable lighting on image clarity

rules.title: Check validity of high-speed imaging assumptions
rules.description: Ensure that the assumptions of high-speed imaging are met, such as negligible air resistance in vacuum-like conditions or the absence of significant external forces.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the environmental and experimental setup meets the assumptions required for the analysis (e.g., no abrupt changes in environmental conditions). Check for external forces or environmental factors that could invalidate the assumptions.
common_errors: Ignoring air resistance in high-speed motion
Assuming constant acceleration when external forces are present
Neglecting temperature effects on high-speed imaging accuracy

rules.title: Verify calibration of imaging system
rules.description: Ensure that the imaging system (e.g., cameras, lenses) is properly calibrated to avoid errors in motion analysis.
rules.check_logic: Verify that the imaging system has been calibrated for lens distortion, alignment, and scaling factors. Check that calibration data is up-to-date and consistent with the experimental setup.
common_errors: Using uncalibrated cameras leading to scaling errors
Ignoring lens distortion in high-speed imaging
Using outdated calibration data for the experimental setup

rules.title: Check for noise and data artifacts
rules.description: Ensure that the motion data is free from significant noise or artifacts that could affect the analysis.
rules.check_logic: Verify that noise reduction techniques (e.g., filtering) have been applied to the data. Check for artifacts caused by sensor errors or environmental interference.
common_errors: Ignoring noise in high-speed motion data
Failing to apply appropriate filters to reduce artifacts
Misinterpreting sensor errors as valid motion data
